253: [P253] End of specification. This document is the single build reference for the Audio Intelligence Plane; the working drafts it consolidates are retired.

# SOURCE: assessment_workspace/canon/drops/20260914_audio_plane_v1/raw/Akki_OS_Audio_Intelligence_Plane_Specification_v1_0.docx
Coordinate: document.xml paragraph in body order, tables included

1: SYNI.AI   ·   ENGINEERING SPECIFICATION
2: The Audio Intelligence Plane
3: Extraction · Learning · Training · Invention — end to end
4: Including the Commission View surface adjustment across all extraction types · v1.0
5: Status of this document: consolidated build specification. It supersedes the working drafts (Audio Capability Spec v1.0 and Addendum v1.1.2) and is the single reference for build. Behavioural clauses state what the system must and must not do, including on failure. Technical clauses state contracts and acceptance criteria. Items requiring verification against current code before build are marked [VERIFY] and collected in §16.
6: Contents
7: 
8: 
9: 
10: 1  Governing Doctrine
11: Five principles govern every clause in this specification. Where a later clause appears to conflict with one of these, the principle wins and the clause is defective.
12: 1.1  An audio file is a data estate, and the framing is recursive
13: The archive is an estate; a programme is an estate; a single file is an estate. Segments are rows; the extractable layers — content, language, condition, prosody, occurrence, code-switch, music, group-level character — are columns; no schema exists until one is declared. Census, admission, registry, and record apply at every scale.
14: 1.2  Modality extension, not parallel machinery
15: The audio plane introduces no sibling services. Mtafiti gains an audio modality; Northena gains audio data classes; the wizard gains an objective variant; Targeta gains a training object. Anything in this document that reads as a parallel to an existing service is rule proliferation and must be collapsed into the existing service before build.
16: 1.3  One record
17: Mtafiti and Northena collaborate to produce a single record, written once. Working state — loss curves, intermediate metrics, partial coverage counts — is scratch, not truth; it becomes record only when finalized and stamped. No local ledger exists. If a measured throughput ceiling ever demands relief, the relief is batched stamping (one row certifying N events with a digest), which remains a single record. That change is made only when a measurement demands it.
18: 1.4  Measure, do not assert
19: No data-volume requirement, accuracy expectation, or cost figure is quoted without a measurement behind it. The calibration stage exists to convert assertions into measurements before commitment.
20: 1.5  Unrepresentable, not policed
21: Safety boundaries are enforced by making the violating state impossible to express in the contract — the pattern established by the assertion floor — not by review after the fact. The Character Register write path (§6) and the voice identity distance gate (§7) both follow this pattern.
22: 2  Capability Statement and Plane Overview
23: Given governed access to an audio estate, the plane provides four functions in one loop:
24: Extraction — audio is converted into provenance-paired facts: transcripts, entities, occurrences, and character observations.
25: Learning — a Character Register accumulates group-level knowledge of how the estate’s languages and audio behave.
26: Training — model production is commissioned against a falsifiable Target Outcome, planned and priced before compute is spent, with per-example provenance.
27: Invention — synthesized voice identities are constructed from the register: authentically of the language, provably of no individual.
28: 
29: Each function feeds the next: extraction populates the register; the register defines the strata training plans against; trained models improve extraction; invention consumes the register’s learned layers. The loop is the capability.
30: Flow of a commission, end to end:
31: Objective Wizard session → compile {TargetOutcome, Collection Schema}
32: → Sampling & Reflection (calibration) → proposed Milestones + priced quote
33: → Owner agrees milestones → Commission opens
34: → Collection → Register update → Curriculum → Training runs → Certificates
35: → Commission View reports against milestones throughout → Commission sealed
36: 3  Tokenized Audio Representation
37: 3.1  Behaviour
38: All downstream audio work — extraction, character analysis, training — operates on discrete token sequences produced by a neural audio codec, not on waveforms.
39: Tokenization exposes two separable streams per segment: the content stream (what was said — input to ASR/NER) and the character stream (how it was said — input to the Character Register). The character stream is retained and routed, never discarded as noise.
40: Control markers (language, register, segment type) are splice-able tokens, enabling one model per estate rather than one per language, and native handling of code-switched speech.
41: Failure behaviour: audio in an unsupported condition fails closed with a stated reason. The codec never silently degrades quality.
42: 3.2  Technical contract
43: Item
44: Specification
45: Service
46: perception/audio_codec/ — registered like any other perception model; census-visible; runs in-perimeter on tenant compute.
47: Input
48: Audio segment (bounds per ingestion segmentation) + declared or detected condition profile.
49: Output
50: { content_tokens[], character_stream, codec_version }
51: Target token rate 50–100 tokens/second of audio.
52: Provenance
53: codec_version is a mandatory field of every downstream artifact’s provenance. A transcript states which codec produced its tokens.
54: Pretraining
55: The codec pretrains unsupervised on unlabelled estate audio, under the standard commissioned-job contract.
56: [VERIFY]
57: Perception router contract: where model registration occurs, and whether the router carries a second output stream per segment or the character stream requires its own artifact type.
58: 
59: 3.3  Acceptance criteria
60: Round-trip fidelity is measured and recorded per codec version before that version serves any commission.
61: A downstream artifact lacking codec_version in provenance is rejected at the registry boundary.
62: An unsupported-condition input produces a refusal with a stated reason and no output artifact.
63: 4  Extraction Layer
64: 4.1  Language identification
65: Behaviour: every segment carries a real language signal. The current plumbing value (language_hint: None) is retired.
66: A lightweight offline language identifier (CPU-viable, in-perimeter) runs at segment level during ingestion.
67: Recorded per segment: languages[], confidences, and code-switch points where multiple languages occur in one utterance.
68: The signal routes downstream model selection (ASR path, NER path, de-identification path) and is written into provenance.
69: [VERIFY] Segment boundaries in current ingestion — confirm the unit to which a language label attaches.
70: 4.2  Code-switch points as facts
71: Switch points (position, from-language, to-language, context class) are registered facts with provenance — not preprocessing metadata. They populate the register’s code-switch layer and stratify test sets.
72: 4.3  Condition profiling
73: Channel condition — studio / field / telephone band, transmission artefacts, background class — is derived per segment at first ingestion. It is cheap to compute, directly predictive of extraction error, and required for training stratification. It is captured at first ingestion because re-ingesting an estate to recover it is the unaffordable mistake.
74: 4.4  Synthesis-relevant attribute capture
75: During the same ingestion pass, group-level acoustic attributes required by any future synthesis capability (pitch statistics, energy contours, duration patterns) are captured, subject to the custody conditions of §6.4. This forecloses nothing and costs little; omitting it forecloses the invention function or forces re-ingestion.
76: 4.5  Deduplication as augmentation
77: The occurrence index already identifies repeated content. Its output contract is extended: for each deduplicated item, the instance condition map — the set of channel/time/condition variants under which identical content occurred — is retained. One canonical extraction is stored; the variant set enters training curricula as a designated robustness stratum at zero acquisition cost. No new detection work; this is a change to what dedup keeps.
78: 4.6  Acceptance criteria
79: No segment leaves ingestion without languages[], condition profile, and (where applicable) switch points in provenance.
80: A deduplicated item without its instance condition map fails the ingestion invariant test.
81: Baseline-tier capture (§9.2) runs for all admitted material regardless of any active objective.
82: 5  The Character Register — Learning
83: 5.1  Definition
84: A registry-modality store of learned, group-level audio characteristics, built from the character stream. Same doctrine as the fact registry: every entry carries provenance to source material and an occurrence count. It is Mtafiti’s qualification-and-index doctrine applied to acoustic observations — an extension, not a sibling (§1.2).
85: 5.2  Layers
86: Layer
87: Contents
88: Primary consumers
89: Phonetic
90: Per-lexeme pronunciation variants, frequency, regional distribution.
91: Curriculum; extraction lexicons; evaluation stratification
92: Prosodic
93: Intonation contours, stress, rate distributions, pause structure.
94: Training; programme-type classification
95: Condition
96: Channel and environment profiles.
97: Stratification; error prediction
98: Code-switch
99: Switch-point patterns, language pairs, context classes.
100: Training; test-set design
101: 
102: 5.3  Build process
103: Unsupervised clustering over the character stream yields candidate strata. A cluster asserts that a distinct variant exists — not what it is called. Naming and validation are human work applied to a sample, commissioned like any other qualified work with quoted cost.
104: 6  Register Custody Boundary
105: 6.1  Governing distinction: organic versus learned
106: Organic characteristics are anatomical — vocal tract length, formant structure, glottal source, fundamental frequency range. They cannot be acquired or shed; they are what speaker verification keys on; they are biometric. They are never registered.
107: Learned characteristics are acquired from a speech community — phonological inventory, pronunciation variants, prosody, code-switching habits. They are group properties by construction. Only learned characteristics may be registered.
108: 6.2  The four conditions — all must hold
109: Acquired, not anatomical. The attribute is learnable by a speaker from a different background.
110: Shared. Observed across at least N distinct speakers. N is a governed seam value; its default inherits the platform minimum-group-size parameter unless the tenant sets a register-specific value.
111: Non-reconstructive in combination. Tested against attribute combinations, not attributes in isolation: language + region + age band + one distinctive feature can reach a single person even when each attribute is group-level.
112: Stored as description, not exemplar. Centroids, distributions, frequencies. Never stored audio; never per-utterance speaker embeddings. Embeddings used during clustering are destroyed after cluster assignment. Provenance points to material, not to speaker identity.
113: 6.3  Enforcement shape
114: The register write path exposes no field through which an instance-level representation can be stored: the schema cannot represent a voiceprint. Unrepresentable, not policed (§1.5). An automated invariant test attempts each known leakage path (small stratum, idiolect marker, narrowing combination, exemplar storage) and must fail to store all of them on every change to the register code.
115: 6.4  Idiolect rule
116: Habitual fillers, characteristic phrasings, and idiosyncratically pronounced words are learned but individuating. They fail condition 2 or 3 and are excluded. “Learned” alone is never sufficient; the four conditions are conjunctive.
117: 7  Synthesized Voice Identity — Invention
118: 7.1  Mechanism: inherit the learned, synthesize the organic
119: Learned characteristics are inherited from the register — this is what makes the voice sound like a speaker of the language rather than a foreigner reading it.
120: Organic characteristics are constructed — vocal tract parameters, F0 range, formant structure, glottal parameters are chosen as a point in acoustic space that no real speaker occupies.
121: This is the inverse of a voice clone. A clone copies the organic and frequently gets the learned wrong; this gets the learned right and owns the organic outright.
122: 7.2  The distance guarantee (mandatory, fail-closed)
123: Every constructed identity is scored against every speaker representation derivable from the corpus using standard speaker-verification methods. A minimum distance from all of them is required. Below threshold, the identity is rejected and resampled. There is no override. The threshold value and the verification method are recorded with the identity.
124: 7.3  The certificate
125: A passing identity is issued a certificate stating that the voice is provably derived from no individual, naming the method, the threshold, and the corpus version scored against. The certificate is a first-class sellable artifact.
126: 7.4  Identity composition and versioning
127: Component
128: Source
129: Acoustic identity
130: Constructed organic parameters (§7.1).
131: Speech character
132: Inherited from register — phonetic and prosodic layers.
133: Interaction character
134: Turn-taking, formality, code-switch behaviour — inherited from register.
135: 
136: Each identity is a versioned artifact with a ledger entry. Changing one is a ceremony with the standard waiting period, because audience recognition accrues to the voice and recognition is the asset. Identities never drift.
137: 7.5  Scope note
138: Rendering requires a synthesis stack, which is a separate build from recognition. What this specification requires now is non-foreclosure: the identity specification (attribute schema, distance method, certificate format) is defined, and §4.4’s ingestion capture ensures the substrate exists when rendering is built.
139: 8  The Objective Wizard — Schema Compiler
140: 8.1  Role
141: No business user hand-writes a Target Outcome. The Objective Wizard — a new variant of the existing shaping wizard, reusing its agent interface, guards, session persistence, and ledger sidecar — elicits an objective in plain language and compiles two governed artifacts:
142: TargetOutcome (§10) — handed to the Training Planner.
143: Collection Schema (§9) — the data dictionary for this objective: which data points are extracted from the sound, at what granularity, at what quality bar.
144: 8.2  Elicitation sequence
145: The question the model must answer — operational and falsifiable.
146: The population — resolved against existing register strata; unresolved populations are flagged as unmeasured and generate census work.
147: The acceptance bar — per stratum, two-dimensional (§10), with the gate-or-document decision recorded explicitly.
148: The collection consequences — the wizard derives required columns, shows which are already collected (baseline tier), which exist but are uncollected, and the cost of collecting them. The owner sees the price of the schema before commissioning.
149: 8.3  Dynamism within scope: propose, qualify, graduate
150: Propose. The agent side may propose novel data points no prior objective collected. This is where innovation enters.
151: Qualify. A proposed column never enters collection directly. It is admitted as a candidate: collected on a sample only, its evidence of value measured against the objective — the same qualification path any fact travels.
152: Graduate. Qualified candidates graduate into the objective tier for that commission. Graduation into the baseline tier is ceremony-governed (proposal, countersignature, waiting period), because a baseline column is paid on every hour ingested for the life of the estate.
153: The compile stage is deterministic throughout: the agent proposes; only qualified columns compile. Mechanical guards prove against a stub agent before any LLM is plugged in, per the existing standing disposition.
154: 8.4  Compile-time rejections
155: The wizard cannot emit an artifact the downstream contracts would refuse. Rejected at compile, not warned:
156: An Outcome without an existing test_set_ref.
157: An acceptance bar missing the per-stratum dimension.
158: A Collection Schema requiring a column whose capture violates the custody conditions of §6.2.
159: 8.5  Record and handoff
160: Every session stamps to the ledger via the existing turn-ledger pattern under a distinct data class (objective_session), including options considered and rejected — which is what makes a later “why was the model built this way” answerable. Compiled artifacts hand off to Targeta through the existing admission-handoff pattern. Objective → schema → plan → run is one provenance chain.
161: [VERIFY] The B-2/B-3 landing state of the current wizard, before choosing between extending the existing state machine with an objective variant or standing up a sibling machine sharing the agent interface and ledger sidecar.
162: 9  The Collection Schema
163: 9.1  Definition
164: The declared data dictionary of a commission: what is extracted from the sound, for what purpose, at what quality bar. It is the admission standard of the audio estate, per objective (§1.1). It has two tiers.
165: 9.2  Baseline tier
166: Standing, objective-independent, collected at first ingestion for all admitted material. Membership criterion: cheap to collect now, unaffordable to collect later. Contents at v1.0: language identification, code-switch points, condition profile, dedup instance condition map, synthesis-relevant group-level acoustics (§4). Changes to the baseline are seam-governed — ceremony, countersignature, waiting period — because silently narrowing the baseline is how an estate quietly becomes unre-readable.
167: 9.3  Objective tier
168: Declared per commission by the Objective Wizard. Collected against material already in governed scope, priced before collection starts, recorded in the commission’s registry namespace. Candidate columns enter through propose–qualify–graduate (§8.3) only.
169: 10  The Target Outcome
170: 10.1  Schema
171: TargetOutcome {
172:   task          operational statement of what the model must do
173:   domain        context of use
174:   population    defined by reference to register strata, not labels
175:   acceptance    threshold per stratum; two-dimensional (accuracy, coverage)
176:   gate_policy   per Outcome: missed stratum gates release | ships documented
177:   test_set_ref  must exist before the Outcome is accepted
178:   constraints   latency, compute budget, deployment target
179: }
180: 
181: 10.2  Binding rules
182: Population is register-defined. “Language L, accent clusters 1–4, telephone band and studio, adult” — never “speakers of L.” This is what makes coverage computable.
183: Acceptance is per stratum. A single global threshold hides the failure that matters: 94% on the majority variant and 61% on the rest passes one test and fails the one that decides whether the work reaches the people it was built for.
184: The test set precedes the training. An Outcome without an existing, stratified test set is rejected at definition time.
185: The gate decision is recorded on the Outcome at definition — not decided ad hoc at ship time.
186: 11  The Training Planner
187: 11.1  Architecture
188: The existing planner pattern is reused unchanged: a deterministic core computes eligibility; a learned layer may only reorder an already-eligible set it receives stripped of the values that decided eligibility; a gate compares learned output against the deterministic baseline; every plan is reproducible from its recorded inputs.
189: 
190: Extraction planning (existing)
191: Training planning (new)
192: Object
193: Source locations
194: Register strata
195: Floor
196: Defensibility class
197: Acceptance threshold — accuracy × coverage
198: Output
199: Mining plan
200: Training plan + curriculum + milestones
201: 
202: 11.2  Sampling & Reflection (calibration) — mandatory first stage
203: Data requirements for low-resource fine-tuning are empirical; no analytical answer exists. The first commissioned stage is therefore a calibration: train at three to four data volumes, evaluate per stratum against the test set, fit the scaling curve, extrapolate to the acceptance threshold. Only then is the full run quoted, with a stated confidence interval — never a point estimate. A plan without a calibration stage is rejected. The first job prices the real job.
204: 11.3  Milestones — the accountability output
205: Sampling & Reflection has two customers. It prices the real job, and it authors the accountability structure: its output to the objective owner is not a curve but a proposed milestone list — the checklist of what must be done, in what order, for the commission to succeed. Each milestone carries a done-condition and an owner. The objective owner reviews and agrees the list at commission; from that point, all reporting is against it. Accountability is set before spend, not discovered during.
206: 11.4  Planner outputs
207: Coverage report — per target stratum: hours available, quality distribution, gaps, cost of closing each gap.
208: Curriculum — ordering and weighting across strata derived from the register, not from the corpus’s natural distribution, which is always skewed toward whatever occurred most. The dedup instance condition map enters as a designated robustness stratum.
209: Proposed milestone list (§11.3).
210: Cost quote with a stated confidence interval.
211: 11.5  Provenance through training
212: Every training example carries its provenance into the training manifest. Consequences: rights are enforceable per example; an example whose rights lapse is identifiable and the affected models enumerable; and “the trained model is the customer’s property” is a statement backed by a manifest, not an assertion.
213: 11.6  Run governance
214: Training runs are commissioned jobs under the existing contract: quoted before start, metered during, certificated on completion. The completion certificate records compute consumed, data touched, manifest hash, and per-stratum results against the Outcome. Failed strata are reported as plainly as passed ones.
215: 12  Record and Registry Integration
216: 12.1  Registry (Mtafiti audio modality)
217: Per commission, a scoped namespace within the registry holds: the Collection Schema (versioned), collected data points mapped against it — with declared-but-not-yet-collected as first-class state — the strata referenced by the Outcome, and coverage state per stratum. Reads compose with the global registry; writes are namespace-scoped. On close, the namespace is sealed, not deleted: it is the record of what was collected and why, and the next objective’s wizard session queries prior schemas and coverage so the second project starts from the first project’s map.
218: 12.2  Record (Northena data classes)
219: Training-workflow operations stamp into the one ledger under training-specific data classes: collection events, calibration runs, curriculum decisions, milestone status changes, run certificates. The workflow’s view of “its” record is a scoped lens filterable by commission ID — a view, not a store. Working state (loss curves, intermediate metrics, partial counts) is scratch until finalized and stamped once (§1.3).
220: 13  Surface Specification — the Commission View
221: 13.1  Scope
222: This surface adjustment applies to all commissioned work on the platform — extraction, census, and training commissions alike, across every extraction type. No modality receives its own UI, and no surface is a rendering of backend internals: rendering internals quietly commits the backend to building displayable versions of its own machinery.
223: 13.2  Behaviour
224: The surface is milestones. The artifacts are evidence behind them.
225: At Sampling & Reflection, the proposed milestone list is presented to the objective owner for agreement. Commission does not open until it is agreed.
226: The Commission View reports against the agreed checklist: each milestone with its done-condition and owner; status in plain terms — done, on track, behind, missed. Missed is shown as plainly as done.
227: Spend against quote is shown at the same plain level.
228: Technical material — calibration results, strata coverage, Collection Schema state — is drill-down evidence for whoever asks why a milestone reads as it does. It is never the front page.
229: 13.3  Modality leaf
230: Modality appears at exactly one leaf: evidence inspection. Where provenance resolves to a recording, the source plays at its timestamp rather than rendering as a page region — the existing trust-receipt pattern (“a disputed number is answered by playing the tape”), unchanged.
231: 13.4  Backend cost constraint
232: Milestones are records with done-conditions; the platform already stamps events. No new machinery is built for display. Any surface element in this section found to require new backend computation beyond reading existing artifacts is out of specification and must be removed or re-specified.
233: 14  Interface Summary
234: Surface
235: Contract
236: audio_codec
237: audio in → { content_tokens, character_stream, codec_version }; fail-closed on unsupported condition.
238: Language ID
239: segment → { languages[], confidences, switch_points }; written to provenance.
240: Occurrence index (ext.)
241: dedup item → + instance condition map.
242: Character Register
243: Write path: schema cannot represent instance-level identity (§6.3). Read path: strata queries for planner and evaluation.
244: Objective Wizard
245: session → { TargetOutcome, CollectionSchema }; deterministic compile; compile-time rejection of contract-violating artifacts; session stamped to ledger.
246: TargetOutcome
247: Rejected without existing test_set_ref; acceptance per stratum; gate_policy recorded at definition.
248: Training Planner
249: Outcome → { coverage report, curriculum, milestone list, quote ± interval }; reproducible plan_id; plan without calibration stage rejected.
250: Training run
251: Commissioned-job contract; completion certificate incl. manifest hash and per-stratum results.
252: Voice identity
253: register strata + constructed organic parameters → identity; distance gate mandatory, fail-closed; certificate issued on pass; versioned; change by ceremony.
254: Commission View
255: Reads milestones, statuses, spend, and existing artifacts only; introduces no new backend computation.
256: 15  Build Sequence
257: Ordered by dependency and cost-of-deferral, not by size.
258: #
259: Item
260: Rationale for position
261: 1
262: Ingestion capture: language ID, code-switch points, condition profile, synthesis attributes (§4.1–4.4)
263: Everything downstream consumes these; only cheap at first ingestion. Deferral cost is a full re-pass over the estate.
264: 2
265: Dedup instance condition map (§4.5)
266: Contract change to existing machinery; near-zero new detection work.
267: 3
268: Character Register schema + custody invariant harness (§6)
269: The boundary must exist before the first cluster is stored; retrofitting means rebuilding from source.
270: 4
271: Codec service (§3)
272: Unsupervised pretraining starts on unlabelled audio while labelled work proceeds elsewhere.
273: 5
274: Clustering + sampled human validation (§5.3)
275: Requires 1–4.
276: 6
277: Objective Wizard variant + Collection Schema type + registry namespace (§8, §9, §12.1)
278: The planner must never accept a hand-authored Outcome once the wizard exists; building the planner first invites the malformed-input class the compile stage makes impossible.
279: 7
280: TargetOutcome type + planner core (§10, §11.1, §11.4)
281: Requires register strata to plan against and the wizard to author Outcomes.
282: 8
283: Sampling & Reflection machinery + milestone records (§11.2–11.3)
284: Requires 7 and a test set.
285: 9
286: Commission View (§13)
287: Reads records created in 8; by §13.4 it cannot precede them.
288: 10
289: Full training runs under the commissioned-job contract (§11.6)
290: Last by construction — the planner refuses to run earlier.
291: P2
292: Voice identity rendering; music register
293: Phase 2. Non-foreclosure is guaranteed by item 1 and §7.5.
294: 16  Verification Register and Open Decisions
295: 16.1  Items to verify against current code before build
296: Perception router contract — model registration point; whether a second output stream per segment is carried or the character stream needs its own artifact type (§3.2).
297: Ingestion segment boundaries — the unit a language label attaches to (§4.1).
298: Wizard B-2/B-3 landing state — extend the existing state machine with an objective variant, or stand a sibling machine on the shared agent interface and ledger sidecar (§8.5).
299: 16.2  Open decisions (owner: product)
300: N for the shared-attribute condition (§6.2.2): inherit the platform minimum-group-size seam value, or set a register-specific one.
301: Platform default for gate_policy (§10.1) where an Outcome does not set it: missed stratum gates release, or ships documented. This default silently decides how minority-variant quality is treated under schedule pressure.
302: Cluster naming validation: commissioned internally or delegated to an external evaluation partner where one exists (§5.3).
303: Codec choice: adopt an existing open codec versus training estate-specific — a trade the Sampling & Reflection machinery can itself answer once built (§3, §11.2).
304: Baseline tier contents (§9.2): the v1.0 set is the proposal; every addition is paid on every hour ingested, every omission is paid at re-ingestion.
305: 
306: End of specification. This document is the single build reference for the Audio Intelligence Plane; the working drafts it consolidates are retired.

# SOURCE: assessment_workspace/canon/drops/20260914_audio_plane_v1/raw/Audio_Intelligence_Plane.md
Coordinate: source line

1: **SYNI.AI   ·   ENGINEERING SPECIFICATION**
2: 
3: **The Audio Intelligence Plane**
4: 
5: *Extraction · Learning · Training · Invention — end to end*
6: 
7: Including the Commission View surface adjustment across all extraction types · v1.0
8: 
9: *Status of this document: consolidated build specification. It supersedes the working drafts (Audio Capability Spec v1.0 and Addendum v1.1.2) and is the single reference for build. Behavioural clauses state what the system must and must not do, including on failure. Technical clauses state contracts and acceptance criteria. Items requiring verification against current code before build are marked [VERIFY] and collected in §16.*
10: 
11: **Contents**
12: 
13: # **1  ****Governing Doctrine**
14: 
15: Five principles govern every clause in this specification. Where a later clause appears to conflict with one of these, the principle wins and the clause is defective.
16: 
17: ### **1.1  An audio file is a data estate, and the framing is recursive**
18: 
19: The archive is an estate; a programme is an estate; a single file is an estate. Segments are rows; the extractable layers — content, language, condition, prosody, occurrence, code-switch, music, group-level character — are columns; no schema exists until one is declared. Census, admission, registry, and record apply at every scale.
20: 
21: ### **1.2  Modality extension, not parallel machinery**
22: 
23: The audio plane introduces no sibling services. Mtafiti gains an audio modality; Northena gains audio data classes; the wizard gains an objective variant; Targeta gains a training object. Anything in this document that reads as a parallel to an existing service is rule proliferation and must be collapsed into the existing service before build.
24: 
25: ### **1.3  One record**
26: 
27: Mtafiti and Northena collaborate to produce a single record, written once. Working state — loss curves, intermediate metrics, partial coverage counts — is scratch, not truth; it becomes record only when finalized and stamped. No local ledger exists. If a measured throughput ceiling ever demands relief, the relief is batched stamping (one row certifying N events with a digest), which remains a single record. That change is made only when a measurement demands it.
28: 
29: ### **1.4  Measure, do not assert**
30: 
31: No data-volume requirement, accuracy expectation, or cost figure is quoted without a measurement behind it. The calibration stage exists to convert assertions into measurements before commitment.
32: 
33: ### **1.5  Unrepresentable, not policed**
34: 
35: Safety boundaries are enforced by making the violating state impossible to express in the contract — the pattern established by the assertion floor — not by review after the fact. The Character Register write path (§6) and the voice identity distance gate (§7) both follow this pattern.
36: 
37: # **2  ****Capability Statement and Plane Overview**
38: 
39: Given governed access to an audio estate, the plane provides four functions in one loop:
40: 
41: - **Extraction** — audio is converted into provenance-paired facts: transcripts, entities, occurrences, and character observations.
42: 
43: - **Learning** — a Character Register accumulates group-level knowledge of how the estate’s languages and audio behave.
44: 
45: - **Training** — model production is commissioned against a falsifiable Target Outcome, planned and priced before compute is spent, with per-example provenance.
46: 
47: - **Invention** — synthesized voice identities are constructed from the register: authentically of the language, provably of no individual.
48: 
49: Each function feeds the next: extraction populates the register; the register defines the strata training plans against; trained models improve extraction; invention consumes the register’s learned layers. The loop is the capability.
50: 
51: **Flow of a commission, end to end:**
52: 
53: Objective Wizard session → compile {TargetOutcome, Collection Schema}
54: 
55: → Sampling & Reflection (calibration) → proposed Milestones + priced quote
56: 
57: → Owner agrees milestones → Commission opens
58: 
59: → Collection → Register update → Curriculum → Training runs → Certificates
60: 
61: → Commission View reports against milestones throughout → Commission sealed
62: 
63: # **3  ****Tokenized Audio Representation**
64: 
65: ## **3.1  ****Behaviour**
66: 
67: - All downstream audio work — extraction, character analysis, training — operates on discrete token sequences produced by a neural audio codec, not on waveforms.
68: 
69: - Tokenization exposes two separable streams per segment: the **content stream** (what was said — input to ASR/NER) and the **character stream** (how it was said — input to the Character Register). The character stream is retained and routed, never discarded as noise.
70: 
71: - Control markers (language, register, segment type) are splice-able tokens, enabling one model per estate rather than one per language, and native handling of code-switched speech.
72: 
73: - Failure behaviour: audio in an unsupported condition fails closed with a stated reason. The codec never silently degrades quality.
74: 
75: ## **3.2  ****Technical contract**
76: 
77: | **Item** | **Specification** |
78: | --- | --- |
79: | **Service** | perception/audio_codec/ — registered like any other perception model; census-visible; runs in-perimeter on tenant compute. |
80: | **Input** | Audio segment (bounds per ingestion segmentation) + declared or detected condition profile. |
81: | **Output** | { content_tokens[], character_stream, codec_version } Target token rate 50–100 tokens/second of audio. |
82: | **Provenance** | codec_version is a mandatory field of every downstream artifact’s provenance. A transcript states which codec produced its tokens. |
83: | **Pretraining** | The codec pretrains unsupervised on unlabelled estate audio, under the standard commissioned-job contract. |
84: | **[VERIFY]** | Perception router contract: where model registration occurs, and whether the router carries a second output stream per segment or the character stream requires its own artifact type. |
85: 
86: ## **3.3  ****Acceptance criteria**
87: 
88: - Round-trip fidelity is measured and recorded per codec version before that version serves any commission.
89: 
90: - A downstream artifact lacking codec_version in provenance is rejected at the registry boundary.
91: 
92: - An unsupported-condition input produces a refusal with a stated reason and no output artifact.
93: 
94: # **4  ****Extraction Layer**
95: 
96: ## **4.1  ****Language identification**
97: 
98: Behaviour: every segment carries a real language signal. The current plumbing value (language_hint: None) is retired.
99: 
100: - A lightweight offline language identifier (CPU-viable, in-perimeter) runs at segment level during ingestion.
101: 
102: - Recorded per segment: languages[], confidences, and code-switch points where multiple languages occur in one utterance.
103: 
104: - The signal routes downstream model selection (ASR path, NER path, de-identification path) and is written into provenance.
105: 
106: **[VERIFY] **Segment boundaries in current ingestion — confirm the unit to which a language label attaches.
107: 
108: ## **4.2  ****Code-switch points as facts**
109: 
110: Switch points (position, from-language, to-language, context class) are registered facts with provenance — not preprocessing metadata. They populate the register’s code-switch layer and stratify test sets.
111: 
112: ## **4.3  ****Condition profiling**
113: 
114: Channel condition — studio / field / telephone band, transmission artefacts, background class — is derived per segment at first ingestion. It is cheap to compute, directly predictive of extraction error, and required for training stratification. It is captured at first ingestion because re-ingesting an estate to recover it is the unaffordable mistake.
115: 
116: ## **4.4  ****Synthesis-relevant attribute capture**
117: 
118: During the same ingestion pass, group-level acoustic attributes required by any future synthesis capability (pitch statistics, energy contours, duration patterns) are captured, subject to the custody conditions of §6.4. This forecloses nothing and costs little; omitting it forecloses the invention function or forces re-ingestion.
119: 
120: ## **4.5  ****Deduplication as augmentation**
121: 
122: The occurrence index already identifies repeated content. Its output contract is extended: for each deduplicated item, the instance condition map — the set of channel/time/condition variants under which identical content occurred — is retained. One canonical extraction is stored; the variant set enters training curricula as a designated robustness stratum at zero acquisition cost. No new detection work; this is a change to what dedup keeps.
123: 
124: ## **4.6  ****Acceptance criteria**
125: 
126: - No segment leaves ingestion without languages[], condition profile, and (where applicable) switch points in provenance.
127: 
128: - A deduplicated item without its instance condition map fails the ingestion invariant test.
129: 
130: - Baseline-tier capture (§9.2) runs for all admitted material regardless of any active objective.
131: 
132: # **5  ****The Character Register — Learning**
133: 
134: ## **5.1  ****Definition**
135: 
136: A registry-modality store of learned, group-level audio characteristics, built from the character stream. Same doctrine as the fact registry: every entry carries provenance to source material and an occurrence count. It is Mtafiti’s qualification-and-index doctrine applied to acoustic observations — an extension, not a sibling (§1.2).
137: 
138: ## **5.2  ****Layers**
139: 
140: | **Layer** | **Contents** | **Primary consumers** |
141: | --- | --- | --- |
142: | **Phonetic** | Per-lexeme pronunciation variants, frequency, regional distribution. | Curriculum; extraction lexicons; evaluation stratification |
143: | **Prosodic** | Intonation contours, stress, rate distributions, pause structure. | Training; programme-type classification |
144: | **Condition** | Channel and environment profiles. | Stratification; error prediction |
145: | **Code-switch** | Switch-point patterns, language pairs, context classes. | Training; test-set design |
146: 
147: ## **5.3  ****Build process**
148: 
149: Unsupervised clustering over the character stream yields candidate strata. A cluster asserts that a distinct variant exists — not what it is called. Naming and validation are human work applied to a sample, commissioned like any other qualified work with quoted cost.
150: 
151: # **6  ****Register Custody Boundary**
152: 
153: ## **6.1  ****Governing distinction: organic versus learned**
154: 
155: Organic characteristics are anatomical — vocal tract length, formant structure, glottal source, fundamental frequency range. They cannot be acquired or shed; they are what speaker verification keys on; they are biometric. They are never registered.
156: 
157: Learned characteristics are acquired from a speech community — phonological inventory, pronunciation variants, prosody, code-switching habits. They are group properties by construction. Only learned characteristics may be registered.
158: 
159: ## **6.2  ****The four conditions — all must hold**
160: 
161: - **Acquired, not anatomical. **The attribute is learnable by a speaker from a different background.
162: 
163: - **Shared. **Observed across at least N distinct speakers. N is a governed seam value; its default inherits the platform minimum-group-size parameter unless the tenant sets a register-specific value.
164: 
165: - **Non-reconstructive in combination. **Tested against attribute combinations, not attributes in isolation: language + region + age band + one distinctive feature can reach a single person even when each attribute is group-level.
166: 
167: - **Stored as description, not exemplar. **Centroids, distributions, frequencies. Never stored audio; never per-utterance speaker embeddings. Embeddings used during clustering are destroyed after cluster assignment. Provenance points to material, not to speaker identity.
168: 
169: ## **6.3  ****Enforcement shape**
170: 
171: The register write path exposes no field through which an instance-level representation can be stored: the schema cannot represent a voiceprint. Unrepresentable, not policed (§1.5). An automated invariant test attempts each known leakage path (small stratum, idiolect marker, narrowing combination, exemplar storage) and must fail to store all of them on every change to the register code.
172: 
173: ## **6.4  ****Idiolect rule**
174: 
175: Habitual fillers, characteristic phrasings, and idiosyncratically pronounced words are learned but individuating. They fail condition 2 or 3 and are excluded. “Learned” alone is never sufficient; the four conditions are conjunctive.
176: 
177: # **7  ****Synthesized Voice Identity — Invention**
178: 
179: ## **7.1  ****Mechanism: inherit the learned, synthesize the organic**
180: 
181: - Learned characteristics are inherited from the register — this is what makes the voice sound like a speaker of the language rather than a foreigner reading it.
182: 
183: - Organic characteristics are constructed — vocal tract parameters, F0 range, formant structure, glottal parameters are chosen as a point in acoustic space that no real speaker occupies.
184: 
185: This is the inverse of a voice clone. A clone copies the organic and frequently gets the learned wrong; this gets the learned right and owns the organic outright.
186: 
187: ## **7.2  ****The distance guarantee (mandatory, fail-closed)**
188: 
189: Every constructed identity is scored against every speaker representation derivable from the corpus using standard speaker-verification methods. A minimum distance from all of them is required. Below threshold, the identity is rejected and resampled. There is no override. The threshold value and the verification method are recorded with the identity.
190: 
191: ## **7.3  ****The certificate**
192: 
193: A passing identity is issued a certificate stating that the voice is provably derived from no individual, naming the method, the threshold, and the corpus version scored against. The certificate is a first-class sellable artifact.
194: 
195: ## **7.4  ****Identity composition and versioning**
196: 
197: | **Component** | **Source** |
198: | --- | --- |
199: | **Acoustic identity** | Constructed organic parameters (§7.1). |
200: | **Speech character** | Inherited from register — phonetic and prosodic layers. |
201: | **Interaction character** | Turn-taking, formality, code-switch behaviour — inherited from register. |
202: 
203: Each identity is a versioned artifact with a ledger entry. Changing one is a ceremony with the standard waiting period, because audience recognition accrues to the voice and recognition is the asset. Identities never drift.
204: 
205: ## **7.5  ****Scope note**
206: 
207: Rendering requires a synthesis stack, which is a separate build from recognition. What this specification requires now is non-foreclosure: the identity specification (attribute schema, distance method, certificate format) is defined, and §4.4’s ingestion capture ensures the substrate exists when rendering is built.
208: 
209: # **8  ****The Objective Wizard — Schema Compiler**
210: 
211: ## **8.1  ****Role**
212: 
213: No business user hand-writes a Target Outcome. The Objective Wizard — a new variant of the existing shaping wizard, reusing its agent interface, guards, session persistence, and ledger sidecar — elicits an objective in plain language and compiles two governed artifacts:
214: 
215: - **TargetOutcome** (§10) — handed to the Training Planner.
216: 
217: - **Collection Schema** (§9) — the data dictionary for this objective: which data points are extracted from the sound, at what granularity, at what quality bar.
218: 
219: ## **8.2  ****Elicitation sequence**
220: 
221: - The question the model must answer — operational and falsifiable.
222: 
223: - The population — resolved against existing register strata; unresolved populations are flagged as unmeasured and generate census work.
224: 
225: - The acceptance bar — per stratum, two-dimensional (§10), with the gate-or-document decision recorded explicitly.
226: 
227: - The collection consequences — the wizard derives required columns, shows which are already collected (baseline tier), which exist but are uncollected, and the cost of collecting them. The owner sees the price of the schema before commissioning.
228: 
229: ## **8.3  ****Dynamism within scope: propose, qualify, graduate**
230: 
231: - **Propose. **The agent side may propose novel data points no prior objective collected. This is where innovation enters.
232: 
233: - **Qualify. **A proposed column never enters collection directly. It is admitted as a candidate: collected on a sample only, its evidence of value measured against the objective — the same qualification path any fact travels.
234: 
235: - **Graduate. **Qualified candidates graduate into the objective tier for that commission. Graduation into the baseline tier is ceremony-governed (proposal, countersignature, waiting period), because a baseline column is paid on every hour ingested for the life of the estate.
236: 
237: The compile stage is deterministic throughout: the agent proposes; only qualified columns compile. Mechanical guards prove against a stub agent before any LLM is plugged in, per the existing standing disposition.
238: 
239: ## **8.4  ****Compile-time rejections**
240: 
241: The wizard cannot emit an artifact the downstream contracts would refuse. Rejected at compile, not warned:
242: 
243: - An Outcome without an existing test_set_ref.
244: 
245: - An acceptance bar missing the per-stratum dimension.
246: 
247: - A Collection Schema requiring a column whose capture violates the custody conditions of §6.2.
248: 
249: ## **8.5  ****Record and handoff**
250: 
251: Every session stamps to the ledger via the existing turn-ledger pattern under a distinct data class (objective_session), including options considered and rejected — which is what makes a later “why was the model built this way” answerable. Compiled artifacts hand off to Targeta through the existing admission-handoff pattern. Objective → schema → plan → run is one provenance chain.
252: 
253: **[VERIFY] **The B-2/B-3 landing state of the current wizard, before choosing between extending the existing state machine with an objective variant or standing up a sibling machine sharing the agent interface and ledger sidecar.
254: 
255: # **9  ****The Collection Schema**
256: 
257: ## **9.1  ****Definition**
258: 
259: The declared data dictionary of a commission: what is extracted from the sound, for what purpose, at what quality bar. It is the admission standard of the audio estate, per objective (§1.1). It has two tiers.
260: 
261: ## **9.2  ****Baseline tier**
262: 
263: Standing, objective-independent, collected at first ingestion for all admitted material. Membership criterion: cheap to collect now, unaffordable to collect later. Contents at v1.0: language identification, code-switch points, condition profile, dedup instance condition map, synthesis-relevant group-level acoustics (§4). Changes to the baseline are seam-governed — ceremony, countersignature, waiting period — because silently narrowing the baseline is how an estate quietly becomes unre-readable.
264: 
265: ## **9.3  ****Objective tier**
266: 
267: Declared per commission by the Objective Wizard. Collected against material already in governed scope, priced before collection starts, recorded in the commission’s registry namespace. Candidate columns enter through propose–qualify–graduate (§8.3) only.
268: 
269: # **10  ****The Target Outcome**
270: 
271: ## **10.1  ****Schema**
272: 
273: TargetOutcome {
274: 
275:   task          operational statement of what the model must do
276: 
277:   domain        context of use
278: 
279:   population    defined by reference to register strata, not labels
280: 
281:   acceptance    threshold per stratum; two-dimensional (accuracy, coverage)
282: 
283:   gate_policy   per Outcome: missed stratum gates release | ships documented
284: 
285:   test_set_ref  must exist before the Outcome is accepted
286: 
287:   constraints   latency, compute budget, deployment target
288: 
289: }
290: 
291: ## **10.2  ****Binding rules**
292: 
293: - **Population is register-defined. **“Language L, accent clusters 1–4, telephone band and studio, adult” — never “speakers of L.” This is what makes coverage computable.
294: 
295: - **Acceptance is per stratum. **A single global threshold hides the failure that matters: 94% on the majority variant and 61% on the rest passes one test and fails the one that decides whether the work reaches the people it was built for.
296: 
297: - **The test set precedes the training. **An Outcome without an existing, stratified test set is rejected at definition time.
298: 
299: - **The gate decision is recorded on the Outcome **at definition — not decided ad hoc at ship time.
300: 
301: # **11  ****The Training Planner**
302: 
303: ## **11.1  ****Architecture**
304: 
305: The existing planner pattern is reused unchanged: a deterministic core computes eligibility; a learned layer may only reorder an already-eligible set it receives stripped of the values that decided eligibility; a gate compares learned output against the deterministic baseline; every plan is reproducible from its recorded inputs.
306: 
307: |  | **Extraction planning (existing)** | **Training planning (new)** |
308: | --- | --- | --- |
309: | **Object** | Source locations | Register strata |
310: | **Floor** | Defensibility class | Acceptance threshold — accuracy × coverage |
311: | **Output** | Mining plan | Training plan + curriculum + milestones |
312: 
313: ## **11.2  ****Sampling ****&**** Reflection (calibration) — mandatory first stage**
314: 
315: Data requirements for low-resource fine-tuning are empirical; no analytical answer exists. The first commissioned stage is therefore a calibration: train at three to four data volumes, evaluate per stratum against the test set, fit the scaling curve, extrapolate to the acceptance threshold. Only then is the full run quoted, with a stated confidence interval — never a point estimate. A plan without a calibration stage is rejected. The first job prices the real job.
316: 
317: ## **11.3  ****Milestones — the accountability output**
318: 
319: Sampling & Reflection has two customers. It prices the real job, and it authors the accountability structure: its output to the objective owner is not a curve but a proposed milestone list — the checklist of what must be done, in what order, for the commission to succeed. Each milestone carries a done-condition and an owner. The objective owner reviews and agrees the list at commission; from that point, all reporting is against it. Accountability is set before spend, not discovered during.
320: 
321: ## **11.4  ****Planner outputs**
322: 
323: - Coverage report — per target stratum: hours available, quality distribution, gaps, cost of closing each gap.
324: 
325: - Curriculum — ordering and weighting across strata derived from the register, not from the corpus’s natural distribution, which is always skewed toward whatever occurred most. The dedup instance condition map enters as a designated robustness stratum.
326: 
327: - Proposed milestone list (§11.3).
328: 
329: - Cost quote with a stated confidence interval.
330: 
331: ## **11.5  ****Provenance through training**
332: 
333: Every training example carries its provenance into the training manifest. Consequences: rights are enforceable per example; an example whose rights lapse is identifiable and the affected models enumerable; and “the trained model is the customer’s property” is a statement backed by a manifest, not an assertion.
334: 
335: ## **11.6  ****Run governance**
336: 
337: Training runs are commissioned jobs under the existing contract: quoted before start, metered during, certificated on completion. The completion certificate records compute consumed, data touched, manifest hash, and per-stratum results against the Outcome. Failed strata are reported as plainly as passed ones.
338: 
339: # **12  ****Record and Registry Integration**
340: 
341: ## **12.1  ****Registry (Mtafiti audio modality)**
342: 
343: Per commission, a scoped namespace within the registry holds: the Collection Schema (versioned), collected data points mapped against it — with declared-but-not-yet-collected as first-class state — the strata referenced by the Outcome, and coverage state per stratum. Reads compose with the global registry; writes are namespace-scoped. On close, the namespace is sealed, not deleted: it is the record of what was collected and why, and the next objective’s wizard session queries prior schemas and coverage so the second project starts from the first project’s map.
344: 
345: ## **12.2  ****Record (Northena data classes)**
346: 
347: Training-workflow operations stamp into the one ledger under training-specific data classes: collection events, calibration runs, curriculum decisions, milestone status changes, run certificates. The workflow’s view of “its” record is a scoped lens filterable by commission ID — a view, not a store. Working state (loss curves, intermediate metrics, partial counts) is scratch until finalized and stamped once (§1.3).
348: 
349: # **13  ****Surface Specification — the Commission View**
350: 
351: ## **13.1  ****Scope**
352: 
353: This surface adjustment applies to all commissioned work on the platform — extraction, census, and training commissions alike, across every extraction type. No modality receives its own UI, and no surface is a rendering of backend internals: rendering internals quietly commits the backend to building displayable versions of its own machinery.
354: 
355: ## **13.2  ****Behaviour**
356: 
357: **The surface is milestones. The artifacts are evidence behind them.**
358: 
359: - At Sampling & Reflection, the proposed milestone list is presented to the objective owner for agreement. Commission does not open until it is agreed.
360: 
361: - The Commission View reports against the agreed checklist: each milestone with its done-condition and owner; status in plain terms — done, on track, behind, missed. Missed is shown as plainly as done.
362: 
363: - Spend against quote is shown at the same plain level.
364: 
365: - Technical material — calibration results, strata coverage, Collection Schema state — is drill-down evidence for whoever asks why a milestone reads as it does. It is never the front page.
366: 
367: ## **13.3  ****Modality leaf**
368: 
369: Modality appears at exactly one leaf: evidence inspection. Where provenance resolves to a recording, the source plays at its timestamp rather than rendering as a page region — the existing trust-receipt pattern (“a disputed number is answered by playing the tape”), unchanged.
370: 
371: ## **13.4  ****Backend cost constraint**
372: 
373: Milestones are records with done-conditions; the platform already stamps events. No new machinery is built for display. Any surface element in this section found to require new backend computation beyond reading existing artifacts is out of specification and must be removed or re-specified.
374: 
375: # **14  ****Interface Summary**
376: 
377: | **Surface** | **Contract** |
378: | --- | --- |
379: | **audio_codec** | audio in → { content_tokens, character_stream, codec_version }; fail-closed on unsupported condition. |
380: | **Language ID** | segment → { languages[], confidences, switch_points }; written to provenance. |
381: | **Occurrence index (ext.)** | dedup item → + instance condition map. |
382: | **Character Register** | Write path: schema cannot represent instance-level identity (§6.3). Read path: strata queries for planner and evaluation. |
383: | **Objective Wizard** | session → { TargetOutcome, CollectionSchema }; deterministic compile; compile-time rejection of contract-violating artifacts; session stamped to ledger. |
384: | **TargetOutcome** | Rejected without existing test_set_ref; acceptance per stratum; gate_policy recorded at definition. |
385: | **Training Planner** | Outcome → { coverage report, curriculum, milestone list, quote ± interval }; reproducible plan_id; plan without calibration stage rejected. |
386: | **Training run** | Commissioned-job contract; completion certificate incl. manifest hash and per-stratum results. |
387: | **Voice identity** | register strata + constructed organic parameters → identity; distance gate mandatory, fail-closed; certificate issued on pass; versioned; change by ceremony. |
388: | **Commission View** | Reads milestones, statuses, spend, and existing artifacts only; introduces no new backend computation. |
389: 
390: # **15  ****Build Sequence**
391: 
392: Ordered by dependency and cost-of-deferral, not by size.
393: 
394: | **#** | **Item** | **Rationale for position** |
395: | --- | --- | --- |
396: | **1** | Ingestion capture: language ID, code-switch points, condition profile, synthesis attributes (§4.1–4.4) | Everything downstream consumes these; only cheap at first ingestion. Deferral cost is a full re-pass over the estate. |
397: | **2** | Dedup instance condition map (§4.5) | Contract change to existing machinery; near-zero new detection work. |
398: | **3** | Character Register schema + custody invariant harness (§6) | The boundary must exist before the first cluster is stored; retrofitting means rebuilding from source. |
399: | **4** | Codec service (§3) | Unsupervised pretraining starts on unlabelled audio while labelled work proceeds elsewhere. |
400: | **5** | Clustering + sampled human validation (§5.3) | Requires 1–4. |
401: | **6** | Objective Wizard variant + Collection Schema type + registry namespace (§8, §9, §12.1) | The planner must never accept a hand-authored Outcome once the wizard exists; building the planner first invites the malformed-input class the compile stage makes impossible. |
402: | **7** | TargetOutcome type + planner core (§10, §11.1, §11.4) | Requires register strata to plan against and the wizard to author Outcomes. |
403: | **8** | Sampling & Reflection machinery + milestone records (§11.2–11.3) | Requires 7 and a test set. |
404: | **9** | Commission View (§13) | Reads records created in 8; by §13.4 it cannot precede them. |
405: | **10** | Full training runs under the commissioned-job contract (§11.6) | Last by construction — the planner refuses to run earlier. |
406: | **P2** | Voice identity rendering; music register | Phase 2. Non-foreclosure is guaranteed by item 1 and §7.5. |
407: 
408: # **16  ****Verification Register and Open Decisions**
409: 
410: ## **16.1  ****Items to verify against current code before build**
411: 
412: - Perception router contract — model registration point; whether a second output stream per segment is carried or the character stream needs its own artifact type (§3.2).
413: 
414: - Ingestion segment boundaries — the unit a language label attaches to (§4.1).
415: 
416: - Wizard B-2/B-3 landing state — extend the existing state machine with an objective variant, or stand a sibling machine on the shared agent interface and ledger sidecar (§8.5).
417: 
418: ## **16.2  ****Open decisions (owner: product)**
419: 
420: - N for the shared-attribute condition (§6.2.2): inherit the platform minimum-group-size seam value, or set a register-specific one.
421: 
422: - Platform default for gate_policy (§10.1) where an Outcome does not set it: missed stratum gates release, or ships documented. This default silently decides how minority-variant quality is treated under schedule pressure.
423: 
424: - Cluster naming validation: commissioned internally or delegated to an external evaluation partner where one exists (§5.3).
425: 
426: - Codec choice: adopt an existing open codec versus training estate-specific — a trade the Sampling & Reflection machinery can itself answer once built (§3, §11.2).
427: 
428: - Baseline tier contents (§9.2): the v1.0 set is the proposal; every addition is paid on every hour ingested, every omission is paid at re-ingestion.
429: 
430: *End of specification. This document is the single build reference for the Audio Intelligence Plane; the working drafts it consolidates are retired.*
431: 
432: Akki OS · Audio Intelligence Plane · Specification v1.0   ·

# SOURCE: assessment_workspace/canon/drops/20260914_pull_seam/extracted/The_Pull_Seam.txt
Coordinate: source line

1: SYNI.AI  ·  AKKI OS  ·  DESIGN PRINCIPLES
2: The Pull Seam
3: How Akki processes data without moving it
4: What this is
5: The design principles behind the pull seam — the mechanism by which an outside party can query, analyse, or train on a data estate while the estate's data stays inside its owner's perimeter.
6: Who it is for
7: Any technical reader. It assumes familiarity with networks, databases, and machine learning, and nothing about Akki.
8: The one idea
9: Reverse the direction of travel. Instead of sending data to where the compute is, put the compute where the data is, and let only governed results travel out.
10: Version
11: pull_seam_principles_v1 · 14 September 2026 · External
12: 1   The Problem
13: Almost every arrangement for letting an outside party work with your data moves the data. It is uploaded to a vendor's cloud, or a credential to all of it is handed to a service outside your network, or a contract promises it will be deleted afterwards. Once data is elsewhere, control of it is elsewhere too: it can be copied, breached, retained, or reused, and the owner learns about it after the fact if at all.
14: Data is most valuable exactly where it is most sensitive — in health, finance, government, research, media archives. Those are also the estates least able to move their data anywhere. The pull seam exists to make those estates usable without moving them.
15: 2   The Principles
16: Principle 1  Compute comes to the data. Never the reverse.
17: The platform runs on a sealed appliance installed inside the customer's own server room or field site. The appliance holds the GPUs. Queries execute on it. Models train on it. An outside party who wants a model shaped by the estate's data sends the model in; the model trains next to the data and leaves as weights. There is no configuration in which estate data is transferred to compute outside the perimeter. This is a prohibition with no exception, not a default setting.
18: Principle 2  One seam. Two ports. No third path.
19: The appliance exposes exactly two network interfaces on physically separate connectors, colour-keyed and labelled: ESTATE, which faces the customer's data network, and WAN, which faces the outside world. Data is read through ESTATE. Parties connect through WAN. Everything that moves from one side to the other passes through a single software crossing. That crossing is enforced at build time: exactly one function may perform it, and a scan on every build fails the build if a second path is introduced. Outbound network connections are allow-listed, so there is no route to an unlisted destination.
20: Principle 3  The two sides share nothing.
21: The estate and the outside party are separate trust domains. They share no identifiers, no storage, and no credentials. A record's identifier inside the estate means nothing outside it and resolves to nothing there. A party's key is its own — revocable in one act, expiring, non-transferable, never written to logs — and identifies an organisation that was admitted through a governed act by the estate owner's named authority.
22: Principle 4  Identity never crosses.
23: Before any result leaves, it passes through the crossing, which replaces identifiers and declared-confidential values with placeholder tokens according to each record's custody class. The party receives the answer to its question with identifying content substituted. Re-identification happens only inside the perimeter, and only for the estate's own use.
24: Principle 5  Six crossings, each governed on its own terms.
25: An outside party can do six things, and each is a different crossing with its own rules for what enters, what leaves, whether a human must approve, and what is recorded. Five of the six release a derivative — a count, a de-identified result, a derived finding, a trained model, a skill. Only one releases estate data itself, and it is deliberately not the ordinary crossing.
26: Operation
27: What enters
28: What leaves
29: Human approval
30: What is recorded
31: Browse the estate
32: Nothing
33: Aggregate composition only — never record contents
34: None
35: The access
36: Query (API)
37: The party's query
38: Results, de-identified
39: Only if controlled data is touched
40: Every query, every result
41: Processed intelligence
42: The party's objective
43: Derived output only — never source records
44: Only if controlled data is touched
45: Objective, output, records read
46: Train a model
47: The party's base model
48: Trained weights, with rights and hash stamped
49: Always
50: Training manifest, weights hash, terms
51: Build a skill
52: The party's skill objective
53: The skill file
54: Always
55: Skill hash, records read, terms
56: Download raw data
57: Nothing
58: Estate data itself
59: Always for controlled; owner-set otherwise
60: Every record, redaction log, sign-off
61: Principle 6  A trained model leaves only after it is measured.
62: Training changes weights, and weights carry the statistical influence of what they trained on. The platform does not pretend otherwise; it bounds that influence three ways. Training is differentially private by default, which limits how much any single record can shape the result. Before release, the trained model is probed for memorisation — sampled against the records it trained on — and does not pass until it sits beyond a set distance from every controlled record. And every release, of any kind, is debited against the estate's release budget: a ceiling on the total information that can ever leave, across all parties, all operations, and all time.
63: Principle 7  Every crossing is recorded — or it does not happen.
64: Each operation writes a receipt: what was accessed, in what quantity, under which terms, by which party, at what time. The receipt is written before the result is returned. If it cannot be written, the operation is refused. The same holds for every governing check: if an approval cannot be reached, a terms lookup returns nothing, or a check errors, the crossing fails closed. No path returns data, a result, or a model when a check did not complete.
65: Principle 8  Raw data leaves only through a separate outer gate.
66: Downloading estate data itself is not the ordinary crossing. It is a distinct outer gate with its own rules: disclosure depth is bounded by rights and custody, redaction runs as a gate rather than a suggestion, a named human signs off, and every released record is individually recorded. Everything else the seam supports releases a derivative. This is the only operation that releases the thing itself, and it is built to be the exception.
67: 3   Seeing It Work: A Query
68: 1.  The party connects on the WAN side  with its own key.
69: 2.  The query enters.  Nothing about the party crosses with it — no identifier from the party's side resolves inside the estate.
70: 3.  The query runs inside the perimeter,  on the estate's own compute, against data that never leaves the ESTATE side.
71: 4.  The result passes the crossing.  Identifiers and confidential values are replaced with placeholders according to custody class.
72: 5.  De-identified results leave on the WAN side.  If controlled data was touched, approval was required before step 3 ran; otherwise no human was in the loop.
73: 6.  A receipt is written.  If it cannot be, the operation is refused.
74: 4   Seeing It Work: A Training Run
75: 1.  The party's base model enters on the WAN side  and is admitted to estate compute. Before it touches any data it is run in a synthetic environment that probes it for hidden behaviour — a model is not trusted on arrival.
76: 2.  Training runs on the estate's GPUs,  against data in place, with a differentially private optimiser by default.
77: 3.  The result is gated before it can leave.  It must meet every accuracy criterion set before training started, or it is refused in full. It is probed for memorisation. Its draw against the release budget is checked.
78: 4.  Weights leave through the model registry,  carrying a rights posture, a recorded hash, and the terms in force. Weights derived from controlled data carry that fact on their registry entry permanently.
79: 5.  A receipt is written:  the training manifest, the weights hash, the terms.
80: What left: a trained model, measured and budgeted. What did not leave: any record it trained on. The data stayed on the ESTATE side of the appliance throughout.
81: 5   What Leaves, Stated Precisely
82: “Nothing leaves” is a slogan. The precise statement is this: no raw record leaves except through the outer gate with a named human's sign-off, and everything else that leaves is a governed derivative — de-identified results, derived intelligence, or measured artefacts — bounded in aggregate by the release budget and recorded individually. Nothing crosses outward that is not one of those, and each crossing has a receipt.
83: 6   Where the Principle Comes From
84: Compute-to-data is not new. Stored procedures send logic into the database rather than pulling rows out. Hadoop schedules jobs onto the nodes that hold the data because moving terabytes is the expensive part. Federated learning sends a model to where data lives and returns only the weight updates. Data clean rooms let two parties compute over combined data without either seeing the other's rows. Confidential computing processes data in a region the host cannot read.
85: The pull seam applies the same direction of travel to a whole estate and adds what those approaches mostly lack: one enforced boundary that every crossing passes through, six distinct crossings each governed on its own terms, measured release of trained artefacts, a finite budget on total release, and a receipt for everything. The principle is familiar. The enforcement is the design.
86: 7   The Trade-Off
87: Compute-to-data means the estate hosts the compute. GPU capacity sits on premises rather than being rented by the hour, and throughput is bounded by that hardware. An outside party's training job runs at the estate's speed. Batch and asynchronous work — analysis, extraction, training — fits this well; interactive, low-latency work fits it less well.
88: What the estate gets in return is the removal of an entire class of risk: no copy of the data elsewhere to breach, no egress to pay for, no deletion promise to audit, and no credential to a full dataset in someone else's key store. For a regulated or sovereignty-constrained estate, that is usually the right trade.
89: 8   What You Can Observe
90: Each principle above corresponds to something a technical reader can see directly on a deployed system.
91: Look at
92: What it shows
93: The appliance's front panel
94: Two ports, ESTATE and WAN, and nothing else. The GPUs are inside.
95: The build test output
96: The single-crossing check, passing on the current build.
97: The outbound allow-list
98: The only destinations the appliance can reach.
99: A receipt and its ledger entry
100: What crossed, how much, under which terms, by whom, when.
101: A memorisation probe result
102: A trained model measured against its own training records before release.
103: The release budget and its consumption
104: The ceiling on total release, and how much of it has been used.
105: The configuration
106: There is no setting that moves estate data to outside compute.
107: 9   Glossary
108: Term
109: Meaning
110: Estate
111: A data holding under one owner's custody — an archive, a database set, a corpus.
112: Seam
113: The single interface where the estate's domain meets an outside party's. Nothing else is shared across it.
114: Crossing
115: One of six governed operations by which something moves from one side of the seam to the other.
116: Custody class
117: A per-record classification governing how it may cross — what is de-identified, whether approval is required.
118: Controlled record
119: A record whose custody class requires approval before an operation touching it may run.
120: Release budget
121: A ceiling on the total information released from an estate across all parties, operations, and time.
122: Receipt
123: The record written for every crossing. If it cannot be written, the crossing does not happen.
