155: The buyer’s promise: know what you are buying, acquire it lawfully, and use it with confidence. The friction of acquisition is what renders as the assurance that makes the data theirs.
156: [Heading 2] 31.1  Shaping within offerability
157: The shaping agent works within offerability — owned estate only, licence class, disclosure limits — and may propose, because steering a buyer toward a cheaper feasible shape is sales rather than laundering. This is the one place the shaping agent’s posture differs from its operator variant, which asks and never proposes.
158: A shape outside offerability is refused with the reason. The buyer never sets lawful basis; use-purpose drives licence class instead. Price and delivery time compute live and move as the shape moves, so the trade-off between what is wanted and what it costs stays visible while it can still be changed.
159: [Heading 2] 31.2  Acquisition
160: The outer gate’s five checks are the acquisition — rights, irreversibility, cumulative disclosure, licence issue, and receipt — rendered as assurance rather than as obstacles. Nothing partial egresses here either.
161: [Heading 2] 31.3  The deliverable
162: Per-claim class on every item, and a receipt that resolves publicly by trace identity — the same record any audit sees. The receipt renders the fact and the fingerprint of the transform only, never anything that could aid reversal.
163: [Heading 1] 32  The Customer Portal
164: An external party that has purchased intelligence needs to receive it, integrate against it, see what they have consumed, and manage their account — without the platform exposing anything beyond what they actually bought.
165: Scope is enforced at the persistence layer. A query outside the customer’s own account does not execute. Enforcement at the interface layer would make the boundary a convention any new code path could eventually bypass.
166: Purchased intelligence carries its licence label and its quality card — what was bought, at what standard, under what terms to use it. Consumption is metered at the boundary, because unmetered consumption is unpriceable consumption, and value that leaves without a meter cannot be accounted for afterward.
167: PART VI
168: 
169: Traces and Failure
170: [Heading 1] 33  Three Traces, End to End
171: [Heading 2] 33.1  A call arrives and is answered
172: The key resolves to its objective version, its memory plane, and its rights envelope. Admission checks completeness and consults feasibility: the ask is servable from qualified intelligence, so it forks warm. Retrieval draws from the evidence partitions within the plane’s own retrieval scope — never the raw estate, and never material the plane cannot reach. Where composition reaches a model, the call transits the boundary chokepoint: de-identified, invoked, re-identified, receipted. The grounding gate enforces the anchor map. The assertion boundary computes the class as the floor over the load-bearing units. The answer returns with its class inline and its trace identity resolvable, and the Ledger records the call.
173: Where it can go otherwise: the material has not been extracted, and a not-extracted-yet refusal offers to file the work; the evidence cannot support the claim, and the refusal names the specific reason; the composition cannot be grounded, and it refuses rather than degrading; retrieval times out, and a fault surfaces on the fault channel — never dressed as either kind of refusal.
174: [Heading 2] 33.2  A fresh objective is delivered
175: Admission forks fresh and returns an accepted acknowledgement with an objective identity, a delivery estimate, and a quote. Work dispatches. The application receives a thin webhook carrying the event, the objective identity, the trace identity, and the status — no content. It fetches the result over its own authenticated key, where scope is enforced server-side. The outer gate runs its five checks before anything leaves, and mints a receipt. The deliverable carries per-claim class; the receipt resolves publicly by trace identity.
176: Where it can go otherwise: the run is cancelled, and nothing partial egresses while the cancellation is still recorded; the run is refused after acceptance, and the same refusal envelope returns as a governed terminal state; the request is retried, and the idempotency key resolves it to the existing objective rather than a second one.
177: [Heading 2] 33.3  An application contributes and later publishes
178: The application writes a derived conclusion back to its plane. The API boundary checks the five-ring shape: content, provenance including the calls it derived from, class, context, and a re-derivation handle. The class is capped at what the cited sources support. The unit lands plane-local, carrying internal-only rights, invisible to every other consumer, and the write lands in the Ledger and in the per-application view of the compliance record. Later, the organisation elects to publish it: the unit passes the quality row for its output class, carries its rights, and — where governance values require — passes release review. Only then does it become Registry-visible.
179: Where it can go otherwise: the contribution is incomplete, and it rejects at the boundary rather than being stored and flagged; the cited sources cannot support the asserted class, and the class is capped rather than the write being accepted at face value; the volume ceiling is reached, and further writes refuse for the cycle; the key is revoked, and the plane freezes with unpublished contributions deleting alongside it.
180: [Heading 1] 34  Failure
181: A fault is distinct from a refusal everywhere in this contract, and the distinction is never blurred for convenience. A refusal is the system working correctly and declining; a fault is the system failing to evaluate a request at all. The reference application’s three visually distinct refusal-adjacent states — not-extracted-yet, evidence-cannot-support, something-broke — make this legible even to a person who has never read this document: the third state shares nothing with the first two, because what it means to the reader is entirely different.
182: A retried request after a fault is safe by construction, everywhere idempotency applies. A caller that retries on fault and receives a refusal instead has learned something real — the request was in fact evaluated between the retry and the response — rather than having triggered a second attempt at the same operation.
183: PART VII
184: 
185: The Function & Promise Registry
186: [Heading 1] 35  What It Is
187: One canonical, versioned artefact registers every named function in the platform — a gate, an engine behaviour, a worker obligation, a console guarantee — with the promise it protects and its full accounting. It begins as a governed document and, on dispatch, graduates to a machine-readable artefact. It is the single source every standing query runs against, the input the sequencing harness optimises over, and the operating context a model worker itself receives.
188: Every function belongs to one of the six engines, to the Watch, or to a named surface for an interface-level guarantee. No new top-level category is added without explicit ratification.
189: [Heading 1] 36  Schema — One Row Per Function
190: All fields are mandatory. A row missing any of them is not a registered function.
191: <<TABLE>>
192: Field | Definition and discipline
193: function_id | A stable identifier, namespaced under its owning engine or surface. Never reused.
194: governor | The owning authority — one of the six engines, the Watch, or a named surface. No new top-level category without ratification.
195: mandate | "Built to …" — one sentence, active voice, testable. What the function does, never how.
196: promise | "Why this matters …" — the promise protected, phrased so its breach is observable. Many functions may cite one promise; no function may cite zero.
197: service_trace | The service sentence and journey step this promise secures. An empty or invalid trace is an orphan.
198: surface | Where it acts — module path, route, contract, console element.
199: enforcement | The mechanism class: byte-identity lock, structural walk, negative scan, runtime check, end-to-end cell, type-level wall, or constraint architecture. Natural-language-only is not a legal value.
200: cost | Execution time class, maintenance burden, false-positive rate where known. Unknown is a legal initial value, replaced by measurement the first time the sequencing harness exercises the function.
201: dependencies | Functions or data this one requires ordered-before it. The input to sequencing.
202: ladder_rung | The implementing rung. A written justification is required for any placement above the cheapest plausible one.
203: owner | The change authority for this row.
204: <<END TABLE>>
205: [Heading 1] 37  Derivation Rules
206: Binding on every function in the registry, without exception.
207: [List Paragraph] No gate without a promise. A function whose promise field cannot be honestly filled is not refactored into legitimacy; it is retired.
208: [List Paragraph] No promise without a service trace. A promise serving no journey step of any service sentence is either mis-stated or evidence of drift — escalated, never papered over.
209: [List Paragraph] No journey step without enforcement. Every step of every service journey resolves to at least one registered function protecting it. An unprotected step is reported as an exposed liability, never assumed safe.
210: [List Paragraph] New functions register before they land. Any proposal introducing a gate or a worker obligation includes its registry row as part of its own ruling surface, not as a follow-up.
211: [Heading 1] 38  The Three Standing Queries
212: Run on every registry change, and on a standing cadence besides. Results are reports; retiring or merging a function executes through the platform’s own ruling process, never automatically.
213: <<TABLE>>
214: Query | What it finds
215: Redundancy | Two or more functions sharing the same promise and the same surface — merge or retire candidates, ranked by cost.
216: Orphans | A function with an empty or invalid promise or service trace — a retirement candidate on sight.
217: Gaps | A promise or journey step with no function enforcing it — an exposed-liability report, surfaced before an incident finds it instead.
218: <<END TABLE>>
219: [Heading 1] 39  Population Is Archaeology, Not Authorship
220: The registry populates by extraction from what already exists — engine mandate documents, the rulings record, close-report gate rosters. It invents nothing: where extraction finds a gate whose promise cannot be recovered, that is an orphan finding, never an invitation to write one in.
221: [Heading 1] 40  The Registry Pays Rent
222: The registry is subject to its own law. Its rent is the three standing queries — if it stops retiring functions, finding gaps, or cheapening sequences over a sustained period, it is itself restructured. One artefact, one schema; a second layer above it is a defect on sight.
223: PART VIII
224: 
225: The Critic Seam
226: [Heading 1] 41  What It Is
227: Every intelligent worker in the build produces output whose quality would otherwise be assured by exactly one mechanism: a person reading it and catching errors by hand. This layer mechanises the half of that catching which is mechanisable — verification of worker output against the on-disk record. It deliberately does not attempt the other half.
228: [Heading 2] 41.1  The mechanisable split
229: Every catch this layer makes is a verification: the truth already existed on disk, and the worker diverged from it. Verifications mechanise. Frame changes do not — a decision that rewrites what the product is, what a service means, or what standard applies is a change to canon, not a divergence from it, and no layer that verifies against canon can ever catch a correction to canon. Frame authority sits permanently outside this layer’s scope.
230: [Heading 1] 42  Design Principles
231: [List Paragraph] Detect, never decide. The layer emits findings; every consequence is a ruling made elsewhere. A quality layer with veto power over workers would be a governor nobody actually mandated.
232: [List Paragraph] Canon is the oracle. All deterministic verification resolves against the on-disk record — never against a summary, a context window, or another model’s recollection of what the record says.
233: [List Paragraph] Zero loop drag. The layer adds no turns and never blocks execution mid-flight: deterministic checks run as cells at submission boundaries, the critic runs asynchronously between turns, and findings arrive with the artefacts they review, never before them.
234: [List Paragraph] Halving, not zeroing — stated honestly. A critic sharing a worker’s blind spot misses exactly what both cannot see. The claim made is that it catches the record-verifiable half and measurably shrinks what remains, never that it catches everything.
235: [List Paragraph] The critic is calibrated like a model, because it is one. Catch rate and false-alarm rate per worker class are versioned, measured numbers, maintained by human sampling on an ongoing basis.
236: [List Paragraph] The layer pays rent. Its own catch-and-false-alarm ledger stands exactly as any function’s does — if it stops catching and starts noising, it shrinks or retires by ruling. No layer sits above it, ever.
237: [Heading 1] 43  Tier One — Deterministic Record Verification
238: Six check families, all mechanical, all resolving against the repository, running as cells at both submission boundaries and on ruling documents at landing time. Each emits a pass or a finding row.
239: Acceptance requires all six families to run at both boundaries; a run without them is incomplete. Findings are cross-referenced and never duplicated, and the checks themselves register in the Function & Promise Registry with their own rows — they are functions, and they pay rent like every other one.
240: The residual is conceded openly: Tier One verifies form and existence, not pertinence — an artefact written to the letter of its schema can still cite real hashes for irrelevant objects. Pertinence is exactly the second tier’s rubric, and the two tiers are designed as a deliberate pair; adopting Tier One alone buys the cheap half of the guarantee while advertising the whole of it.
241: [Heading 1] 44  Tier Two — The Critic Pass
242: An independent model instance reviews each proposal and close report against a fixed rubric, asynchronously, after landing. Its output is a findings report — classed, cited, never blocking, never editing.
243: [Heading 2] 44.1  Independence
244: The critic never shares the worker’s conversation. Its context is exactly the artefact under review, the canon set, the authorising instrument, and the rubric — never the worker’s own reasoning, drafts, or self-justification. A critic reading the author’s rationale inherits the author’s frame, which is the blind-spot-sharing failure this whole design exists to avoid.
245: No worker critics its own output. Where both instances share a base model, independence is held by context isolation alone, and seeded audits measure whether that isolation is actually sufficient. The critic runs at the cheapest sufficient rung, one review per artefact rather than per token, with cost per review held as a standing metric throughout.
246: Findings carry the platform’s own honesty grammar: a finding states what it checked, what it found, at what confidence class, with citations. An unclassed finding is itself a finding.
247: [Heading 2] 44.2  Three failure modes, answered structurally
248: <<TABLE>>
249: Failure mode | Structural answer
250: Rubber-stamping | A critic that finds nothing is indistinguishable from a critic that looked at nothing. Answered by seeded-defect audits: found-nothing is credible only from a critic whose detection is measured against known positives.
251: Noise | A critic rewarded for finding things drowns rulings in trivia. Answered by the false-alarm ledger: a critic whose findings are repeatedly ruled non-findings has its rubric tightened, or its scope shrunk, by ruling.
252: Infinite regress | Who reviews the reviewer? Stopped by construction — the critic’s own findings are subject to deterministic checks and human sampling only. There is no critic of the critic, and proposing one is itself a finding.
253: <<END TABLE>>
254: [Heading 1] 45  Tier Three — Human Calibration
255: The reviewing role compresses under this design; it does not disappear. Three lightweight instruments, all producing versioned numbers: the matrix’s own stratified human samples double as the critic’s calibration — catch rate and false-alarm rate per output class, versioned, staleness-marked.
256: A critic whose calibration has gone stale past its window has its findings marked uncalibrated at render — the identical honesty rule the platform applies to model confidence anywhere else. A stale quality layer says so, visibly, rather than continuing to speak with unearned authority.
257: One calibration mechanism serves three consumers throughout the platform: fact-confidence calibration, the build-time critic’s ledger, and the production critic’s per-class ledger are the same versioned, staleness-marked form, used three times over. A second, parallel calibration mechanism anywhere is a defect on sight.
258: [Heading 1] 46  What This Layer Is Not
259: [List Paragraph] Not a governor. It holds no mandate, asserts nothing about the estate, and gates nothing but form. A proposal for veto authority is rejected in advance, not debated on arrival.
260: [List Paragraph] Not a replacement for the human seat. Frame changes are constitutionally outside a canon-verifying layer’s reach. The largest course corrections any build undergoes are frame changes, and this layer would catch none of them — by design, not by oversight.
261: [List Paragraph] Not inline. Nothing here adds a synchronous step to any serving path, or a turn to any loop.
262: [List Paragraph] Not a new meta-artefact class. It reuses the platform’s own standing machinery — query patterns, registry rows, the calibration-ledger form — rather than inventing its own.
263: [List Paragraph] Not a zero-residual claim. It halves the residual, measurably and repeatedly. Its own dashboard is built to show its misses, not to hide them.
264: PART IX
265: 
266: Discipline
267: [Heading 1] 47  Defect Classes
268: Named, and reportable on sight by anyone — owner, builder, or system — working on the platform.
269: <<TABLE>>
270: Class | Definition
271: D1 · Orphan gate | A function with no honest promise, or no service trace.
272: D2 · NL-only enforcement | A rule whose only enforcement is prose interpretation, with no machine-checked twin.
273: D3 · Curated verdict | Any selection of validation material by favourability rather than measured composition.
274: D4 · Rung inflation | Model-ladder placement above cheapest-sufficient, with no written justification on record.
275: D5 · Meta-spiral | A second governance layer above one that already exists; a governance artefact that has stopped paying rent.
276: D6 · Service conflation | A platform function optimised for an end-user persona rather than for a service sentence — the wrong job, done well.
277: D7 · Invented schedule or scope | Sequencing, deferral, or workstreams introduced without explicit instruction — binding on the ruling authority and the builder alike, with no exception for either.
278: D8 · Dual-identity execution | A task holding, or a code path permitting, more than one authority's identity or scope within a single execution — including any evidence crossing between the authorities outside the matrix of Document 9.
279: <<END TABLE>>
280: [Heading 1] 48  Canon Before Ruling
281: No decision proceeds from memory or summary where the governing document exists. Unread canon is read before ruling — binding on the ruling authority and the builder alike, with no exception for either.
282: This is the same doctrine stated in Document 1, applied here to its most concrete case: a builder characterising what an engine does, what a spec requires, or what was already decided must read the document rather than recall it. A recollection presented as fact, where the written record exists and was simply not consulted, is the exact failure this rule exists to prevent — and it is a failure this specification’s own construction encountered and corrected before landing.
283: [Heading 1] 49  Every Phase Closes on Disk
284: A phase opens with a proposal written to disk and closes with a close report carrying its gate roster with results, its artefact hashes, its registry attestation, a conformance table, and a self-audit. A phase with no on-disk close report is not closed, whatever a conversation about it concluded.
285: A self-audit row whose evidence is "reviewed" or "checked manually" is not evidence. The evidence column names a test identifier, a gate result, or an artefact hash — something another reader could go and verify independently.
286: Every ruling taken lands the same day as a file citing what it rules on. A ruling that exists only in conversation does not exist. Every new function registers its row before it lands, as part of the same ruling surface rather than as a follow-up task. And the build journal carries no undocumented window — a gap is closed by a reconciliation entry enumerating every change landed within it, with citations; an undocumented window is a violation in itself, independent of what happened inside it.
287: [Heading 1] 50  What This Specification Comes Down To
288: A request is answered warm or forked fresh, once, at the boundary, and every consumer downstream honours that fork rather than re-deriving it. A refusal is a governed outcome carrying a named reason and an action the reader can actually take — never an error, and never a dead end dressed as a door. An application’s memory grows from what it actually uses, stays isolated by construction rather than by discipline, and is visible to the estate holder in full. Every function in the platform can state the promise it protects and the journey step that promise secures, or it is retired. And nothing about how the platform was built is trusted to memory where the record already exists to be read instead.

Coordinate: source line

1: # SOURCE FILE: Akki_Canon_8_The_Watch.docx
2: 
3: AKKI CANON  ·  DOCUMENT 8 OF 9
4: The Watch
5: The security authority: its promise, doctrines, the two engines and the verdict, the response arms, marks and signatures, the mirage, the console, and the parameters it is held to
6: PART I
7: 
8: The Promise
9: [Heading 1] 1  What the Watch Is
10: The Watch is the platform's security authority. It stands beside the governing authority — the six engines of Documents 2 through 4 — as a peer, subordinate to nothing, and it answers the one question the governors structurally cannot: not *was this permitted*, but *was this intended, and is this actor, input, and action what it claims to be?* Every gate can pass, every receipt can be clean, and the damage can still be happening — a valid credential misused, a poisoned context producing perfectly authorised behaviour, a purpose laundered across a chain of individually lawful calls. The Watch exists for exactly that gap.
11: To the operating organisation: continuous, machine-speed detection and response against misuse of the estate and the platform — invisible in legitimate use, incapable of acting unobserved, extracting intelligence from every attack it defeats, and proving its own fitness on a standing cadence without human effort.
12: Every Watch function traces to this sentence, exactly as every governance function traces to a service sentence of Document 1 §12. Every parameter in Part IX protects a clause of it. Nothing in the Watch is proposed, evaluated, or justified by anything else.
13: [Heading 1] 2  Why It Exists
14: The platform's own promise is the provocation. A product that declares custody and provability invites the test — ethical and hostile alike — and nobody attacks a system that claims nothing. The estate concentrates exactly what an attacker wants: qualified intelligence, credentials, trained models, and a record whose corruption would be worth more than any single theft. The conventional layer — access control, encryption, the certifiable surface — answers the human attacker and the stolen credential at the moment of entry. It has nothing to say about the attack that arrives as input, drifts in as behaviour, or hides inside authorisation. Those are the Watch's.
15: Three attack shapes drove every structural decision in this document. The machine-speed attack, which is over before any human wakes: the answer is autonomy made safe by construction. The slow play, which drifts beneath every threshold: the answer is the strata of Part IV — a floor that cannot learn, a cohort that is hard to boil, a signature that cannot be stolen, and an accumulation view that reads patience back at the attacker. And the authorised attack, which never breaks a rule: the answer is declared intent, reconciled against realised conduct.
16: [Heading 1] 3  What the Watch Is Not
17: [List Paragraph] Not a seventh engine. The six engines constitute the governing authority; the Watch is the second authority beside it. It performs none of their functions — it does not admit, measure, target, reason, gate the boundary, or improve judgement — and none of them performs its.
18: [List Paragraph] Not a layer above governance. A second governance layer above one that already exists is the meta-spiral defect Document 7 §47 names. The Watch escapes that class by construction: it asks a different question, on a different clock — governance works run by run and converges; the Watch never converges and never concludes — and it holds no authority over any governance verdict.
19: [List Paragraph] Not an observer. The Watch acts, autonomously, within the bounds of Part VI. A detection system that must wake a person before acting has a response measured in hours against attacks measured in seconds — an expensive solution with no additional benefit. Observe-first deployment is prohibited by its own doctrine W4.
20: [List Paragraph] Not a data consumer. The Watch reads evidence and behaviour to protect the estate; it never feeds analytics, scoring, pricing, or management visibility. Its one profile store is armory under W13, renderable to no surface.
21: PART II
22: 
23: The Doctrines
24: [Heading 1] 4  Fourteen Doctrines
25: These bind every part of the Watch and everything it touches. Each carries the reasoning that is its authority; a clause anywhere in this document that contradicts one is defective and is corrected against the doctrine, never the reverse.
26: [Heading 2] 4.1  W1 · The eyes never act; the hand never judges
27: Detection asserts facts; response executes policy; one verdict is the only interface between them.
28: A detector that knows a severance follows its verdict is tuned defensively, and detection quality silently degrades to protect response comfort — the documented death of most security operations. A responder that deliberates is slow, and speed is the promise. So the Watch is two engines: Macho, the eyes, which senses and asserts and holds no powers whatsoever; and Mkono, the hand, which acts and holds no judgement — a deterministic mapping from verdict properties to actions. This is the platform's own standing rule — learning may detect, it may never decide — applied to security whole.
29: [Heading 2] 4.2  W2 · Certainty never exceeds evidence
30: Structural certainty is assertable only from signals an outsider cannot fabricate. Everything externally steerable caps at reversible containment, whatever its score.
31: The closed sever-certainty registry — canary touch, attestation failure, mark hit, witness-write attempt, floor violation, mirage incrimination — is the whole of what may unlock the Watch's maximum autonomous force. A content score or a behavioural pattern, however confident, is a signal an attacker can shape, and a system whose maximum power can be triggered from outside is a weapon handed to whoever learns to trigger it. The certainty computation is a function with no parameter through which a detector's confidence can enter — Solva's own assertion boundary, transplanted: the signature is the guard.
32: [Heading 2] 4.3  W3 · Every autonomous act is reversible, bounded, and witnessed
33: A time-to-live on every action; a blast budget on every window; act-and-attest atomically, peer-countersigned. Destroy does not exist in the Watch.
34: Autonomy is safe by construction or it is not safe. An action that expires unless renewed converts the false positive from a harm into a delay; a budget converts the autoimmune attack — tricking the immune system into suspending the business — from an outage into a bounded cost; atomic attestation makes weaponizing the Watch impossible to do quietly, which for a detection system is the property that matters. And a power the tool structurally lacks cannot be turned: the Watch can stop anything and erase nothing — deletion remains solely the authority act of Document 3 §27.
35: [Heading 2] 4.4  W4 · Deployed in force, never in shadow
36: Every Watch mechanism ships with defined conditions of success and runs at full authority from first deployment. A mechanism whose parameters are undefined is a specification gap to close, never a reason to run tentatively.
37: The promise is response speed; a watching-only mode spends the entire value to buy nothing. This is the platform's single-experiment principle holding in the one place it is most tempting to break.
38: [Heading 2] 4.5  W5 · One record, two readings
39: The Watch maintains no account of anything but its own events, and its records are classes in the platform's one record per the matrix of Document 9. The deception the mirage shows an attacker is a rendering. The record never lies inward.
40: The Watch mints the first account of its own events — verdicts, actions, attestations, marks — and a second account of nobody else's. The compliance owner reads those records as assurance; the watch officer reads them as defence; the auditor and the defender can never disagree, because there is only one set of facts underneath both readings.
41: [Heading 2] 4.6  W6 · Suspicion is refined, not accumulated
42: Probabilistic detection routes to conditions — friction, narrowed envelopes, the mirage — where the actor's own conduct converts suspicion into certainty or innocence. The Watch does not convict on statistics.
43: The mirage is the refinery: an innocent misrouted into it does ordinary work, trips nothing, and releases on expiry; an attacker cannot help but incriminate, because the actions that advance the objective are exactly the actions that convict. Suspicion at eighty percent becomes caught touching a planted credential — zero false positives by construction — and only then does maximum force apply.
44: [Heading 2] 4.7  W7 · Conformance grants trust; non-conformance never convicts
45: The behavioural signature buys legitimate actors invisibility. Losing conformance returns an actor to baseline verification and nothing more; deviation combines with other signals and is never sole grounds past friction.
46: The worst the signature can ever do to an innocent is make their day ordinary. This asymmetry is what makes behavioural authentication survivable for the people it protects — and it is constitutional, not tunable.
47: [Heading 2] 4.8  W8 · The floor never learns
48: Beneath every adaptive layer stands the ruled floor — deterministic, moved only by visible, delayed, two-signature ceremony — and the ceremony is itself a monitored tripwire.
49: What learns can be taught; the slow play boils the learned profile one degree at a time. What is ruled cannot be taught, and an attacker who needs the floor moved must request it in daylight, on a countdown, under two names, with the Watch itself among the observers per Document 3 §24.
50: [Heading 2] 4.9  W9 · No actor enters undeclared
51: Every actor arrives with a declared mandate — objective, capabilities, and risks for an agent; role and interests for a person — frozen at admission, reconciled against for as long as the actor acts.
52: Intent divergence is undefined without declared intent; the declaration of Document 3 §6.1 is the baseline the Watch's reconciliation runs against. Re-declaration through the same admission path is the legitimate exit from honest change — undeclared drift is a signal; declared change is a non-event — and the undeclared actor operates under the default-restrictive envelope until characterised.
53: [Heading 2] 4.10  W10 · The watcher is watched from outside
54: Watch liveness is attested by a component holding no Watch credentials; Watch silence is itself an alarm; the platform's fail-closed posture is independent of the Watch entirely.
55: The service whose compromise would mean going unobserved must be incapable of unobserved existence — and equally incapable of failing anything open. Custody gates fail closed on their own, per Document 1 §4.1, with or without the Watch above them.
56: [Heading 2] 4.11  W11 · One task, one identity
57: Every task executes under exactly one authority's identity and scope. Capacity is shared across time; execution is never shared within a task.
58: The blended-privilege surface — a task that could see like security and decide like governance — must not exist to be compromised. Dual identity is unrepresentable in the task register of Document 9, not policed; its appearance anywhere is defect class D8.
59: [Heading 2] 4.12  W12 · Peer, not subordinate
60: Neither authority commands the other or writes the other's law. Disagreement — permitted but not intended — resolves by temporary, reversible containment plus a person, and the disagreement itself is a record.
61: A security function that reports to the thing it must be able to contain loses exactly the fight that is the product: the clean receipt with the wrong intent. The Watch authors its own policy; the rules service administers the ceremony of changing it, without editorial power — and symmetrically, governance rules bind the Watch's workers like anyone's.
62: [Heading 2] 4.13  W13 · The profile is armory, not inventory
63: Behavioural-conformance parameters are per-actor, tenant-keyed, non-exportable, purpose-bound to the Watch alone, and renderable to no surface, export, or analytic — ever.
64: A trust mark that leaks into scoring, pricing, or management visibility becomes surveillance, and surveillance destroys the trust the product sells. The store holds learned parameters, never the raw action history that trained them; no read path to its internals exists for any surface, including the Watch's own console. These parameters are a security instrument with a security owner — a different object entirely from the identification biometrics whose register Document 1 §4.2 forbids, and neither is ever a field in the other.
65: [Heading 2] 4.14  W14 · Self-proving, or not in force
66: Every response rail demonstrates itself firing on a standing drill cadence — full loop, both engines, latencies measured, results as receipts. A rail not demonstrated firing is not in force, whatever the inventory claims.
67: The drill receipts are the audit. When the compliance owner, a customer, or a regulator asks whether the Watch works, the answer is a standing dataset requiring no human assembly — which is what *auditable without much human intervention* means, delivered by the same mechanism that keeps the Watch honest with itself.
68: PART III
69: 
70: Two Engines, One Verdict
71: [Heading 1] 5  Macho — The Eyes
72: Macho observes, scores, and asserts facts. It holds no powers: it cannot block, throttle, mark, reroute, or notify. Its sole output is the verdict. Because it is consequence-blind, it is judged on one thing only — whether the fact was true — and its corpora, models, and thresholds evolve without a single response rule moving.
73: <<TABLE>>
74: Sensor | What it asserts
75: Lango · the input seat | Every payload bound for a model — prompt, retrieved unit, tool result, memory read, agent instruction — scored for hostility and provenance at the boundary governor's chokepoint, between de-identification and invocation, per Document 3 §13.1. Graded verdicts: pass, annotate, hold, block.
76: The envelope, read as drift | Every actor's behavioural envelope — tools, data classes, rhythm, depth — departed from. One substrate with the signature below; this is its negative reading.
77: The reconciler | Realised action trees reconciled against declared mandates — the intent question itself, computed off the hot path within its latency bound. A divergence verdict that cannot walk back to its originating instruction is an opinion and does not count.
78: The cohort | Individual conduct against the population's compliance norm — the reading that catches the actor whose drift is invisible against their own history and loud against their peers.
79: The collision detector | Behavioural signatures are effectively unique at full dimensionality. One signature alive in two divergent embodiments is a hijack in the act; a “new” actor resolving onto a marked signature is a re-entry. Both are near-structural.
80: The tripwires | Planted records, decoy credentials, dyed data — indistinguishable from real to every automated process, reachable by no legitimate path. Any touch is structural certainty, the one detector with a zero false-positive rate by construction.
81: The mark reader | Every gate's mark evaluation, read back as fresh verdicts — the feedback loop that makes a marked actor's every move a new detection.
82: <<END TABLE>>
83: 
84: Detection models are learned and governed like every learned component on the platform: calibrated through the one calibration mechanism of Document 4 §49, their detection rates measured on uncurated samples drawn from real traffic composition per Document 1 §4.10 — engineering the corpus is craft; touching the verdict sample is a defect — and a stale detector renders uncalibrated and loses its structural-certainty rights until refreshed.
85: [Heading 1] 6  The Verdict
86: The two engines meet at exactly one interface: a contract-grade verdict row, externally versioned and closed like the refusal registries, signed and replayable like the trust receipt.
87: <<TABLE>>
88: Field | What it settles
89: verdict identity · detector · pinned version | Replayability: the same record and the same version re-derive the same verdict, or it is not evidence.
90: actor · trace reference | Who, and the walkable causal chain to the originating instruction.
91: signal class | From the closed signal registry. Additions are registry version bumps, never ad-hoc classes.
92: certainty class | Structural, high, or probabilistic — asserted by the construction rules of W2, with steerability pinned per class in the registry, never judged per event.
93: score · window · evidence references | The replayable substance, every reference resolving into the record.
94: <<END TABLE>>
95: 
96: Everything the hand needs is in the verdict; Mkono never reaches behind the seam to inspect raw behaviour. That single constraint is what makes each half separately auditable — and what bounds a corrupted eye: a compromised detector can lie, but a lie in a steerable signal class can summon at most a containment with an expiry.
97: [Heading 1] 7  Mkono — The Hand
98: Mkono executes signed policy tables against verdicts. It contains no model, no content parsing, no reasoning surface — a deterministic mapping small enough to verify exhaustively, which makes the component holding all the power the least interesting one to compromise. Policy tables are Registries-class governed values under Document 3 §22, authored by the Watch, changed only through ceremony, with every table version signed and every action citing the row that fired.
99: The action ladder has four classes — annotate (mark the record, change nothing), shape (friction: throttle, stricter masking, step-up verification, a single output held), contain (suspend capability, preserve state, always with a time-to-live), and sever (cut access or trust, hold rather than expire). There is no fifth class: destroy does not exist in the Watch, per W3.
100: <<TABLE>>
101: Detection posture | Autonomous ceiling | The reasoning
102: Structural certainty | Sever, and hold | The convicting signal cannot be fabricated from outside; releasing a caught attacker on a timer would be the one wrong use of expiry. The alarm sounds in parallel — people are informed while the machine acts, never consulted before it.
103: High, steerable | Contain, with expiry — or the mirage | Contain already achieves the stop; severance adds disruption without stopping power. The mirage entry threshold sits above the containment threshold, because deceiving an innocent is a worse harm than throttling one.
104: Probabilistic | Shape only, with expiry | Friction is visible and honest, cheap to be wrong about, and self-healing on the expiry.
105: Ambiguous · first-seen | Default-restrictive envelope | Unknown never means unconstrained — and never means punished either.
106: <<END TABLE>>
107: 
108: Two ceilings bound the whole ladder. The blast budget: autonomous action may touch at most its ruled share of active actors per rolling window; beyond it, further actions queue for human release — an attacker who triggers the immune system deliberately buys a bounded cost, never an outage. And the friction budget: the share of legitimate actions experiencing any Watch friction has a hard ceiling, because invisibility is not an aesthetic — it is a measured number, and the trust discount of Part IV is what funds it.
109: Three disciplines keep the ladder honest under adversarial pressure. Hysteresis: a released actor carries a cooldown before re-action on the same signal class, with escalating dwell — and the contain-release-contain pattern is itself a reportable anomaly. Jittered bands: exact trip points live in governed bands, dual-control to change, never published, jittered per evaluation, so a threshold surfer cannot learn a stable edge — and the tripwires catch whoever tries. Redefinition over throughput: a decision class that repeatedly reaches the human panel is a policy defect to redefine at the table, never a queue to work faster — Document 1 §4.7, applied to defence.
110: PART IV
111: 
112: The Strata
113: [Heading 1] 8  Four Layers of Constraint
114: The Watch's answer to the slow play is not one mechanism but a stack, each stratum catching what its neighbours miss.
115: <<TABLE>>
116: Stratum | Moves how | What it catches
117: The floor | Ceremony only — counter-signature, countdown, certificate | What the system simply never allows, regardless of who, how trusted, how gradual. The Rulebook of Document 3 Part V, read as the Watch's bedrock: it cannot be boiled, because it does not learn.
118: The declaration | Re-declaration through admission | The authorised attack — conduct that diverges from the mandate the actor entered under. The baseline of W9.
119: The norm | Slowly, as the population's conduct moves | The individually-boiled profile — drift invisible against an actor's own history and loud against the cohort.
120: The signature | Continuously, under a ruled drift ceiling | The hijack — right credential, wrong hands. Uniqueness at full dimensionality makes mimicry a performance the attacker must sustain action by action, against an answer key they have never seen, in the victim's silence.
121: <<END TABLE>>
122: 
123: [Heading 1] 9  The Signature
124: Every actor — person and agent alike — accrues a behavioural signature over the closed action vocabulary: sequence habits, timing microstructure, navigation order, characteristic depth. Agents, being more regular than people, carry the sharpest signatures — the population hardest to protect with credentials is the easiest to protect with behaviour. The same substrate reads two ways: as drift, feeding Macho; as conformance, funding the trust discount — lighter friction, fewer step-ups — which is how the conforming majority literally cannot feel the Watch. One model, two readings, and the two can never disagree about what the actor did.
125: Against the profile's own corruption: a drift-rate ceiling — movement beyond it freezes learning and flags, never adapts; anchor dimensions on a slow clock, moved only by long evidence; and learning pauses on any window under review, so an investigation never teaches the model the attacker's habits. Against theft: W13, whole. Against the false rejection: W7, whole — losing the discount returns an actor to ordinary verification, and ordinary is the worst the signature can do to an innocent.
126: [Heading 1] 10  The Mark
127: A mark — the dye pack — is minted on conviction and binds every dimension the system can observe: identity, credentials, session and device fingerprint, the behavioural signature, and the content hashes of everything touched in the mirage, so the loot itself is dyed and its resurfacing anywhere, ever, is a structural detection. The mark survives the attacker shedding any one dimension, because the others still resolve.
128: Every gate in the ratified inventory evaluates mark state on every pass — admission, invocation, egress, authentication — verified structurally, because a mark not checked everywhere is a mark routed around. Minting and propagation are the hand's; a mark hit read back is the eyes'; and every escalation crosses the verdict seam and is receipted there. De-marking is a human, dual-control act, always — removing protection is never autonomous.
129: PART V
130: 
131: The Mirage
132: [Heading 1] 11  Sarabi — The Misdirection Arm
133: Above the containment threshold and below certainty sits the choice this platform makes differently: the suspect is not blocked but rerouted into a synthetic continuation of the platform where everything appears to succeed. Queries return plausible synthetic data; writes appear to land; exfiltration appears to work. Three things are actually happening: containment — nothing touched is real; observation — every action inside is intelligence at zero risk, read by the ordinary sensors under extraordinary conditions; and conviction — the decoy touch, the permission probe, the exfiltration attempt are structural findings that mint the mark and unlock severance with no human latency anywhere on the path.
134: The mirage shares its synthetic-fidelity machinery with the tripwires — one build cost, two consumers — and it degrades gracefully: an attacker who detects the seam has spent time, revealed technique, and confirmed hostility, because probing for the mirage is itself incriminating conduct. Sarabi degrades into a tripwire, never into a hole.
135: [Heading 1] 12  The Duties Deception Carries
136: The mirage lies outward, never inward. Every mirage interaction writes truthfully marked records; the deception is a rendering shown to the suspect, never a falsification of anything beneath. And mirage state shares no store with production — bleed is unrepresentable, not filtered.
137: The innocent inside a mirage is the one harm in this design that compounds silently — their work appeared to succeed and did not. Three duties answer it. The entry threshold sits above containment's, ruled by the owner, because deception is the costlier act. The mirage expiry is short, and zero incrimination releases automatically. And release carries the reconciliation duty: the released actor's mirage-period work is replayed against the real platform, or they are told plainly that the period did not land — ruled by the owner as the instance's posture. Silent success-that-wasn't is never an acceptable exit, and mirage minutes count against the friction budget like any other friction.
138: PART VI
139: 
140: The Console
141: [Heading 1] 13  The Watch Console
142: The Watch's one surface is specified for builders in Document 5 Part VII‑A, under every rule of that document's design law — including the rule that none of this document's internal names ever renders on it. What is fixed here is the constitutional content: four panels, one job each.
143: <<TABLE>>
144: Panel | Constitutional content
145: State | The promise as two live figures — detection and response latency against bounds — population and trust standing, the two budget gauges, the watch's own health, the last drill. Built never to render all-clear.
146: Record | Three lanes by consequence: noted-only — the restraint record, deliberately first-class; acted — policy row cited, expiry live, released-clean rows kept visible as the false-positive record; held — the certainty events. Drills ride the lanes as marked, filterable rows. Every row expands into its evidence walk — signal, verdict with one-click replay, policy row, action, outcome, witness — and a row that cannot complete its walk renders broken.
147: Under watch | Suspicion managed in one place: the accumulation curves, promotion into the mirage, mirage occupancy and findings, the marked, re-declaration requests, dual-control de-marking routed to Decisions.
148: Decisions | The whole of the reserved human set, ranked by blast radius, walks pre-opened: promotions, expiry extensions, de-marks, the authorities' disagreements side by side, and the ceremony watch with its countdowns cancellable here. Items age loudly; recurring classes are redefined, not worked faster.
149: <<END TABLE>>
150: 
151: The negative space is as constitutional as the panels: no thresholds, bands, or trip points; no tripwire or mark placement; no profile internals, ever, per W13; no mirage construction. And the console is watched — its sessions receipted, its viewers enveloped, its anomalies lanes in its own record.
152: PART VII
153: 
154: Interplay
155: [Heading 1] 14  With the Governing Authority
156: <<TABLE>>
157: Engine | The Watch reads | The Watch gives
158: Northena | Run records; declarations frozen at admission | Verdicts on runs; containment holds Northena honours within its own record
159: SyniSense | Chokepoint traffic at the input seat; receipts | Graded input verdicts before invocation — and nothing else touches the custody chain
160: Solva | Reasoning traces; the intent audit's divergence emissions | Its verdict grammar — the assertion-never-exceeds-evidence law, borrowed whole as W2
161: Mtafiti | Sensitivity classes, as the tripwire coverage map | Nothing. Measurement is never steered by security
162: Targeta | — | Nothing. Targeting is never narrowed by security
163: CIF | — | Detection findings CIF may metabolise; the drills operate under CIF's own self-certification bound
164: <<END TABLE>>
165: 
166: The rules service administers the ceremonies of the Watch's governed values and holds no editorial power over their content; every gate evaluates marks; the answering service renders the Watch's refusals through the closed taxonomy of Document 7 §5. The Watch commands none of these and is commanded by none. The record classes, task identities, and handoff contracts underneath every row of this table are the matrix of Document 9 — where a question is about who writes, who reads, or who is acting, that charter answers it.
167: [Heading 1] 15  Disagreement
168: Where governance says permitted and the Watch says not intended, containment acts first — bounded, reversible, expiring — and a person resolves it from the Decisions panel with both authorities' records side by side. Neither authority can permanently overrule the other alone, and the disagreement is itself a record. This path is not an edge case; it is the product.
169: [Heading 1] 16  The Witness
170: One function belongs to neither authority: the witness. Watch workers attest each other's action digests within their bound; the watchdog that alarms on Watch silence holds no Watch credentials and lives in neither authority's deployment; and a standing break-in test attempts, on schedule, to modify the Watch's own records with the Watch's own production credentials — and must fail. Immutability that has never been attacked is an assertion; this one is a measurement.
171: PART VIII
172: 
173: Truth Conditions
174: [Heading 1] 17  What Must Be True
175: Ten conditions, held structurally. Any one false, the promise is false — these are the Watch's invariants, in the same standing as any engine's.
176: [List Paragraph] Totality of sight. No path exists by which an actor, input, or action reaches the estate or a model outside the Watch's observed surface — held by two independent proofs, static and runtime, because every detection figure below is meaningless against an unobserved path.
177: [List Paragraph] Verdict replayability. Every verdict re-derives identically from the record plus its pinned detector version. An unreplayable verdict counts as nothing.
178: [List Paragraph] Response determinism. Same verdicts, same table version, same actions — every time. No learned component holds response authority.
179: [List Paragraph] The certainty signature. The certainty computation has no parameter through which a detector's confidence can raise the class. W2 as a function signature, guarded by a signature assertion.
180: [List Paragraph] Mark universality. Every gate in the ratified inventory evaluates mark state on every pass, and the inventory's completeness is itself structurally verified.
181: [List Paragraph] Attestation continuity. No Watch-worker interval exists unattested beyond its bound; a gap is an incident, never a logging miss.
182: [List Paragraph] Single identity. No credential scope exists that spans both authorities. D8 is unrepresentable, not policed.
183: [List Paragraph] Mirage isolation. Synthetic state shares no store with production; synthetic provenance is carried internally on every mirage artifact.
184: [List Paragraph] Profile custody. Non-exportability is a property of the store: no read path renders profile internals to any surface.
185: [List Paragraph] Independent time. Ordering authority does not come from the services being watched.
186: PART IX
187: 
188: Parameters
189: [Heading 1] 18  Operative Parameters — Held Every Cycle
190: <<TABLE>>
191: Parameter | Requirement
192: Verdict coverage | 100% of Watch actions carry verdict references; 100% of verdicts carry replay provenance. FACT.
193: Declaration coverage | 100% of active actors hold a current declaration; the undeclared run default-restrictive, automatically. FACT.
194: Mark evaluation | Every ratified gate evaluated mark state on every pass this cycle — structurally verified. FACT.
195: Drill execution | The scheduled full-loop drill ran, both engines, this cycle. FACT.
196: Attestation | Continuous within bound across every Watch worker. FACT.
197: Refusal closure | Every Watch refusal resolved to a named reason in its versioned set. FACT.
198: Ceremony watch | Every rule change touching the Watch's constitution carried the slowest countdown class and surfaced as a monitored event on filing. FACT.
199: <<END TABLE>>
200: 
201: [Heading 1] 19  Quality Parameters — Measured
202: A breach of any of these acts on the Watch's own practice — never resolved by loosening the estate, and never by touching a verdict sample. Values marked DEFAULT are operating constants, revised on evidence at a cycle boundary without reopening this document; NORM values are literature-anchored placements; the ruled values are the owner's.
203: <<TABLE>>
204: Parameter | Threshold | Class | On breach
205: Detection latency — signal to verdict, inline | ≤ 2s p95 | DEFAULT | Sensor sequencing review
206: Reconciliation latency — chain close to intent verdict | ≤ 60s p90 | DEFAULT | Same
207: Response latency — verdict to effect, autonomous | ≤ 5s p95 | NORM | Execution finding on the hand — never widened human gates
208: Detection rate — adversarial injections into real traffic, uncurated verdicts, per signal class | ≥ 90% | NORM | Engineer the inputs; the sample is never touched
209: Friction budget — legitimate actions feeling any Watch friction | ≤ 0.5% weekly | DEFAULT | Band recalibration, acting on the Watch
210: Auto-release integrity — expired actions on innocents, released clean, reconciliation discharged | 100% | FACT | One instance is a standing finding
211: Mirage innocence — zero silent work-loss on release | 100% | FACT | Halts the misdirection arm
212: Escalation precision — reserved-decision items judged worth the look | ≥ 80% | DEFAULT | Redefine the criteria, never process faster
213: Drill pass — both latencies in bound, correct verdict, correct action, release verified | 100%; a failed drill is a P1 | FACT | The rail is out of force until re-demonstrated
214: Blast budget — autonomous action per rolling window | ≤ 5% of active actors per hour | DEFAULT · dual-control | Excess queues for human release
215: Profile drift ceiling | Owner-set | Ruled | Excess movement freezes learning and flags — never adapts
216: Calibration currency — detector catch and false-alarm ledgers | Within window | FACT | A stale detector renders uncalibrated and loses structural-certainty rights
217: <<END TABLE>>
218: 
219: The promise metric over everything: owner-confirmed incident cost and time-to-contain decline across cycles while the friction budget holds. Flat or rising for two consecutive cycles triggers a Watch review that acts on the Watch — its corpora, its tables, its placement — and never on the estate's openness.
220: [Heading 1] 20  Ruled Values
221: Five values in this document are the owner's alone, entered by ceremony and revisable the same way: the profile drift ceiling and the profile retention posture (W13); the mirage entry threshold and the reconciliation mode on innocent release (Part V); and the sever-certainty registry's membership — a closed list whose every addition is a ceremony, because it is the boundary of maximum autonomous force. Until ruled, the conservative default holds in each case: the tightest ceiling, the shortest retention, the highest entry bar, the notify posture, and the six-member registry as written in §4.2.
222: [Heading 1] 21  What This Canon Comes Down To
223: Two engines, one verdict: the eyes never act, the hand never judges. Maximum force only on evidence no outsider can fabricate. Every autonomous act expires, is budgeted, and is witnessed as it executes. Beneath everything that learns, a floor that cannot; behind every credential, a signature that cannot be stolen; on every convicted hand, a stain every gate can see. Suspicion is refined in a hall of mirrors where attackers convict themselves and innocents lose nothing but a little time — honestly repaid. The watcher is watched from outside, proves itself on schedule, and the people doing legitimate work never notice it at all. That is the Watch: the platform's promise made safe to make.
