# SOURCE: assessment_workspace/canon/text/Akki_OS_Audio_Intelligence_Plane_Specification_v1_0.txt
Coordinate: source line

1: SYNI.AI   ·   ENGINEERING SPECIFICATION
2: The Audio Intelligence Plane
3: Extraction · Learning · Training · Invention — end to end
4: Including the Commission View surface adjustment across all extraction types · v1.0
5: Status of this document: consolidated build specification. It supersedes the working drafts (Audio Capability Spec v1.0 and Addendum v1.1.2) and is the single reference for build. Behavioural clauses state what the system must and must not do, including on failure. Technical clauses state contracts and acceptance criteria. Items requiring verification against current code before build are marked [VERIFY] and collected in §16.
6: Contents
7: 
8: 1  Governing Doctrine
9: Five principles govern every clause in this specification. Where a later clause appears to conflict with one of these, the principle wins and the clause is defective.
10: 1.1  An audio file is a data estate, and the framing is recursive
11: The archive is an estate; a programme is an estate; a single file is an estate. Segments are rows; the extractable layers — content, language, condition, prosody, occurrence, code-switch, music, group-level character — are columns; no schema exists until one is declared. Census, admission, registry, and record apply at every scale.
12: 1.2  Modality extension, not parallel machinery
13: The audio plane introduces no sibling services. Mtafiti gains an audio modality; Northena gains audio data classes; the wizard gains an objective variant; Targeta gains a training object. Anything in this document that reads as a parallel to an existing service is rule proliferation and must be collapsed into the existing service before build.
14: 1.3  One record
15: Mtafiti and Northena collaborate to produce a single record, written once. Working state — loss curves, intermediate metrics, partial coverage counts — is scratch, not truth; it becomes record only when finalized and stamped. No local ledger exists. If a measured throughput ceiling ever demands relief, the relief is batched stamping (one row certifying N events with a digest), which remains a single record. That change is made only when a measurement demands it.
16: 1.4  Measure, do not assert
17: No data-volume requirement, accuracy expectation, or cost figure is quoted without a measurement behind it. The calibration stage exists to convert assertions into measurements before commitment.
18: 1.5  Unrepresentable, not policed
19: Safety boundaries are enforced by making the violating state impossible to express in the contract — the pattern established by the assertion floor — not by review after the fact. The Character Register write path (§6) and the voice identity distance gate (§7) both follow this pattern.
20: 2  Capability Statement and Plane Overview
21: Given governed access to an audio estate, the plane provides four functions in one loop:
22: Extraction — audio is converted into provenance-paired facts: transcripts, entities, occurrences, and character observations.
23: Learning — a Character Register accumulates group-level knowledge of how the estate’s languages and audio behave.
24: Training — model production is commissioned against a falsifiable Target Outcome, planned and priced before compute is spent, with per-example provenance.
25: Invention — synthesized voice identities are constructed from the register: authentically of the language, provably of no individual.
26: 
27: Each function feeds the next: extraction populates the register; the register defines the strata training plans against; trained models improve extraction; invention consumes the register’s learned layers. The loop is the capability.
28: Flow of a commission, end to end:
29: Objective Wizard session → compile {TargetOutcome, Collection Schema}
30: → Sampling & Reflection (calibration) → proposed Milestones + priced quote
31: → Owner agrees milestones → Commission opens
32: → Collection → Register update → Curriculum → Training runs → Certificates
33: → Commission View reports against milestones throughout → Commission sealed
34: 3  Tokenized Audio Representation
35: 3.1  Behaviour
36: All downstream audio work — extraction, character analysis, training — operates on discrete token sequences produced by a neural audio codec, not on waveforms.
37: Tokenization exposes two separable streams per segment: the content stream (what was said — input to ASR/NER) and the character stream (how it was said — input to the Character Register). The character stream is retained and routed, never discarded as noise.
38: Control markers (language, register, segment type) are splice-able tokens, enabling one model per estate rather than one per language, and native handling of code-switched speech.
39: Failure behaviour: audio in an unsupported condition fails closed with a stated reason. The codec never silently degrades quality.
40: 3.2  Technical contract
41: 
42: 3.3  Acceptance criteria
43: Round-trip fidelity is measured and recorded per codec version before that version serves any commission.
44: A downstream artifact lacking codec_version in provenance is rejected at the registry boundary.
45: An unsupported-condition input produces a refusal with a stated reason and no output artifact.
46: 4  Extraction Layer
47: 4.1  Language identification
48: Behaviour: every segment carries a real language signal. The current plumbing value (language_hint: None) is retired.
49: A lightweight offline language identifier (CPU-viable, in-perimeter) runs at segment level during ingestion.
50: Recorded per segment: languages[], confidences, and code-switch points where multiple languages occur in one utterance.
51: The signal routes downstream model selection (ASR path, NER path, de-identification path) and is written into provenance.
52: [VERIFY] Segment boundaries in current ingestion — confirm the unit to which a language label attaches.
53: 4.2  Code-switch points as facts
54: Switch points (position, from-language, to-language, context class) are registered facts with provenance — not preprocessing metadata. They populate the register’s code-switch layer and stratify test sets.
55: 4.3  Condition profiling
56: Channel condition — studio / field / telephone band, transmission artefacts, background class — is derived per segment at first ingestion. It is cheap to compute, directly predictive of extraction error, and required for training stratification. It is captured at first ingestion because re-ingesting an estate to recover it is the unaffordable mistake.
57: 4.4  Synthesis-relevant attribute capture
58: During the same ingestion pass, group-level acoustic attributes required by any future synthesis capability (pitch statistics, energy contours, duration patterns) are captured, subject to the custody conditions of §6.4. This forecloses nothing and costs little; omitting it forecloses the invention function or forces re-ingestion.
59: 4.5  Deduplication as augmentation
60: The occurrence index already identifies repeated content. Its output contract is extended: for each deduplicated item, the instance condition map — the set of channel/time/condition variants under which identical content occurred — is retained. One canonical extraction is stored; the variant set enters training curricula as a designated robustness stratum at zero acquisition cost. No new detection work; this is a change to what dedup keeps.
61: 4.6  Acceptance criteria
62: No segment leaves ingestion without languages[], condition profile, and (where applicable) switch points in provenance.
63: A deduplicated item without its instance condition map fails the ingestion invariant test.
64: Baseline-tier capture (§9.2) runs for all admitted material regardless of any active objective.
65: 5  The Character Register — Learning
66: 5.1  Definition
67: A registry-modality store of learned, group-level audio characteristics, built from the character stream. Same doctrine as the fact registry: every entry carries provenance to source material and an occurrence count. It is Mtafiti’s qualification-and-index doctrine applied to acoustic observations — an extension, not a sibling (§1.2).
68: 5.2  Layers
69: 
70: 5.3  Build process
71: Unsupervised clustering over the character stream yields candidate strata. A cluster asserts that a distinct variant exists — not what it is called. Naming and validation are human work applied to a sample, commissioned like any other qualified work with quoted cost.
72: 6  Register Custody Boundary
73: 6.1  Governing distinction: organic versus learned
74: Organic characteristics are anatomical — vocal tract length, formant structure, glottal source, fundamental frequency range. They cannot be acquired or shed; they are what speaker verification keys on; they are biometric. They are never registered.
75: Learned characteristics are acquired from a speech community — phonological inventory, pronunciation variants, prosody, code-switching habits. They are group properties by construction. Only learned characteristics may be registered.
76: 6.2  The four conditions — all must hold
77: Acquired, not anatomical. The attribute is learnable by a speaker from a different background.
78: Shared. Observed across at least N distinct speakers. N is a governed seam value; its default inherits the platform minimum-group-size parameter unless the tenant sets a register-specific value.
79: Non-reconstructive in combination. Tested against attribute combinations, not attributes in isolation: language + region + age band + one distinctive feature can reach a single person even when each attribute is group-level.
80: Stored as description, not exemplar. Centroids, distributions, frequencies. Never stored audio; never per-utterance speaker embeddings. Embeddings used during clustering are destroyed after cluster assignment. Provenance points to material, not to speaker identity.
81: 6.3  Enforcement shape
82: The register write path exposes no field through which an instance-level representation can be stored: the schema cannot represent a voiceprint. Unrepresentable, not policed (§1.5). An automated invariant test attempts each known leakage path (small stratum, idiolect marker, narrowing combination, exemplar storage) and must fail to store all of them on every change to the register code.
83: 6.4  Idiolect rule
84: Habitual fillers, characteristic phrasings, and idiosyncratically pronounced words are learned but individuating. They fail condition 2 or 3 and are excluded. “Learned” alone is never sufficient; the four conditions are conjunctive.
85: 7  Synthesized Voice Identity — Invention
86: 7.1  Mechanism: inherit the learned, synthesize the organic
87: Learned characteristics are inherited from the register — this is what makes the voice sound like a speaker of the language rather than a foreigner reading it.
88: Organic characteristics are constructed — vocal tract parameters, F0 range, formant structure, glottal parameters are chosen as a point in acoustic space that no real speaker occupies.
89: This is the inverse of a voice clone. A clone copies the organic and frequently gets the learned wrong; this gets the learned right and owns the organic outright.
90: 7.2  The distance guarantee (mandatory, fail-closed)
91: Every constructed identity is scored against every speaker representation derivable from the corpus using standard speaker-verification methods. A minimum distance from all of them is required. Below threshold, the identity is rejected and resampled. There is no override. The threshold value and the verification method are recorded with the identity.
92: 7.3  The certificate
93: A passing identity is issued a certificate stating that the voice is provably derived from no individual, naming the method, the threshold, and the corpus version scored against. The certificate is a first-class sellable artifact.
94: 7.4  Identity composition and versioning
95: 
96: Each identity is a versioned artifact with a ledger entry. Changing one is a ceremony with the standard waiting period, because audience recognition accrues to the voice and recognition is the asset. Identities never drift.
97: 7.5  Scope note
98: Rendering requires a synthesis stack, which is a separate build from recognition. What this specification requires now is non-foreclosure: the identity specification (attribute schema, distance method, certificate format) is defined, and §4.4’s ingestion capture ensures the substrate exists when rendering is built.
99: 8  The Objective Wizard — Schema Compiler
100: 8.1  Role
101: No business user hand-writes a Target Outcome. The Objective Wizard — a new variant of the existing shaping wizard, reusing its agent interface, guards, session persistence, and ledger sidecar — elicits an objective in plain language and compiles two governed artifacts:
102: TargetOutcome (§10) — handed to the Training Planner.
103: Collection Schema (§9) — the data dictionary for this objective: which data points are extracted from the sound, at what granularity, at what quality bar.
104: 8.2  Elicitation sequence
105: The question the model must answer — operational and falsifiable.
106: The population — resolved against existing register strata; unresolved populations are flagged as unmeasured and generate census work.
107: The acceptance bar — per stratum, two-dimensional (§10), with the gate-or-document decision recorded explicitly.
108: The collection consequences — the wizard derives required columns, shows which are already collected (baseline tier), which exist but are uncollected, and the cost of collecting them. The owner sees the price of the schema before commissioning.
109: 8.3  Dynamism within scope: propose, qualify, graduate
110: Propose. The agent side may propose novel data points no prior objective collected. This is where innovation enters.
111: Qualify. A proposed column never enters collection directly. It is admitted as a candidate: collected on a sample only, its evidence of value measured against the objective — the same qualification path any fact travels.
112: Graduate. Qualified candidates graduate into the objective tier for that commission. Graduation into the baseline tier is ceremony-governed (proposal, countersignature, waiting period), because a baseline column is paid on every hour ingested for the life of the estate.
113: The compile stage is deterministic throughout: the agent proposes; only qualified columns compile. Mechanical guards prove against a stub agent before any LLM is plugged in, per the existing standing disposition.
114: 8.4  Compile-time rejections
115: The wizard cannot emit an artifact the downstream contracts would refuse. Rejected at compile, not warned:
116: An Outcome without an existing test_set_ref.
117: An acceptance bar missing the per-stratum dimension.
118: A Collection Schema requiring a column whose capture violates the custody conditions of §6.2.
119: 8.5  Record and handoff
120: Every session stamps to the ledger via the existing turn-ledger pattern under a distinct data class (objective_session), including options considered and rejected — which is what makes a later “why was the model built this way” answerable. Compiled artifacts hand off to Targeta through the existing admission-handoff pattern. Objective → schema → plan → run is one provenance chain.
121: [VERIFY] The B-2/B-3 landing state of the current wizard, before choosing between extending the existing state machine with an objective variant or standing up a sibling machine sharing the agent interface and ledger sidecar.
122: 9  The Collection Schema
123: 9.1  Definition
124: The declared data dictionary of a commission: what is extracted from the sound, for what purpose, at what quality bar. It is the admission standard of the audio estate, per objective (§1.1). It has two tiers.
125: 9.2  Baseline tier
126: Standing, objective-independent, collected at first ingestion for all admitted material. Membership criterion: cheap to collect now, unaffordable to collect later. Contents at v1.0: language identification, code-switch points, condition profile, dedup instance condition map, synthesis-relevant group-level acoustics (§4). Changes to the baseline are seam-governed — ceremony, countersignature, waiting period — because silently narrowing the baseline is how an estate quietly becomes unre-readable.
127: 9.3  Objective tier
128: Declared per commission by the Objective Wizard. Collected against material already in governed scope, priced before collection starts, recorded in the commission’s registry namespace. Candidate columns enter through propose–qualify–graduate (§8.3) only.
129: 10  The Target Outcome
130: 10.1  Schema
131: TargetOutcome {
132:   task          operational statement of what the model must do
133:   domain        context of use
134:   population    defined by reference to register strata, not labels
135:   acceptance    threshold per stratum; two-dimensional (accuracy, coverage)
136:   gate_policy   per Outcome: missed stratum gates release | ships documented
137:   test_set_ref  must exist before the Outcome is accepted
138:   constraints   latency, compute budget, deployment target
139: }
140: 
141: 10.2  Binding rules
142: Population is register-defined. “Language L, accent clusters 1–4, telephone band and studio, adult” — never “speakers of L.” This is what makes coverage computable.
143: Acceptance is per stratum. A single global threshold hides the failure that matters: 94% on the majority variant and 61% on the rest passes one test and fails the one that decides whether the work reaches the people it was built for.
144: The test set precedes the training. An Outcome without an existing, stratified test set is rejected at definition time.
145: The gate decision is recorded on the Outcome at definition — not decided ad hoc at ship time.
146: 11  The Training Planner
147: 11.1  Architecture
148: The existing planner pattern is reused unchanged: a deterministic core computes eligibility; a learned layer may only reorder an already-eligible set it receives stripped of the values that decided eligibility; a gate compares learned output against the deterministic baseline; every plan is reproducible from its recorded inputs.
149: 
150: 11.2  Sampling & Reflection (calibration) — mandatory first stage
151: Data requirements for low-resource fine-tuning are empirical; no analytical answer exists. The first commissioned stage is therefore a calibration: train at three to four data volumes, evaluate per stratum against the test set, fit the scaling curve, extrapolate to the acceptance threshold. Only then is the full run quoted, with a stated confidence interval — never a point estimate. A plan without a calibration stage is rejected. The first job prices the real job.
152: 11.3  Milestones — the accountability output
153: Sampling & Reflection has two customers. It prices the real job, and it authors the accountability structure: its output to the objective owner is not a curve but a proposed milestone list — the checklist of what must be done, in what order, for the commission to succeed. Each milestone carries a done-condition and an owner. The objective owner reviews and agrees the list at commission; from that point, all reporting is against it. Accountability is set before spend, not discovered during.
154: 11.4  Planner outputs
155: Coverage report — per target stratum: hours available, quality distribution, gaps, cost of closing each gap.
156: Curriculum — ordering and weighting across strata derived from the register, not from the corpus’s natural distribution, which is always skewed toward whatever occurred most. The dedup instance condition map enters as a designated robustness stratum.
157: Proposed milestone list (§11.3).
158: Cost quote with a stated confidence interval.
159: 11.5  Provenance through training
160: Every training example carries its provenance into the training manifest. Consequences: rights are enforceable per example; an example whose rights lapse is identifiable and the affected models enumerable; and “the trained model is the customer’s property” is a statement backed by a manifest, not an assertion.
161: 11.6  Run governance
162: Training runs are commissioned jobs under the existing contract: quoted before start, metered during, certificated on completion. The completion certificate records compute consumed, data touched, manifest hash, and per-stratum results against the Outcome. Failed strata are reported as plainly as passed ones.
163: 12  Record and Registry Integration
164: 12.1  Registry (Mtafiti audio modality)
165: Per commission, a scoped namespace within the registry holds: the Collection Schema (versioned), collected data points mapped against it — with declared-but-not-yet-collected as first-class state — the strata referenced by the Outcome, and coverage state per stratum. Reads compose with the global registry; writes are namespace-scoped. On close, the namespace is sealed, not deleted: it is the record of what was collected and why, and the next objective’s wizard session queries prior schemas and coverage so the second project starts from the first project’s map.
166: 12.2  Record (Northena data classes)
167: Training-workflow operations stamp into the one ledger under training-specific data classes: collection events, calibration runs, curriculum decisions, milestone status changes, run certificates. The workflow’s view of “its” record is a scoped lens filterable by commission ID — a view, not a store. Working state (loss curves, intermediate metrics, partial counts) is scratch until finalized and stamped once (§1.3).
168: 13  Surface Specification — the Commission View
169: 13.1  Scope
170: This surface adjustment applies to all commissioned work on the platform — extraction, census, and training commissions alike, across every extraction type. No modality receives its own UI, and no surface is a rendering of backend internals: rendering internals quietly commits the backend to building displayable versions of its own machinery.
171: 13.2  Behaviour
172: The surface is milestones. The artifacts are evidence behind them.
173: At Sampling & Reflection, the proposed milestone list is presented to the objective owner for agreement. Commission does not open until it is agreed.
174: The Commission View reports against the agreed checklist: each milestone with its done-condition and owner; status in plain terms — done, on track, behind, missed. Missed is shown as plainly as done.
175: Spend against quote is shown at the same plain level.
176: Technical material — calibration results, strata coverage, Collection Schema state — is drill-down evidence for whoever asks why a milestone reads as it does. It is never the front page.
177: 13.3  Modality leaf
178: Modality appears at exactly one leaf: evidence inspection. Where provenance resolves to a recording, the source plays at its timestamp rather than rendering as a page region — the existing trust-receipt pattern (“a disputed number is answered by playing the tape”), unchanged.
179: 13.4  Backend cost constraint
180: Milestones are records with done-conditions; the platform already stamps events. No new machinery is built for display. Any surface element in this section found to require new backend computation beyond reading existing artifacts is out of specification and must be removed or re-specified.
181: 14  Interface Summary
182: 15  Build Sequence
183: Ordered by dependency and cost-of-deferral, not by size.
184: 16  Verification Register and Open Decisions
185: 16.1  Items to verify against current code before build
186: Perception router contract — model registration point; whether a second output stream per segment is carried or the character stream needs its own artifact type (§3.2).
187: Ingestion segment boundaries — the unit a language label attaches to (§4.1).
188: Wizard B-2/B-3 landing state — extend the existing state machine with an objective variant, or stand a sibling machine on the shared agent interface and ledger sidecar (§8.5).
189: 16.2  Open decisions (owner: product)
190: N for the shared-attribute condition (§6.2.2): inherit the platform minimum-group-size seam value, or set a register-specific one.
191: Platform default for gate_policy (§10.1) where an Outcome does not set it: missed stratum gates release, or ships documented. This default silently decides how minority-variant quality is treated under schedule pressure.
192: Cluster naming validation: commissioned internally or delegated to an external evaluation partner where one exists (§5.3).
193: Codec choice: adopt an existing open codec versus training estate-specific — a trade the Sampling & Reflection machinery can itself answer once built (§3, §11.2).
194: Baseline tier contents (§9.2): the v1.0 set is the proposal; every addition is paid on every hour ingested, every omission is paid at re-ingestion.
195: 
196: End of specification. This document is the single build reference for the Audio Intelligence Plane; the working drafts it consolidates are retired.

1: SYNI.AI   ·   MODULE BRIEFING
2: Incremental Training & Capacity
3: A module for objective-driven model training, designed on the Theory of Constructive Operators
4: This document defines the module: the problem it solves, the theory it draws on, the concepts it introduces, the components that implement it, the surfaces it touches, and how it is built and validated. It is a platform module — modality-independent. Audio is its first consumer, not its container.
5: Contents
6: 1   The problem this module solves	2
7: 2   The theory, and the discipline around it	2
8: 3   Concepts and definitions	3
9: 4   Components	4
10: 5   Design rationale — why this shape	6
11: 6   Surfaces and handoffs	7
12: 7   Build order	8
13: 8   Validation gate	8
14: 9   Open decisions	9
15: 
16: 1  The problem this module solves
17: The platform trains models against specific customer objectives, on customer estates, as commissioned work. Four problems arise in that setting, and they compound.
18: 1.1  Every objective starts from nothing
19: A commission trains a model for an objective. A later commission on the same estate trains for a related objective and begins again — no record exists of what the first model demonstrably learned, at what level, on which material. Capability is produced and then lost as an asset. The second commission costs what the first cost, indefinitely.
20: 1.2  Nobody knows what an objective actually demands
21: An objective arrives as a description of a desired outcome. Nothing converts it into a statement of what the model must be able to do — how many distinct capabilities must be correct at the same moment for a single output to be right. Without that, planning is guesswork: the work is scoped by intuition, priced by analogy, and the first real evidence of difficulty arrives after the compute is spent.
22: 1.3  Gaps are discovered, not predicted
23: Trained models fail unevenly. They perform on the material the corpus is rich in and fail on the variants it is thin in — minority dialects, degraded channels, code-switched speech, unusual document conditions. Today those gaps surface at evaluation, after training. Nothing in the process identifies, before training begins, which strata are at risk and why.
24: 1.4  The corpus’s own skew steers the model
25: Left to its natural distribution, training follows whatever the estate holds most of. That is not neutral: it actively pulls the model toward the dominant variant and away from the ones that most need deliberate attention. The skew is invisible in the training configuration and visible only in the results.
26: 
27: The module addresses all four with one mechanism: state what an objective demands, measure what the trainer already holds, plan from the difference, and record what each commission adds.
28: 2  The theory, and the discipline around it
29: 2.1  What the Theory of Constructive Operators says
30: Juan Pascual-Leone’s Theory of Constructive Operators explains why children move between cognitive stages. Piaget described the stages; TCO supplies the mechanism. A child can perform a task when their mental attentional capacity — how many mental schemes they can hold and coordinate at once — meets the number of schemes the task requires coordinated simultaneously. Capacity grows with development; when it crosses a task’s demand, the task becomes solvable.
31: The theory also describes forces acting on that capacity: a field pull toward whatever is perceptually dominant, and silent operators that boost relevant schemes and suppress interfering ones. It distinguishes facilitating situations, where the obvious response is the correct one, from misleading situations, where capacity must be spent inhibiting a wrong but dominant response.
32: 2.2  What transfers to model training
33: The structural correspondence is close enough to be useful without being forced:
34: 2.3  The discipline: shape, not numbers
35: What the module borrows is the shape — measure capacity, compute demand, stage transitions by the gap, reuse what is held, guard against interference. What it does not borrow is any quantity. TCO’s growth rates and capacity units are empirical claims about children; they say nothing about transformers on a broadcast archive.
36: Every rate, step and threshold in this module is measured per commission. Nothing is assumed from the theory, and the module’s central claim — that demand-staged training produces fewer gaps than flat training — is held unpublished until it is measured (§8).
37: 3  Concepts and definitions
38: Seven terms carry the module. They are used with these meanings throughout the platform.
39: 3.1  Scheme
40: A discrete, named, reusable capability a model either holds or does not — for example, entity recognition in a given language, transcription under telephone-band conditions, table extraction from degraded scans, clause identification in commercial contracts. Schemes are modality-independent and drawn from a shared taxonomy so that a scheme name means the same thing across commissions.
41: 3.2  Stratum
42: A defined slice of material with distinct characteristics — a language variant, a channel condition, a document class, an accent cluster. Strata come from the platform’s registry work: they are what the estate is actually made of, measured rather than assumed. Demand, capacity and acceptance are all expressed per stratum, because that is where performance genuinely differs.
43: 3.3  Coordination breadth (B)
44: For a required output, the number of schemes that must be simultaneously correct for that output to be correct. B is the maximum co-activation across the objective’s outputs — not a total inventory of everything the objective touches somewhere.
45: Worked example. For the output “brand X was mentioned by presenter Y at time T”, three schemes must all be right at once: transcription in the segment’s language, brand entity recognition, and speaker attribution. B = 3. On code-switched segments, switch handling must also be right at the same moment: B = 4. The same objective therefore makes different demands of different strata, which is precisely what the table is for.
46: 3.4  Interference (I)
47: A per-stratum flag marking strata where the corpus’s natural pull opposes the required behaviour — majority-variant gravity over a minority variant, cross-language model pull on non-English text, frequency pull from heavily repeated material. In TCO terms these are misleading situations: capacity must be spent suppressing a dominant wrong response, so interference adds to demand rather than sitting beside it.
48: I is binary at introduction. It is re-weighted only if calibration data shows misleading strata cost more than one unit of capacity — measured, never assumed.
49: 3.5  Effective demand (E)
50: E = B + I, per stratum. Effective demand is a fact about the objective: model-independent, portable across model lines, computed once at compile and never revised downstream.
51: 3.6  Capacity (C)
52: What a model line demonstrably holds, per scheme, at a measured level — established by probing during calibration, not inferred from training history. Capacity is a fact about the trainer on a particular estate, and it changes as commissions complete.
53: 3.7  Gap, step, and saturation
54: Gap = E − C per stratum. It is what the plan must close, and the planner’s first computation.
55: Step = how much new coordination the model absorbs in one stage while retaining what it already holds. Measured at calibration on this estate; never a constant.
56: Saturation = the state of a capability whose measured level stops moving as data is added. Derived from marginal-gain records, never declared.
57: 4  Components
58: Four components implement the module. Each attaches to a surface that already exists; none is a new service.
59: 4.1  The Demand Table
60: Compiled by the Objective Wizard alongside the TargetOutcome and Collection Schema, for every objective. It states what the objective requires, per stratum.
61: DemandTable {
62:   schemes[]      each: { id, named_failure }
63:   per_stratum {
64:     B            coordination breadth — max simultaneous co-activation
65:     I            interference flag — corpus pull opposes required behaviour
66:     E = B + I    effective demand
67:   }
68: }
69: 
70: The admissibility rule
71: A scheme enters the table only with its named failure — the concrete thing that breaks without it. “Code-switch handling, because entity boundaries break at switch points” is admissible. “Robustness” is not. The compile stage rejects unnamed-failure schemes as it rejects an objective with no test set.
72: This rule exists for one reason: it keeps the table a surgical map of what the objective actually needs, rather than an inventory that grows to look thorough. A demand count that cannot be audited to named failures is a busyness score, and would corrupt every plan built on it.
73: 4.2  The Capacity Ledger
74: A modality within the existing registry service — not a new store. It records what has been built, so the next commission does not begin from nothing.
75: CapacityEntry {
76:   scheme_id
77:   stratum        per-stratum where flagged; ‘global’ otherwise
78:   level          measured, from calibration
79:   provenance[]   which commission(s) built it
80:   marginal_gain  what the last data increment moved
81:   state          building | held | saturated   (derived)
82: }
83: 
84: Resolution rule
85: Per-stratum entries for schemes touched by strata flagged I = 1, plus any stratum the objective’s acceptance gates on. Global entries elsewhere. Precision where risk lives, economy everywhere else: the ledger can afford completeness, but the calibration probe suite must stay selective or it becomes the expensive part of every commission.
86: 4.3  The capacity probe
87: An addition to Sampling & Reflection — the calibration stage that already precedes every commissioned training run. It gains one function and changes nothing else:
88: Read the ledger for the schemes named in the Demand Table.
89: Probe only what the resolution rule requires: which schemes are held, at what level, per flagged stratum.
90: Measure the step — how much new coordination the model absorbs while retaining prior capability.
91: Write marginal-gain rows back to the ledger.
92: Calibration continues to do what it already did: price the job and author the proposed milestone list. It now also answers what the trainer already knows.
93: 4.4  Gap-shaped staged plans
94: The Training Planner’s first computation becomes the gap, and the plan takes its shape from it:
95: Small gap — compose the schemes already held; train only the residual.
96: Large gap — a staged curriculum: stages ordered by ascending effective demand, facilitating strata before misleading ones, each stage introducing no more new coordination than the measured step.
97: Stage gate — each stage must retain prior capability, checked against earlier stage test sets, before the next opens. This is the suppression half of the mechanism: growth that destroys what came before is not growth.
98: Near-saturated schemes — shift the quote from training spend to composition work, before the quote is issued.
99: 5  Design rationale — why this shape
100: 5.1  Demand travels with the objective; capacity stays with the trainer
101: Demand is analytic and model-independent: the same objective makes the same demand of any model that attempts it, so it is computed once at compile and travels with the objective. Capacity and growth rate are empirical and specific: they belong to a model line on an estate, and are measured at calibration.
102: Mixing them would make objectives non-portable and put invented constants into the compile stage — the exact failure the analogy discipline (§2.3) exists to prevent.
103: 5.2  Per-stratum resolution, selectively probed
104: Global capability figures hide the failures that matter: a model at a high average can be failing the minority stratum entirely. Per-stratum resolution is where the module earns its value. But probing every scheme on every stratum would make calibration the dominant cost of a commission, so resolution is full in the ledger and selective in the probe.
105: 5.3  Provenance ships on day one
106: Every capacity write records which commission built it. Nothing in the module requires this today. It is included now because a ledger without provenance cannot later answer whose data built a capability — and that question must be answerable before any capability is ever shared across commissions or tenants, given that trained models are the customer’s property.
107: It is the one field that cannot be retrofitted: adding it later means rebuilding the ledger from source.
108: 5.4  Saturation is a discount, not a checkpoint
109: As incremental modelling matures, later commissions increasingly find their demand already met and additional data stops moving measured capability. The module makes that visible without making it a burden:
110: Derived, never declared. Computed from marginal-gain rows calibration already writes. No one enters it; no one maintains it.
111: Informational, never gating. Nothing blocks on saturation. No ceremony to enter or exit the state. No user action is ever required by it.
112: Acts only in the customer’s favour. Its single effect is the quote shift in §4.4 — cheaper composition instead of futile training.
113: Shared-learning policy — cross-commission transfer, common substrates, tenant boundaries — is deliberately deferred until marginal-gain data exists to inform it. The schema above is sufficient preparation; deciding the policy now would be assertion where measurement is pending.
114: 6  Surfaces and handoffs
115: The module touches six surfaces and introduces no new one. It adds no human approval anywhere: the only decisions in the journey remain the two that already exist — the objective owner agrees milestones at commission, and decides on a budget-ceiling breach.
116: 
117: 6.1  Handoff chain
118: Each step produces a typed artifact with a single owner. The consumer is prohibited from redoing what the producer guaranteed — redoing upstream work is a specification violation, not diligence.
119: 
120: Ownership check: demand is computed only at compile; capacity only at probe; the plan only at plan; approval only at commission; capability writes only during training. No surface owns the same value twice.
121: 7  Build order
122: Six items. Order is by dependency, and by what becomes expensive if deferred.
123: 
124: Items 1 and 2 carry the deferral cost. Taxonomy instability makes every later scheme name ambiguous, and a ledger without provenance must be rebuilt from source rather than amended.
125: 8  Validation gate
126: The module makes one mechanism claim: that demand-staged training produces better coverage — particularly on misleading strata — than training on the corpus’s natural distribution or on a flat curriculum. That claim is held until it is measured.
127: 8.1  The experiment
128: Three arms, equal budget, scored per stratum under the platform’s blind dual-judge protocol:
129: Baseline: training on the corpus’s natural distribution.
130: Naive control: a flat curriculum — deliberate ordering, but without demand computation or staging.
131: Full mechanism: demand-staged curriculum with no-regression gates.
132: The naive control is the arm that matters: it isolates whether the structure does the work, or whether deliberate ordering alone would have produced the same result.
133: 8.2  What follows from the result
134: If staging beats the flat curriculum on misleading-strata acceptance, the claim is published with its measurement. If it does not, the claim is not published — internally or externally — and the Demand Table remains in force regardless, because task analysis and the capacity ledger earn their place independent of whether staging outperforms.
135: The result is recorded either way. A negative result retires the claim, not the record.
136: 9  Open decisions
137: 
138: End of briefing. This module is platform-wide and modality-independent; the audio intelligence plane is its first consumer. Component-level contracts are carried in the Incremental Training & Capacity Specification.
139: TCO
140: Module equivalent
141: Schemes
142: Trained capabilities — what a model demonstrably does, held as reusable units.
143: Capacity (M-power)
144: What a model line demonstrably holds, measured on the estate.
145: Task demand (M-demand)
146: What an objective requires held at once, computed at compile.
147: Baseline plus growth
148: A frozen base model plus incrementally trained capability.
149: Stage transition on capacity meeting demand
150: A training stage is admissible only when its demand is within reach of measured capacity.
151: Field pull
152: The corpus’s natural distribution — the majority variant’s gravity.
153: Silent operators (boost / suppress)
154: Curriculum weighting, and no-regression gates against interference with prior capability.
155: Facilitating vs misleading situations
156: Strata the data supports, versus strata where surface statistics work against the required behaviour.
157: Surface
158: What the module adds
159: Objective Wizard
160: Compiles the Demand Table alongside its existing outputs; enforces the named-failure admissibility rule at compile.
161: Capability taxonomy
162: A shared scheme vocabulary, governed by the existing propose–qualify–graduate mechanism — no new governance body.
163: Registry (Mtafiti)
164: A capacity modality holding the ledger. Not a new service.
165: Sampling & Reflection
166: The capacity probe; marginal-gain writes; the measured step.

169: Commission View

# SOURCE: assessment_workspace/canon/text/Akki_Training_Techniques_Spec.txt

1: AKKI · GOVERNED ARTIFACT · REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION
2: Training & Optimization Techniques Specification v1.0
3: The training-recipe seat · optimizer selection · ensemble critics · cascade offload · Owner-ratified · 2026-07-17
4: Scope and reading guide: this specification governs four technique areas in Akki's model-producing and quality-assurance paths. It is written for a reader with no prior context: §1 supplies the systems each requirement references. Adoption principle, Owner-ratified: a technique enters the platform only where proven use cases match the platform's targeted results, and every adoption decision is made on measured evidence from the platform's own material. Normative language: MUST / MUST NOT / MAY. Evidence classes on values: FACT (established, verifiable) · NORM (anchored in a defensible range) · DEFAULT (operating constant, revisable on evidence without reopening this document).
5: §1 — Referenced systems
6: Model training path: Akki trains adapters (LoRA/PEFT) on registered open base models, using qualified, de-duplicated units from the customer estate. Trained models are accepted through MOAC — six criteria including improvement over base (M-a), no collateral regression (M-b), lineage completeness (M-d), and calibration (M-e) — defined in the Transformation Quality Specification v1.0 §6.
7: P4 baseline harness: the first real-material run of any extraction or training pipeline is instrumented by design — utilization, throughput, and quality deltas emitted from run one (EAB Tier-1 Adoption Spec v1.1, Part X).
8: The Critic Seam: the three-tier QA layer for worker output — deterministic checks, an independent critic model, human calibration with seeded-defect audits (Critic Seam Specification v1.0). QA-1: the layer detects and never decides.
9: F3 run telemetry: every run emits throughput telemetry; cost columns activate only when compute is metered.
10: ES-4: efficiency machinery builds only against a measured shortfall; a measured shortfall makes it mandatory.
11: D-7: verdicts are never curated — evaluation inputs may be engineered, evaluation samples may not.
12: §2 — T-1 · The training-recipe seat
13: Purpose
14: Every trained model must be reproducible and attributable to the exact configuration that produced it, and configuration must improve only on evidence. The recipe seat makes training configuration a governed, versioned object rather than code.
15: Requirements
16: T-1.1 · All training configuration — optimizer and its parameters, learning-rate schedule, batch and epoch parameters, adapter rank and target modules — MUST live under training_params@v0, a sidecar configuration class with the same discipline as extraction_params@v0: versioned, ledgered, outside contracts/, no Parity contact.
17: T-1.2 · The seat ships EMPTY. No default recipe exists until the first training run fills it through the §3 protocol.
18: T-1.3 · Every trained model's registry entry MUST cite the recipe_version that trained it. MOAC M-d (lineage) extends by this field.
19: T-1.4 · Recipe revisions are DEFAULT-class: no approval ceremony. Each revision MUST attach the measured comparison that justifies it and MUST write a ledger row. A revision without attached evidence is a defect.
20: T-1.5 · Foundation methods (FACT, standing from Operating Values §1–§2): LoRA/PEFT adapters on registered open bases; training material drawn exclusively from de-duplicated, VAD-cleaned, qualified units; acceptance exclusively through MOAC on uncurated held-out sets.
21: §3 — T-2 · Optimizer selection protocol
22: Purpose
23: The optimizer is a recipe component with material effect on compute cost and model quality. Candidate optimizers — Muon is the first named candidate — are selected by measured comparison on the platform's own workload, because published optimizer results concentrate at transformer pretraining scale and the platform's workload is adapter fine-tuning.
24: Requirements
25: T-2.1 Trigger: the protocol executes at the first adapter training on real material, inside the P4-instrumented run.
26: T-2.2 Shape: one two-arm comparison — the baseline optimizer versus the candidate — with identical training data, identical base model, identical evaluation sets, and an identical compute budget cap, executed on the smallest stratum that yields a valid MOAC evaluation. The comparison's cost MUST be disclosed in the carrying phase's LoC/compute band.
27: T-2.3 Measured outputs: target-stratum improvement (the MOAC M-a metric) · non-target regression (M-b) · wall-clock and GPU-hours to convergence · calibration quality (M-e input). All four MUST be reported for both arms.
28: T-2.4 Verdict rule: quality parity on M-a and M-b is MANDATORY for a candidate to remain eligible. Compute-to-convergence is REPORTED. The adopt/reject decision is an Owner ruling made on the measured results; no adoption threshold exists in advance of the evidence. Verdict samples are uncurated per D-7.
29: T-2.5 Outcome recording: on adoption, the winning arm writes training_params@v0 v1 with the comparison attached (satisfying T-1.4). On rejection, the candidate is recorded as tested with its numbers. Either way the result is permanent record.
30: T-2.6 Recurrence: the same protocol governs every future optimizer or recipe-component candidate: two arms, identical conditions, parity mandatory, Owner-ruled on evidence.
31: §4 — T-3 · Ensemble critics
32: Purpose
33: Detection quality in the Critic Seam may require more than one reviewing instance. Ensembles are legitimate for detection and prohibited for decision: multiple reviewers may surface findings; no collection of models may hold decision authority on any platform surface. This boundary is permanent and follows from the platform's design (one walled learner; one reasoning faculty; QA-1).
34: Requirements
35: T-3.1 Deployment order: when Tier-3 seeded audits show single-critic catch-rate below the standing bar on any fall class across two consecutive audits, rubric and context repair MUST execute first. An ensemble MAY deploy only if the repaired critic still misses on a subsequent audit.
36: T-3.2 Independence: ensemble members MUST differ genuinely — a different base model, or a materially different context shape. Same-base, same-context replicas are prohibited: correlated reviewers share failure modes and add cost without detection gain (FACT, established ensemble-diversity results).
37: T-3.3 Findings-only: all ensemble output is findings, per QA-1. Voting, override, and critic-of-critic structures are prohibited.
38: T-3.4 Disagreement: disagreement between critics is itself a finding class (CRITIC-DISAGREE), routed to rulings like every finding class.
39: T-3.5 Bounds: N ≤ 3 members without an Owner ruling. Cost-per-review telemetry MUST be emitted per member.
40: T-3.6 Rent: the ensemble retires if its catch-rate gain over the single repaired critic is under 10pp (DEFAULT) after one full calibration cycle.
41: §5 — T-4 · Local-cascade LLM offload
42: Purpose
43: Where a metered LLM carries workload that cheaper local models could filter, a cascade — local model drafts, LLM handles only what the local model cannot — reduces spend. Cascades carry a documented failure mode: when too many items escalate, each escalated item pays twice and the cascade is net-negative. The platform already minimizes LLM load by construction (the rung ladder; record-derived facts are never re-asked of the LLM; the mechanical composition arm; the critic-succession seat), so a cascade builds only against demonstrated cost pressure.
44: Requirements
45: T-4.1 Trigger: cascade work MAY begin only when F3 telemetry, with cost columns active, shows LLM spend on a named seam exceeding a threshold the Owner sets at that time. No threshold is defined in advance of metered evidence.
46: T-4.2 Pre-work: before the trigger, no cascade scaffolding, draft-model acquisition, or routing machinery may be built (D7 fence). ES-4 governs: a measured shortfall makes the build mandatory; absent one, it never builds.
47: T-4.3 Shape: local model drafts → deterministic acceptance check → LLM invoked only on rejects. The acceptance check is rung-1 machinery, not a second model judgment.
48: T-4.4 Kill metric: the double-pay rate — the share of items incurring both local and LLM cost. The cascade MUST emit it from first run and MUST retire if escalation makes the cascade net-negative against the pre-cascade baseline.
49: §6 — Registry and execution
50: R4 registry rows for these requirements land only with their carrying phases: T-1 and T-2 with the first training phase; T-3 with a Critic Seam calibration phase; T-4 only if its trigger fires. Nothing lands from this specification alone.
51: This document is the drafting source for those phases' Stage As. It lands on-disk as requirements canon with the first carrying phase, or earlier on Owner word, via the standard doc-landing pattern (verbatim conversion, SHA reply, governance pointer).
52: Syni.ai · Training & Optimization Techniques Specification v1.0 · 2026-07-17 · Companion to: Operating Values v1.0 · Transformation Quality Specification v1.0 · Critic Seam Specification v1.0 · EAB Tier-1 Adoption Specification v1.1

# SOURCE: assessment_workspace/canon/text/Audio_Intelligence_Plane.md
Coordinate: source line

1: **SYNI.AI   ·   ENGINEERING SPECIFICATION**
2: 
3: **The Audio Intelligence Plane**
4: 
5: *Extraction · Learning · Training · Invention — end to end*
6: 
7: Including the Commission View surface adjustment across all extraction types · v1.0
8: 
9: *Status of this document: consolidated build specification. It supersedes the working drafts (Audio Capability Spec v1.0 and Addendum v1.1.2) and is the single reference for build. Behavioural clauses state what the system must and must not do, including on failure. Technical clauses state contracts and acceptance criteria. Items requiring verification against current code before build are marked [VERIFY] and collected in §16.*
10: 
11: **Contents**
12: 
13: # **1  ****Governing Doctrine**
14: 
15: Five principles govern every clause in this specification. Where a later clause appears to conflict with one of these, the principle wins and the clause is defective.
16: 
17: ### **1.1  An audio file is a data estate, and the framing is recursive**
18: 
19: The archive is an estate; a programme is an estate; a single file is an estate. Segments are rows; the extractable layers — content, language, condition, prosody, occurrence, code-switch, music, group-level character — are columns; no schema exists until one is declared. Census, admission, registry, and record apply at every scale.
20: 
21: ### **1.2  Modality extension, not parallel machinery**
22: 
23: The audio plane introduces no sibling services. Mtafiti gains an audio modality; Northena gains audio data classes; the wizard gains an objective variant; Targeta gains a training object. Anything in this document that reads as a parallel to an existing service is rule proliferation and must be collapsed into the existing service before build.
24: 
25: ### **1.3  One record**
26: 
27: Mtafiti and Northena collaborate to produce a single record, written once. Working state — loss curves, intermediate metrics, partial coverage counts — is scratch, not truth; it becomes record only when finalized and stamped. No local ledger exists. If a measured throughput ceiling ever demands relief, the relief is batched stamping (one row certifying N events with a digest), which remains a single record. That change is made only when a measurement demands it.
28: 
29: ### **1.4  Measure, do not assert**
30: 
31: No data-volume requirement, accuracy expectation, or cost figure is quoted without a measurement behind it. The calibration stage exists to convert assertions into measurements before commitment.
32: 
33: ### **1.5  Unrepresentable, not policed**
34: 
35: Safety boundaries are enforced by making the violating state impossible to express in the contract — the pattern established by the assertion floor — not by review after the fact. The Character Register write path (§6) and the voice identity distance gate (§7) both follow this pattern.
36: 
37: # **2  ****Capability Statement and Plane Overview**
38: 
39: Given governed access to an audio estate, the plane provides four functions in one loop:
40: 
41: - **Extraction** — audio is converted into provenance-paired facts: transcripts, entities, occurrences, and character observations.
42: 
43: - **Learning** — a Character Register accumulates group-level knowledge of how the estate’s languages and audio behave.
44: 
45: - **Training** — model production is commissioned against a falsifiable Target Outcome, planned and priced before compute is spent, with per-example provenance.
46: 
47: - **Invention** — synthesized voice identities are constructed from the register: authentically of the language, provably of no individual.
48: 
49: Each function feeds the next: extraction populates the register; the register defines the strata training plans against; trained models improve extraction; invention consumes the register’s learned layers. The loop is the capability.
50: 
51: **Flow of a commission, end to end:**
52: 
53: Objective Wizard session → compile {TargetOutcome, Collection Schema}
54: 
55: → Sampling & Reflection (calibration) → proposed Milestones + priced quote
56: 
57: → Owner agrees milestones → Commission opens
58: 
59: → Collection → Register update → Curriculum → Training runs → Certificates
60: 
61: → Commission View reports against milestones throughout → Commission sealed
62: 
63: # **3  ****Tokenized Audio Representation**
64: 
65: ## **3.1  ****Behaviour**
66: 
67: - All downstream audio work — extraction, character analysis, training — operates on discrete token sequences produced by a neural audio codec, not on waveforms.
68: 
69: - Tokenization exposes two separable streams per segment: the **content stream** (what was said — input to ASR/NER) and the **character stream** (how it was said — input to the Character Register). The character stream is retained and routed, never discarded as noise.
70: 
71: - Control markers (language, register, segment type) are splice-able tokens, enabling one model per estate rather than one per language, and native handling of code-switched speech.
72: 
73: - Failure behaviour: audio in an unsupported condition fails closed with a stated reason. The codec never silently degrades quality.
74: 
75: ## **3.2  ****Technical contract**
76: 
77: | **Item** | **Specification** |
78: | --- | --- |
79: | **Service** | perception/audio_codec/ — registered like any other perception model; census-visible; runs in-perimeter on tenant compute. |
80: | **Input** | Audio segment (bounds per ingestion segmentation) + declared or detected condition profile. |
81: | **Output** | { content_tokens[], character_stream, codec_version } Target token rate 50–100 tokens/second of audio. |
82: | **Provenance** | codec_version is a mandatory field of every downstream artifact’s provenance. A transcript states which codec produced its tokens. |
83: | **Pretraining** | The codec pretrains unsupervised on unlabelled estate audio, under the standard commissioned-job contract. |
84: | **[VERIFY]** | Perception router contract: where model registration occurs, and whether the router carries a second output stream per segment or the character stream requires its own artifact type. |
85: 
86: ## **3.3  ****Acceptance criteria**
87: 
88: - Round-trip fidelity is measured and recorded per codec version before that version serves any commission.
89: 
90: - A downstream artifact lacking codec_version in provenance is rejected at the registry boundary.
91: 
92: - An unsupported-condition input produces a refusal with a stated reason and no output artifact.
93: 
94: # **4  ****Extraction Layer**
95: 
96: ## **4.1  ****Language identification**
97: 
98: Behaviour: every segment carries a real language signal. The current plumbing value (language_hint: None) is retired.
99: 
100: - A lightweight offline language identifier (CPU-viable, in-perimeter) runs at segment level during ingestion.
101: 
102: - Recorded per segment: languages[], confidences, and code-switch points where multiple languages occur in one utterance.
103: 
104: - The signal routes downstream model selection (ASR path, NER path, de-identification path) and is written into provenance.
105: 
106: **[VERIFY] **Segment boundaries in current ingestion — confirm the unit to which a language label attaches.
107: 
108: ## **4.2  ****Code-switch points as facts**
109: 
110: Switch points (position, from-language, to-language, context class) are registered facts with provenance — not preprocessing metadata. They populate the register’s code-switch layer and stratify test sets.
111: 
112: ## **4.3  ****Condition profiling**
113: 
114: Channel condition — studio / field / telephone band, transmission artefacts, background class — is derived per segment at first ingestion. It is cheap to compute, directly predictive of extraction error, and required for training stratification. It is captured at first ingestion because re-ingesting an estate to recover it is the unaffordable mistake.
115: 
116: ## **4.4  ****Synthesis-relevant attribute capture**
117: 
118: During the same ingestion pass, group-level acoustic attributes required by any future synthesis capability (pitch statistics, energy contours, duration patterns) are captured, subject to the custody conditions of §6.4. This forecloses nothing and costs little; omitting it forecloses the invention function or forces re-ingestion.
119: 
120: ## **4.5  ****Deduplication as augmentation**
121: 
122: The occurrence index already identifies repeated content. Its output contract is extended: for each deduplicated item, the instance condition map — the set of channel/time/condition variants under which identical content occurred — is retained. One canonical extraction is stored; the variant set enters training curricula as a designated robustness stratum at zero acquisition cost. No new detection work; this is a change to what dedup keeps.
123: 
124: ## **4.6  ****Acceptance criteria**
125: 
126: - No segment leaves ingestion without languages[], condition profile, and (where applicable) switch points in provenance.
127: 
128: - A deduplicated item without its instance condition map fails the ingestion invariant test.
129: 
130: - Baseline-tier capture (§9.2) runs for all admitted material regardless of any active objective.
131: 
132: # **5  ****The Character Register — Learning**
133: 
134: ## **5.1  ****Definition**
135: 
136: A registry-modality store of learned, group-level audio characteristics, built from the character stream. Same doctrine as the fact registry: every entry carries provenance to source material and an occurrence count. It is Mtafiti’s qualification-and-index doctrine applied to acoustic observations — an extension, not a sibling (§1.2).
137: 
138: ## **5.2  ****Layers**
139: 
140: | **Layer** | **Contents** | **Primary consumers** |
141: | --- | --- | --- |
142: | **Phonetic** | Per-lexeme pronunciation variants, frequency, regional distribution. | Curriculum; extraction lexicons; evaluation stratification |
143: | **Prosodic** | Intonation contours, stress, rate distributions, pause structure. | Training; programme-type classification |
144: | **Condition** | Channel and environment profiles. | Stratification; error prediction |
145: | **Code-switch** | Switch-point patterns, language pairs, context classes. | Training; test-set design |
146: 
147: ## **5.3  ****Build process**
148: 
149: Unsupervised clustering over the character stream yields candidate strata. A cluster asserts that a distinct variant exists — not what it is called. Naming and validation are human work applied to a sample, commissioned like any other qualified work with quoted cost.
150: 
151: # **6  ****Register Custody Boundary**
152: 
153: ## **6.1  ****Governing distinction: organic versus learned**
154: 
155: Organic characteristics are anatomical — vocal tract length, formant structure, glottal source, fundamental frequency range. They cannot be acquired or shed; they are what speaker verification keys on; they are biometric. They are never registered.
156: 
157: Learned characteristics are acquired from a speech community — phonological inventory, pronunciation variants, prosody, code-switching habits. They are group properties by construction. Only learned characteristics may be registered.
158: 
159: ## **6.2  ****The four conditions — all must hold**
160: 
161: - **Acquired, not anatomical. **The attribute is learnable by a speaker from a different background.
162: 
163: - **Shared. **Observed across at least N distinct speakers. N is a governed seam value; its default inherits the platform minimum-group-size parameter unless the tenant sets a register-specific value.
164: 
165: - **Non-reconstructive in combination. **Tested against attribute combinations, not attributes in isolation: language + region + age band + one distinctive feature can reach a single person even when each attribute is group-level.
166: 
167: - **Stored as description, not exemplar. **Centroids, distributions, frequencies. Never stored audio; never per-utterance speaker embeddings. Embeddings used during clustering are destroyed after cluster assignment. Provenance points to material, not to speaker identity.
168: 
169: ## **6.3  ****Enforcement shape**
170: 
171: The register write path exposes no field through which an instance-level representation can be stored: the schema cannot represent a voiceprint. Unrepresentable, not policed (§1.5). An automated invariant test attempts each known leakage path (small stratum, idiolect marker, narrowing combination, exemplar storage) and must fail to store all of them on every change to the register code.
172: 
173: ## **6.4  ****Idiolect rule**
174: 
175: Habitual fillers, characteristic phrasings, and idiosyncratically pronounced words are learned but individuating. They fail condition 2 or 3 and are excluded. “Learned” alone is never sufficient; the four conditions are conjunctive.
176: 
177: # **7  ****Synthesized Voice Identity — Invention**
178: 
179: ## **7.1  ****Mechanism: inherit the learned, synthesize the organic**
180: 
181: - Learned characteristics are inherited from the register — this is what makes the voice sound like a speaker of the language rather than a foreigner reading it.
182: 
183: - Organic characteristics are constructed — vocal tract parameters, F0 range, formant structure, glottal parameters are chosen as a point in acoustic space that no real speaker occupies.
184: 
185: This is the inverse of a voice clone. A clone copies the organic and frequently gets the learned wrong; this gets the learned right and owns the organic outright.
186: 
187: ## **7.2  ****The distance guarantee (mandatory, fail-closed)**
188: 
189: Every constructed identity is scored against every speaker representation derivable from the corpus using standard speaker-verification methods. A minimum distance from all of them is required. Below threshold, the identity is rejected and resampled. There is no override. The threshold value and the verification method are recorded with the identity.
190: 
191: ## **7.3  ****The certificate**
192: 
193: A passing identity is issued a certificate stating that the voice is provably derived from no individual, naming the method, the threshold, and the corpus version scored against. The certificate is a first-class sellable artifact.
194: 
195: ## **7.4  ****Identity composition and versioning**
196: 
197: | **Component** | **Source** |
198: | --- | --- |
199: | **Acoustic identity** | Constructed organic parameters (§7.1). |
200: | **Speech character** | Inherited from register — phonetic and prosodic layers. |
201: | **Interaction character** | Turn-taking, formality, code-switch behaviour — inherited from register. |
202: 
203: Each identity is a versioned artifact with a ledger entry. Changing one is a ceremony with the standard waiting period, because audience recognition accrues to the voice and recognition is the asset. Identities never drift.
204: 
205: ## **7.5  ****Scope note**
206: 
207: Rendering requires a synthesis stack, which is a separate build from recognition. What this specification requires now is non-foreclosure: the identity specification (attribute schema, distance method, certificate format) is defined, and §4.4’s ingestion capture ensures the substrate exists when rendering is built.
208: 
209: # **8  ****The Objective Wizard — Schema Compiler**
210: 
211: ## **8.1  ****Role**
212: 
213: No business user hand-writes a Target Outcome. The Objective Wizard — a new variant of the existing shaping wizard, reusing its agent interface, guards, session persistence, and ledger sidecar — elicits an objective in plain language and compiles two governed artifacts:
214: 
215: - **TargetOutcome** (§10) — handed to the Training Planner.
216: 
217: - **Collection Schema** (§9) — the data dictionary for this objective: which data points are extracted from the sound, at what granularity, at what quality bar.
218: 
219: ## **8.2  ****Elicitation sequence**
220: 
221: - The question the model must answer — operational and falsifiable.
222: 
223: - The population — resolved against existing register strata; unresolved populations are flagged as unmeasured and generate census work.
224: 
225: - The acceptance bar — per stratum, two-dimensional (§10), with the gate-or-document decision recorded explicitly.
226: 
227: - The collection consequences — the wizard derives required columns, shows which are already collected (baseline tier), which exist but are uncollected, and the cost of collecting them. The owner sees the price of the schema before commissioning.
228: 
229: ## **8.3  ****Dynamism within scope: propose, qualify, graduate**
230: 
231: - **Propose. **The agent side may propose novel data points no prior objective collected. This is where innovation enters.
232: 
233: - **Qualify. **A proposed column never enters collection directly. It is admitted as a candidate: collected on a sample only, its evidence of value measured against the objective — the same qualification path any fact travels.
234: 
235: - **Graduate. **Qualified candidates graduate into the objective tier for that commission. Graduation into the baseline tier is ceremony-governed (proposal, countersignature, waiting period), because a baseline column is paid on every hour ingested for the life of the estate.
236: 
237: The compile stage is deterministic throughout: the agent proposes; only qualified columns compile. Mechanical guards prove against a stub agent before any LLM is plugged in, per the existing standing disposition.
238: 
239: ## **8.4  ****Compile-time rejections**
240: 
241: The wizard cannot emit an artifact the downstream contracts would refuse. Rejected at compile, not warned:
242: 
243: - An Outcome without an existing test_set_ref.
244: 
245: - An acceptance bar missing the per-stratum dimension.
246: 
247: - A Collection Schema requiring a column whose capture violates the custody conditions of §6.2.
248: 
249: ## **8.5  ****Record and handoff**
250: 
251: Every session stamps to the ledger via the existing turn-ledger pattern under a distinct data class (objective_session), including options considered and rejected — which is what makes a later “why was the model built this way” answerable. Compiled artifacts hand off to Targeta through the existing admission-handoff pattern. Objective → schema → plan → run is one provenance chain.
252: 
253: **[VERIFY] **The B-2/B-3 landing state of the current wizard, before choosing between extending the existing state machine with an objective variant or standing up a sibling machine sharing the agent interface and ledger sidecar.
254: 
255: # **9  ****The Collection Schema**
256: 
257: ## **9.1  ****Definition**
258: 
259: The declared data dictionary of a commission: what is extracted from the sound, for what purpose, at what quality bar. It is the admission standard of the audio estate, per objective (§1.1). It has two tiers.
260: 
261: ## **9.2  ****Baseline tier**
262: 
263: Standing, objective-independent, collected at first ingestion for all admitted material. Membership criterion: cheap to collect now, unaffordable to collect later. Contents at v1.0: language identification, code-switch points, condition profile, dedup instance condition map, synthesis-relevant group-level acoustics (§4). Changes to the baseline are seam-governed — ceremony, countersignature, waiting period — because silently narrowing the baseline is how an estate quietly becomes unre-readable.
264: 
265: ## **9.3  ****Objective tier**
266: 
267: Declared per commission by the Objective Wizard. Collected against material already in governed scope, priced before collection starts, recorded in the commission’s registry namespace. Candidate columns enter through propose–qualify–graduate (§8.3) only.
268: 
269: # **10  ****The Target Outcome**
270: 
271: ## **10.1  ****Schema**
272: 
273: TargetOutcome {
274: 
275:   task          operational statement of what the model must do
276: 
277:   domain        context of use
278: 
279:   population    defined by reference to register strata, not labels
280: 
281:   acceptance    threshold per stratum; two-dimensional (accuracy, coverage)
282: 
283:   gate_policy   per Outcome: missed stratum gates release | ships documented
284: 
285:   test_set_ref  must exist before the Outcome is accepted
286: 
287:   constraints   latency, compute budget, deployment target
288: 
289: }
290: 
291: ## **10.2  ****Binding rules**
292: 
293: - **Population is register-defined. **“Language L, accent clusters 1–4, telephone band and studio, adult” — never “speakers of L.” This is what makes coverage computable.
294: 
295: - **Acceptance is per stratum. **A single global threshold hides the failure that matters: 94% on the majority variant and 61% on the rest passes one test and fails the one that decides whether the work reaches the people it was built for.
296: 
297: - **The test set precedes the training. **An Outcome without an existing, stratified test set is rejected at definition time.
298: 
299: - **The gate decision is recorded on the Outcome **at definition — not decided ad hoc at ship time.
300: 
301: # **11  ****The Training Planner**
302: 
303: ## **11.1  ****Architecture**
304: 
305: The existing planner pattern is reused unchanged: a deterministic core computes eligibility; a learned layer may only reorder an already-eligible set it receives stripped of the values that decided eligibility; a gate compares learned output against the deterministic baseline; every plan is reproducible from its recorded inputs.
306: 
307: |  | **Extraction planning (existing)** | **Training planning (new)** |
308: | --- | --- | --- |
309: | **Object** | Source locations | Register strata |
310: | **Floor** | Defensibility class | Acceptance threshold — accuracy × coverage |
311: | **Output** | Mining plan | Training plan + curriculum + milestones |
312: 
313: ## **11.2  ****Sampling ****&**** Reflection (calibration) — mandatory first stage**
314: 
315: Data requirements for low-resource fine-tuning are empirical; no analytical answer exists. The first commissioned stage is therefore a calibration: train at three to four data volumes, evaluate per stratum against the test set, fit the scaling curve, extrapolate to the acceptance threshold. Only then is the full run quoted, with a stated confidence interval — never a point estimate. A plan without a calibration stage is rejected. The first job prices the real job.
316: 
317: ## **11.3  ****Milestones — the accountability output**
318: 
319: Sampling & Reflection has two customers. It prices the real job, and it authors the accountability structure: its output to the objective owner is not a curve but a proposed milestone list — the checklist of what must be done, in what order, for the commission to succeed. Each milestone carries a done-condition and an owner. The objective owner reviews and agrees the list at commission; from that point, all reporting is against it. Accountability is set before spend, not discovered during.
320: 
321: ## **11.4  ****Planner outputs**
322: 
323: - Coverage report — per target stratum: hours available, quality distribution, gaps, cost of closing each gap.
324: 
325: - Curriculum — ordering and weighting across strata derived from the register, not from the corpus’s natural distribution, which is always skewed toward whatever occurred most. The dedup instance condition map enters as a designated robustness stratum.
326: 
327: - Proposed milestone list (§11.3).
328: 
329: - Cost quote with a stated confidence interval.
330: 
331: ## **11.5  ****Provenance through training**
332: 
333: Every training example carries its provenance into the training manifest. Consequences: rights are enforceable per example; an example whose rights lapse is identifiable and the affected models enumerable; and “the trained model is the customer’s property” is a statement backed by a manifest, not an assertion.
334: 
335: ## **11.6  ****Run governance**
336: 
337: Training runs are commissioned jobs under the existing contract: quoted before start, metered during, certificated on completion. The completion certificate records compute consumed, data touched, manifest hash, and per-stratum results against the Outcome. Failed strata are reported as plainly as passed ones.
338: 
339: # **12  ****Record and Registry Integration**
340: 
341: ## **12.1  ****Registry (Mtafiti audio modality)**
342: 
343: Per commission, a scoped namespace within the registry holds: the Collection Schema (versioned), collected data points mapped against it — with declared-but-not-yet-collected as first-class state — the strata referenced by the Outcome, and coverage state per stratum. Reads compose with the global registry; writes are namespace-scoped. On close, the namespace is sealed, not deleted: it is the record of what was collected and why, and the next objective’s wizard session queries prior schemas and coverage so the second project starts from the first project’s map.
344: 
345: ## **12.2  ****Record (Northena data classes)**
346: 
347: Training-workflow operations stamp into the one ledger under training-specific data classes: collection events, calibration runs, curriculum decisions, milestone status changes, run certificates. The workflow’s view of “its” record is a scoped lens filterable by commission ID — a view, not a store. Working state (loss curves, intermediate metrics, partial counts) is scratch until finalized and stamped once (§1.3).
348: 
349: # **13  ****Surface Specification — the Commission View**
350: 
351: ## **13.1  ****Scope**
352: 
353: This surface adjustment applies to all commissioned work on the platform — extraction, census, and training commissions alike, across every extraction type. No modality receives its own UI, and no surface is a rendering of backend internals: rendering internals quietly commits the backend to building displayable versions of its own machinery.
354: 
355: ## **13.2  ****Behaviour**
356: 
357: **The surface is milestones. The artifacts are evidence behind them.**
358: 
359: - At Sampling & Reflection, the proposed milestone list is presented to the objective owner for agreement. Commission does not open until it is agreed.
360: 
361: - The Commission View reports against the agreed checklist: each milestone with its done-condition and owner; status in plain terms — done, on track, behind, missed. Missed is shown as plainly as done.
362: 
363: - Spend against quote is shown at the same plain level.
364: 
365: - Technical material — calibration results, strata coverage, Collection Schema state — is drill-down evidence for whoever asks why a milestone reads as it does. It is never the front page.
366: 
367: ## **13.3  ****Modality leaf**
368: 
369: Modality appears at exactly one leaf: evidence inspection. Where provenance resolves to a recording, the source plays at its timestamp rather than rendering as a page region — the existing trust-receipt pattern (“a disputed number is answered by playing the tape”), unchanged.
370: 
371: ## **13.4  ****Backend cost constraint**
372: 
373: Milestones are records with done-conditions; the platform already stamps events. No new machinery is built for display. Any surface element in this section found to require new backend computation beyond reading existing artifacts is out of specification and must be removed or re-specified.
374: 
375: # **14  ****Interface Summary**
376: 
377: | **Surface** | **Contract** |
378: | --- | --- |
379: | **audio_codec** | audio in → { content_tokens, character_stream, codec_version }; fail-closed on unsupported condition. |
