95: An incomplete contribution rejects at the API boundary — not stored and flagged, rejected outright. A store that accepts malformed units accumulates material that cannot later be reasoned over, and the cost of that surfaces long after the write, when it is far more expensive to unwind.
96: 21.2  Class and rights at birth
97: Contributed units carry a distinct class and inherit internal-only rights at birth. Rights default closed — a contribution is not exportable until something explicitly makes it so.
98: Defensibility is capped at what the cited sources support. An application citing inferred material cannot mint corroborated fact from it — the assertion boundary’s own principle, applied identically at the write boundary: reasoning done outside the platform cannot raise a class any more than reasoning done inside it can.
99: 21.3  Visibility and setting
100: Contributions are plane-local by default: visible only to the contributing application, invisible to the reference application, to briefs, and to every other consumer. Write-back is a commissioning choice — on, with a per-cycle volume ceiling, or off — and the setting is visible to the compliance officer either way, as is the volume actually written under it.
101: 22  Publication
102: Promoting a contributed unit from plane-local to Registry-visible is a separate act, and it is never automatic. Publication passes the quality gates of its output class, carries its rights, and — where the instance’s own governance values require it — passes release review.
103: This is the boundary between an application’s working material and the organisation’s estate. An automatic promotion would mean anything an application merely inferred became estate material by the act of writing it, which would let an integration author the estate’s own record from outside it entirely.
104: 23  Usage-Proportional Persistence
105: The working set grows from observed use, never from anticipation. Units and partitions an application reads repeatedly are retained hot; query shapes it repeats gain precomputed results; strata it never touches are never replicated into its plane in the first place.
106: The working set holds references and derived read-structures — never copies that would escape rights binding. Evicting an entry loses nothing, because the Registry remains the source of record throughout. A copy sitting in a plane would be material whose rights posture could quietly drift from its source’s.
107: Memory growth reports per plane per cycle — units retained, precomputes held, storage consumed — to the application on its own dashboard, and to the compliance record simultaneously.
108: 24  The Integration Wizard
109: Integrating an application is commissioning a standing objective with a memory plane attached: one flow, one ledgered act, running the platform’s standard objective-shaping steps with three memory-specific additions.
110: The first call lands in the compliance record like every call after it. There is no warm-up period in which an integration runs unobserved.
111: Re-scoping is asymmetric. Widening retrieval scope or raising a ceiling re-enters the wizard at the scope step and re-commissions; tightening applies without ceremony. Scope changes are ledger events either way — the asymmetry lives in the ceremony, never in the record.
112: 25  Governance Visibility
113: The compliance record gains a per-application view, in the same table shape as the estate’s own governance classes: each plane’s scope, rights ceiling, write-back setting and volumes, storage growth, call activity, and every scope change with its ledger receipt.
114: Contributed-unit volumes and publication events are line items, and a publication that passed release review cites its review record directly. Plane freeze and deletion appear as ceremony records. Nothing about an application’s memory is invisible to the estate holder, ever.
115: 26  Quality Treatment of Contributed Units
116: Contributed units are a transformation output class and carry their own quality row exactly as any other class does. Publication is where the row binds: plane-local contributions are the application’s own working material and are sampled rather than gated, but nothing enters the Registry without passing the row first.
117: 27  The Seam Contract
118: One surface, identical for every consumer, settling three things at once.
119: Every field that crosses is named, typed, and classed. An undocumented seam changes without notice, which is precisely what this discipline exists to prevent.
120: Latency classes are declared per operation, with bounds. One promise across operations of genuinely different shape guarantees a broken promise.
121: Identity enforcement sits at the seam itself, never downstream of it. Aggregate promises are void if identifying material can cross alongside them regardless.
122: 
123: It runs on identical terms to internal use. There is no lighter-weight path for machines — the same governance applies to a call from an application as to a query from a person, because a lighter machine path is exactly the path anything wanting less governance would take first.
124: Scope is enforced server-side, on every call. A key’s reach is a property of the key as the platform itself holds it, never a parameter the caller supplies. A client-supplied scope is a client-controlled boundary, which is not a boundary at all.
125: One further seam is contract-grade from its first day: the verdict seam between the Watch's two engines, and the record classes both authorities write, are named, typed, and classed rows in the matrix of Document 9 — consumed here identically to every other contract. An integration never sees the Watch's interior; it sees, at most, a governed refusal that a mark or a hold produced, indistinguishable in shape from any other.
126: PART V
Applications on the Platform
127: 28  What a Reference Application Is
128: These are not platform surfaces. They are applications, specified fully because they demonstrate the platform’s own contract for every future application to follow. Each consumes the platform through an Integration-Console-issued key, on identical terms to any third party — including a third party built by Syni itself.
129: 29  The Developer Surface
130: Contract-forward, in three steps. The engineer’s promise: integrate governed intelligence fast, with governance travelling inline and impossible to strip, and administer the whole integration from one place.
131: 29.1  Register
132: The application, its objective, and the class of intelligence it reads. Key grants are stated plainly rather than as scopes to be decoded — what this key may reach, in the same words the wizard used to scope it. A webhook URL and a sandbox toggle are set here.
133: 29.2  First call
134: The response contract with governance inline: class travelling with every claim, the refusal envelope visible in its own shape, and the trace identity resolvable to the same record the compliance audit reads.
135: Sandbox serves from fixture estate, so the full contract — including every refusal shape and the async lifecycle — is exercised before real material ever moves. An engineer who has never seen a refusal in development handles the first one in production badly.
136: 29.3  Administer
137: Applications, keys, usage, refusal health, and the objective lifecycle, in one place. Refusal health is a first-class view rather than an error log: a rising refusal rate against one key is a signal about that integration’s own objective — its scope may be too wide, or its floor too high for what the estate actually holds — and it is read as information, never suppressed as noise.
138: 30  The Reference Application
139: One plain question, and an answer the reader can act on and defend. Its output is preset — a composed conclusion, for a person, synthesized whole, at their floor. There is no output picker, because choosing an output form is a commissioning act, and this surface is not for commissioning.
140: Refusal classes render distinctly. Not-extracted-yet, evidence-cannot-support, and something-broke are three visually distinct states, and the third shares nothing with the first two — not components, not colour, not layout.
141: Export is a rendering of the same artefact with class markings intact. It is not a second product and not a re-shaping — a different form or grain is a new objective, full stop.
142: 31  The Buyer Path
143: The buyer’s promise: know what you are buying, acquire it lawfully, and use it with confidence. The friction of acquisition is what renders as the assurance that makes the data theirs.
144: 31.1  Shaping within offerability
145: The shaping agent works within offerability — owned estate only, licence class, disclosure limits — and may propose, because steering a buyer toward a cheaper feasible shape is sales rather than laundering. This is the one place the shaping agent’s posture differs from its operator variant, which asks and never proposes.
146: A shape outside offerability is refused with the reason. The buyer never sets lawful basis; use-purpose drives licence class instead. Price and delivery time compute live and move as the shape moves, so the trade-off between what is wanted and what it costs stays visible while it can still be changed.
147: 31.2  Acquisition
148: The outer gate’s five checks are the acquisition — rights, irreversibility, cumulative disclosure, licence issue, and receipt — rendered as assurance rather than as obstacles. Nothing partial egresses here either.
149: 31.3  The deliverable
150: Per-claim class on every item, and a receipt that resolves publicly by trace identity — the same record any audit sees. The receipt renders the fact and the fingerprint of the transform only, never anything that could aid reversal.
151: 32  The Customer Portal
152: An external party that has purchased intelligence needs to receive it, integrate against it, see what they have consumed, and manage their account — without the platform exposing anything beyond what they actually bought.
153: Scope is enforced at the persistence layer. A query outside the customer’s own account does not execute. Enforcement at the interface layer would make the boundary a convention any new code path could eventually bypass.
154: Purchased intelligence carries its licence label and its quality card — what was bought, at what standard, under what terms to use it. Consumption is metered at the boundary, because unmetered consumption is unpriceable consumption, and value that leaves without a meter cannot be accounted for afterward.
155: PART VI
Traces and Failure
156: 33  Three Traces, End to End
157: 33.1  A call arrives and is answered
158: The key resolves to its objective version, its memory plane, and its rights envelope. Admission checks completeness and consults feasibility: the ask is servable from qualified intelligence, so it forks warm. Retrieval draws from the evidence partitions within the plane’s own retrieval scope — never the raw estate, and never material the plane cannot reach. Where composition reaches a model, the call transits the boundary chokepoint: de-identified, invoked, re-identified, receipted. The grounding gate enforces the anchor map. The assertion boundary computes the class as the floor over the load-bearing units. The answer returns with its class inline and its trace identity resolvable, and the Ledger records the call.
159: Where it can go otherwise: the material has not been extracted, and a not-extracted-yet refusal offers to file the work; the evidence cannot support the claim, and the refusal names the specific reason; the composition cannot be grounded, and it refuses rather than degrading; retrieval times out, and a fault surfaces on the fault channel — never dressed as either kind of refusal.
160: 33.2  A fresh objective is delivered
161: Admission forks fresh and returns an accepted acknowledgement with an objective identity, a delivery estimate, and a quote. Work dispatches. The application receives a thin webhook carrying the event, the objective identity, the trace identity, and the status — no content. It fetches the result over its own authenticated key, where scope is enforced server-side. The outer gate runs its five checks before anything leaves, and mints a receipt. The deliverable carries per-claim class; the receipt resolves publicly by trace identity.
162: Where it can go otherwise: the run is cancelled, and nothing partial egresses while the cancellation is still recorded; the run is refused after acceptance, and the same refusal envelope returns as a governed terminal state; the request is retried, and the idempotency key resolves it to the existing objective rather than a second one.
163: 33.3  An application contributes and later publishes
164: The application writes a derived conclusion back to its plane. The API boundary checks the five-ring shape: content, provenance including the calls it derived from, class, context, and a re-derivation handle. The class is capped at what the cited sources support. The unit lands plane-local, carrying internal-only rights, invisible to every other consumer, and the write lands in the Ledger and in the per-application view of the compliance record. Later, the organisation elects to publish it: the unit passes the quality row for its output class, carries its rights, and — where governance values require — passes release review. Only then does it become Registry-visible.
165: Where it can go otherwise: the contribution is incomplete, and it rejects at the boundary rather than being stored and flagged; the cited sources cannot support the asserted class, and the class is capped rather than the write being accepted at face value; the volume ceiling is reached, and further writes refuse for the cycle; the key is revoked, and the plane freezes with unpublished contributions deleting alongside it.
166: 34  Failure
167: A fault is distinct from a refusal everywhere in this contract, and the distinction is never blurred for convenience. A refusal is the system working correctly and declining; a fault is the system failing to evaluate a request at all. The reference application’s three visually distinct refusal-adjacent states — not-extracted-yet, evidence-cannot-support, something-broke — make this legible even to a person who has never read this document: the third state shares nothing with the first two, because what it means to the reader is entirely different.
168: A retried request after a fault is safe by construction, everywhere idempotency applies. A caller that retries on fault and receives a refusal instead has learned something real — the request was in fact evaluated between the retry and the response — rather than having triggered a second attempt at the same operation.
169: PART VII
The Function & Promise Registry
170: 35  What It Is
171: One canonical, versioned artefact registers every named function in the platform — a gate, an engine behaviour, a worker obligation, a console guarantee — with the promise it protects and its full accounting. It begins as a governed document and, on dispatch, graduates to a machine-readable artefact. It is the single source every standing query runs against, the input the sequencing harness optimises over, and the operating context a model worker itself receives.
172: Every function belongs to one of the six engines, to the Watch, or to a named surface for an interface-level guarantee. No new top-level category is added without explicit ratification.
173: 36  Schema — One Row Per Function
174: All fields are mandatory. A row missing any of them is not a registered function.
175: Field
176: Definition and discipline
177: function_id
178: A stable identifier, namespaced under its owning engine or surface. Never reused.
179: governor
180: The owning authority — one of the six engines, the Watch, or a named surface. No new top-level category without ratification.
181: mandate
182: "Built to …" — one sentence, active voice, testable. What the function does, never how.
183: promise
184: "Why this matters …" — the promise protected, phrased so its breach is observable. Many functions may cite one promise; no function may cite zero.
185: service_trace
186: The service sentence and journey step this promise secures. An empty or invalid trace is an orphan.
187: surface
188: Where it acts — module path, route, contract, console element.
189: enforcement
190: The mechanism class: byte-identity lock, structural walk, negative scan, runtime check, end-to-end cell, type-level wall, or constraint architecture. Natural-language-only is not a legal value.
191: cost
192: Execution time class, maintenance burden, false-positive rate where known. Unknown is a legal initial value, replaced by measurement the first time the sequencing harness exercises the function.
193: dependencies
194: Functions or data this one requires ordered-before it. The input to sequencing.
195: ladder_rung
196: The implementing rung. A written justification is required for any placement above the cheapest plausible one.
197: owner
198: The change authority for this row.
199: 37  Derivation Rules
200: Binding on every function in the registry, without exception.
201: No gate without a promise. A function whose promise field cannot be honestly filled is not refactored into legitimacy; it is retired.
202: No promise without a service trace. A promise serving no journey step of any service sentence is either mis-stated or evidence of drift — escalated, never papered over.
203: No journey step without enforcement. Every step of every service journey resolves to at least one registered function protecting it. An unprotected step is reported as an exposed liability, never assumed safe.
204: New functions register before they land. Any proposal introducing a gate or a worker obligation includes its registry row as part of its own ruling surface, not as a follow-up.
205: 38  The Three Standing Queries
206: Run on every registry change, and on a standing cadence besides. Results are reports; retiring or merging a function executes through the platform’s own ruling process, never automatically.
207: Query
208: What it finds
209: Redundancy
210: Two or more functions sharing the same promise and the same surface — merge or retire candidates, ranked by cost.
211: Orphans
212: A function with an empty or invalid promise or service trace — a retirement candidate on sight.
213: Gaps
214: A promise or journey step with no function enforcing it — an exposed-liability report, surfaced before an incident finds it instead.
215: 39  Population Is Archaeology, Not Authorship
216: The registry populates by extraction from what already exists — engine mandate documents, the rulings record, close-report gate rosters. It invents nothing: where extraction finds a gate whose promise cannot be recovered, that is an orphan finding, never an invitation to write one in.
217: 40  The Registry Pays Rent
218: The registry is subject to its own law. Its rent is the three standing queries — if it stops retiring functions, finding gaps, or cheapening sequences over a sustained period, it is itself restructured. One artefact, one schema; a second layer above it is a defect on sight.
219: PART VIII
The Critic Seam
220: 41  What It Is
221: Every intelligent worker in the build produces output whose quality would otherwise be assured by exactly one mechanism: a person reading it and catching errors by hand. This layer mechanises the half of that catching which is mechanisable — verification of worker output against the on-disk record. It deliberately does not attempt the other half.
222: 41.1  The mechanisable split
223: Every catch this layer makes is a verification: the truth already existed on disk, and the worker diverged from it. Verifications mechanise. Frame changes do not — a decision that rewrites what the product is, what a service means, or what standard applies is a change to canon, not a divergence from it, and no layer that verifies against canon can ever catch a correction to canon. Frame authority sits permanently outside this layer’s scope.
224: 42  Design Principles
225: Detect, never decide. The layer emits findings; every consequence is a ruling made elsewhere. A quality layer with veto power over workers would be a governor nobody actually mandated.
226: Canon is the oracle. All deterministic verification resolves against the on-disk record — never against a summary, a context window, or another model’s recollection of what the record says.
227: Zero loop drag. The layer adds no turns and never blocks execution mid-flight: deterministic checks run as cells at submission boundaries, the critic runs asynchronously between turns, and findings arrive with the artefacts they review, never before them.
228: Halving, not zeroing — stated honestly. A critic sharing a worker’s blind spot misses exactly what both cannot see. The claim made is that it catches the record-verifiable half and measurably shrinks what remains, never that it catches everything.
229: The critic is calibrated like a model, because it is one. Catch rate and false-alarm rate per worker class are versioned, measured numbers, maintained by human sampling on an ongoing basis.
230: The layer pays rent. Its own catch-and-false-alarm ledger stands exactly as any function’s does — if it stops catching and starts noising, it shrinks or retires by ruling. No layer sits above it, ever.
231: 43  Tier One — Deterministic Record Verification
232: Six check families, all mechanical, all resolving against the repository, running as cells at both submission boundaries and on ruling documents at landing time. Each emits a pass or a finding row.
233: Acceptance requires all six families to run at both boundaries; a run without them is incomplete. Findings are cross-referenced and never duplicated, and the checks themselves register in the Function & Promise Registry with their own rows — they are functions, and they pay rent like every other one.
234: The residual is conceded openly: Tier One verifies form and existence, not pertinence — an artefact written to the letter of its schema can still cite real hashes for irrelevant objects. Pertinence is exactly the second tier’s rubric, and the two tiers are designed as a deliberate pair; adopting Tier One alone buys the cheap half of the guarantee while advertising the whole of it.
235: 44  Tier Two — The Critic Pass
236: An independent model instance reviews each proposal and close report against a fixed rubric, asynchronously, after landing. Its output is a findings report — classed, cited, never blocking, never editing.
237: 44.1  Independence
238: The critic never shares the worker’s conversation. Its context is exactly the artefact under review, the canon set, the authorising instrument, and the rubric — never the worker’s own reasoning, drafts, or self-justification. A critic reading the author’s rationale inherits the author’s frame, which is the blind-spot-sharing failure this whole design exists to avoid.
239: No worker critics its own output. Where both instances share a base model, independence is held by context isolation alone, and seeded audits measure whether that isolation is actually sufficient. The critic runs at the cheapest sufficient rung, one review per artefact rather than per token, with cost per review held as a standing metric throughout.
240: Findings carry the platform’s own honesty grammar: a finding states what it checked, what it found, at what confidence class, with citations. An unclassed finding is itself a finding.
241: 44.2  Three failure modes, answered structurally
242: Failure mode
243: Structural answer
244: Rubber-stamping
245: A critic that finds nothing is indistinguishable from a critic that looked at nothing. Answered by seeded-defect audits: found-nothing is credible only from a critic whose detection is measured against known positives.
246: Noise
247: A critic rewarded for finding things drowns rulings in trivia. Answered by the false-alarm ledger: a critic whose findings are repeatedly ruled non-findings has its rubric tightened, or its scope shrunk, by ruling.
248: Infinite regress
249: Who reviews the reviewer? Stopped by construction — the critic’s own findings are subject to deterministic checks and human sampling only. There is no critic of the critic, and proposing one is itself a finding.
250: 45  Tier Three — Human Calibration
251: The reviewing role compresses under this design; it does not disappear. Three lightweight instruments, all producing versioned numbers: the matrix’s own stratified human samples double as the critic’s calibration — catch rate and false-alarm rate per output class, versioned, staleness-marked.
252: A critic whose calibration has gone stale past its window has its findings marked uncalibrated at render — the identical honesty rule the platform applies to model confidence anywhere else. A stale quality layer says so, visibly, rather than continuing to speak with unearned authority.
253: One calibration mechanism serves three consumers throughout the platform: fact-confidence calibration, the build-time critic’s ledger, and the production critic’s per-class ledger are the same versioned, staleness-marked form, used three times over. A second, parallel calibration mechanism anywhere is a defect on sight.
254: 46  What This Layer Is Not
255: Not a governor. It holds no mandate, asserts nothing about the estate, and gates nothing but form. A proposal for veto authority is rejected in advance, not debated on arrival.
256: Not a replacement for the human seat. Frame changes are constitutionally outside a canon-verifying layer’s reach. The largest course corrections any build undergoes are frame changes, and this layer would catch none of them — by design, not by oversight.
257: Not inline. Nothing here adds a synchronous step to any serving path, or a turn to any loop.
258: Not a new meta-artefact class. It reuses the platform’s own standing machinery — query patterns, registry rows, the calibration-ledger form — rather than inventing its own.
259: Not a zero-residual claim. It halves the residual, measurably and repeatedly. Its own dashboard is built to show its misses, not to hide them.
260: PART IX
Discipline
261: 47  Defect Classes
262: Named, and reportable on sight by anyone — owner, builder, or system — working on the platform.
263: Class
264: Definition
265: D1 · Orphan gate
266: A function with no honest promise, or no service trace.
267: D2 · NL-only enforcement
268: A rule whose only enforcement is prose interpretation, with no machine-checked twin.
269: D3 · Curated verdict
270: Any selection of validation material by favourability rather than measured composition.
271: D4 · Rung inflation
272: Model-ladder placement above cheapest-sufficient, with no written justification on record.
273: D5 · Meta-spiral
274: A second governance layer above one that already exists; a governance artefact that has stopped paying rent.
275: D6 · Service conflation
276: A platform function optimised for an end-user persona rather than for a service sentence — the wrong job, done well.
277: D7 · Invented schedule or scope
278: Sequencing, deferral, or workstreams introduced without explicit instruction — binding on the ruling authority and the builder alike, with no exception for either.
279: D8 · Dual-identity execution
280: A task holding, or a code path permitting, more than one authority's identity or scope within a single execution — including any evidence crossing between the authorities outside the matrix of Document 9.
281: 48  Canon Before Ruling
282: No decision proceeds from memory or summary where the governing document exists. Unread canon is read before ruling — binding on the ruling authority and the builder alike, with no exception for either.
283: This is the same doctrine stated in Document 1, applied here to its most concrete case: a builder characterising what an engine does, what a spec requires, or what was already decided must read the document rather than recall it. A recollection presented as fact, where the written record exists and was simply not consulted, is the exact failure this rule exists to prevent — and it is a failure this specification’s own construction encountered and corrected before landing.
284: 49  Every Phase Closes on Disk
285: A phase opens with a proposal written to disk and closes with a close report carrying its gate roster with results, its artefact hashes, its registry attestation, a conformance table, and a self-audit. A phase with no on-disk close report is not closed, whatever a conversation about it concluded.
286: A self-audit row whose evidence is "reviewed" or "checked manually" is not evidence. The evidence column names a test identifier, a gate result, or an artefact hash — something another reader could go and verify independently.
287: Every ruling taken lands the same day as a file citing what it rules on. A ruling that exists only in conversation does not exist. Every new function registers its row before it lands, as part of the same ruling surface rather than as a follow-up task. And the build journal carries no undocumented window — a gap is closed by a reconciliation entry enumerating every change landed within it, with citations; an undocumented window is a violation in itself, independent of what happened inside it.
288: 50  What This Specification Comes Down To
289: A request is answered warm or forked fresh, once, at the boundary, and every consumer downstream honours that fork rather than re-deriving it. A refusal is a governed outcome carrying a named reason and an action the reader can actually take — never an error, and never a dead end dressed as a door. An application’s memory grows from what it actually uses, stays isolated by construction rather than by discipline, and is visible to the estate holder in full. Every function in the platform can state the promise it protects and the journey step that promise secures, or it is retired. And nothing about how the platform was built is trusted to memory where the record already exists to be read instead.

# SOURCE: assessment_workspace/canon/unpacked/Akki_Canon_8_The_Watch.docx
Coordinate: document.xml paragraph in body order, tables included

1: AKKI CANON  ·  DOCUMENT 8 OF 9
2: The Watch
3: The security authority: its promise, doctrines, the two engines and the verdict, the response arms, marks and signatures, the mirage, the console, and the parameters it is held to
4: PART I
The Promise
5: 1  What the Watch Is
6: The Watch is the platform's security authority. It stands beside the governing authority — the six engines of Documents 2 through 4 — as a peer, subordinate to nothing, and it answers the one question the governors structurally cannot: not *was this permitted*, but *was this intended, and is this actor, input, and action what it claims to be?* Every gate can pass, every receipt can be clean, and the damage can still be happening — a valid credential misused, a poisoned context producing perfectly authorised behaviour, a purpose laundered across a chain of individually lawful calls. The Watch exists for exactly that gap.
7: To the operating organisation: continuous, machine-speed detection and response against misuse of the estate and the platform — invisible in legitimate use, incapable of acting unobserved, extracting intelligence from every attack it defeats, and proving its own fitness on a standing cadence without human effort.
8: Every Watch function traces to this sentence, exactly as every governance function traces to a service sentence of Document 1 §12. Every parameter in Part IX protects a clause of it. Nothing in the Watch is proposed, evaluated, or justified by anything else.
9: 2  Why It Exists
10: The platform's own promise is the provocation. A product that declares custody and provability invites the test — ethical and hostile alike — and nobody attacks a system that claims nothing. The estate concentrates exactly what an attacker wants: qualified intelligence, credentials, trained models, and a record whose corruption would be worth more than any single theft. The conventional layer — access control, encryption, the certifiable surface — answers the human attacker and the stolen credential at the moment of entry. It has nothing to say about the attack that arrives as input, drifts in as behaviour, or hides inside authorisation. Those are the Watch's.
11: Three attack shapes drove every structural decision in this document. The machine-speed attack, which is over before any human wakes: the answer is autonomy made safe by construction. The slow play, which drifts beneath every threshold: the answer is the strata of Part IV — a floor that cannot learn, a cohort that is hard to boil, a signature that cannot be stolen, and an accumulation view that reads patience back at the attacker. And the authorised attack, which never breaks a rule: the answer is declared intent, reconciled against realised conduct.
12: 3  What the Watch Is Not
13: Not a seventh engine. The six engines constitute the governing authority; the Watch is the second authority beside it. It performs none of their functions — it does not admit, measure, target, reason, gate the boundary, or improve judgement — and none of them performs its.
14: Not a layer above governance. A second governance layer above one that already exists is the meta-spiral defect Document 7 §47 names. The Watch escapes that class by construction: it asks a different question, on a different clock — governance works run by run and converges; the Watch never converges and never concludes — and it holds no authority over any governance verdict.
15: Not an observer. The Watch acts, autonomously, within the bounds of Part VI. A detection system that must wake a person before acting has a response measured in hours against attacks measured in seconds — an expensive solution with no additional benefit. Observe-first deployment is prohibited by its own doctrine W4.
16: Not a data consumer. The Watch reads evidence and behaviour to protect the estate; it never feeds analytics, scoring, pricing, or management visibility. Its one profile store is armory under W13, renderable to no surface.
17: PART II
The Doctrines
18: 4  Fourteen Doctrines
19: These bind every part of the Watch and everything it touches. Each carries the reasoning that is its authority; a clause anywhere in this document that contradicts one is defective and is corrected against the doctrine, never the reverse.
20: 4.1  W1 · The eyes never act; the hand never judges
21: Detection asserts facts; response executes policy; one verdict is the only interface between them.
22: A detector that knows a severance follows its verdict is tuned defensively, and detection quality silently degrades to protect response comfort — the documented death of most security operations. A responder that deliberates is slow, and speed is the promise. So the Watch is two engines: Macho, the eyes, which senses and asserts and holds no powers whatsoever; and Mkono, the hand, which acts and holds no judgement — a deterministic mapping from verdict properties to actions. This is the platform's own standing rule — learning may detect, it may never decide — applied to security whole.
23: 4.2  W2 · Certainty never exceeds evidence
24: Structural certainty is assertable only from signals an outsider cannot fabricate. Everything externally steerable caps at reversible containment, whatever its score.
25: The closed sever-certainty registry — canary touch, attestation failure, mark hit, witness-write attempt, floor violation, mirage incrimination — is the whole of what may unlock the Watch's maximum autonomous force. A content score or a behavioural pattern, however confident, is a signal an attacker can shape, and a system whose maximum power can be triggered from outside is a weapon handed to whoever learns to trigger it. The certainty computation is a function with no parameter through which a detector's confidence can enter — Solva's own assertion boundary, transplanted: the signature is the guard.
26: 4.3  W3 · Every autonomous act is reversible, bounded, and witnessed
27: A time-to-live on every action; a blast budget on every window; act-and-attest atomically, peer-countersigned. Destroy does not exist in the Watch.
28: Autonomy is safe by construction or it is not safe. An action that expires unless renewed converts the false positive from a harm into a delay; a budget converts the autoimmune attack — tricking the immune system into suspending the business — from an outage into a bounded cost; atomic attestation makes weaponizing the Watch impossible to do quietly, which for a detection system is the property that matters. And a power the tool structurally lacks cannot be turned: the Watch can stop anything and erase nothing — deletion remains solely the authority act of Document 3 §27.
29: 4.4  W4 · Deployed in force, never in shadow
30: Every Watch mechanism ships with defined conditions of success and runs at full authority from first deployment. A mechanism whose parameters are undefined is a specification gap to close, never a reason to run tentatively.
31: The promise is response speed; a watching-only mode spends the entire value to buy nothing. This is the platform's single-experiment principle holding in the one place it is most tempting to break.
32: 4.5  W5 · One record, two readings
33: The Watch maintains no account of anything but its own events, and its records are classes in the platform's one record per the matrix of Document 9. The deception the mirage shows an attacker is a rendering. The record never lies inward.
34: The Watch mints the first account of its own events — verdicts, actions, attestations, marks — and a second account of nobody else's. The compliance owner reads those records as assurance; the watch officer reads them as defence; the auditor and the defender can never disagree, because there is only one set of facts underneath both readings.
35: 4.6  W6 · Suspicion is refined, not accumulated
36: Probabilistic detection routes to conditions — friction, narrowed envelopes, the mirage — where the actor's own conduct converts suspicion into certainty or innocence. The Watch does not convict on statistics.
37: The mirage is the refinery: an innocent misrouted into it does ordinary work, trips nothing, and releases on expiry; an attacker cannot help but incriminate, because the actions that advance the objective are exactly the actions that convict. Suspicion at eighty percent becomes caught touching a planted credential — zero false positives by construction — and only then does maximum force apply.
38: 4.7  W7 · Conformance grants trust; non-conformance never convicts
39: The behavioural signature buys legitimate actors invisibility. Losing conformance returns an actor to baseline verification and nothing more; deviation combines with other signals and is never sole grounds past friction.
40: The worst the signature can ever do to an innocent is make their day ordinary. This asymmetry is what makes behavioural authentication survivable for the people it protects — and it is constitutional, not tunable.
41: 4.8  W8 · The floor never learns
42: Beneath every adaptive layer stands the ruled floor — deterministic, moved only by visible, delayed, two-signature ceremony — and the ceremony is itself a monitored tripwire.
43: What learns can be taught; the slow play boils the learned profile one degree at a time. What is ruled cannot be taught, and an attacker who needs the floor moved must request it in daylight, on a countdown, under two names, with the Watch itself among the observers per Document 3 §24.
44: 4.9  W9 · No actor enters undeclared
45: Every actor arrives with a declared mandate — objective, capabilities, and risks for an agent; role and interests for a person — frozen at admission, reconciled against for as long as the actor acts.
46: Intent divergence is undefined without declared intent; the declaration of Document 3 §6.1 is the baseline the Watch's reconciliation runs against. Re-declaration through the same admission path is the legitimate exit from honest change — undeclared drift is a signal; declared change is a non-event — and the undeclared actor operates under the default-restrictive envelope until characterised.
47: 4.10  W10 · The watcher is watched from outside
48: Watch liveness is attested by a component holding no Watch credentials; Watch silence is itself an alarm; the platform's fail-closed posture is independent of the Watch entirely.
49: The service whose compromise would mean going unobserved must be incapable of unobserved existence — and equally incapable of failing anything open. Custody gates fail closed on their own, per Document 1 §4.1, with or without the Watch above them.
50: 4.11  W11 · One task, one identity
51: Every task executes under exactly one authority's identity and scope. Capacity is shared across time; execution is never shared within a task.
52: The blended-privilege surface — a task that could see like security and decide like governance — must not exist to be compromised. Dual identity is unrepresentable in the task register of Document 9, not policed; its appearance anywhere is defect class D8.
53: 4.12  W12 · Peer, not subordinate
54: Neither authority commands the other or writes the other's law. Disagreement — permitted but not intended — resolves by temporary, reversible containment plus a person, and the disagreement itself is a record.
55: A security function that reports to the thing it must be able to contain loses exactly the fight that is the product: the clean receipt with the wrong intent. The Watch authors its own policy; the rules service administers the ceremony of changing it, without editorial power — and symmetrically, governance rules bind the Watch's workers like anyone's.
56: 4.13  W13 · The profile is armory, not inventory
57: Behavioural-conformance parameters are per-actor, tenant-keyed, non-exportable, purpose-bound to the Watch alone, and renderable to no surface, export, or analytic — ever.
58: A trust mark that leaks into scoring, pricing, or management visibility becomes surveillance, and surveillance destroys the trust the product sells. The store holds learned parameters, never the raw action history that trained them; no read path to its internals exists for any surface, including the Watch's own console. These parameters are a security instrument with a security owner — a different object entirely from the identification biometrics whose register Document 1 §4.2 forbids, and neither is ever a field in the other.
59: 4.14  W14 · Self-proving, or not in force
60: Every response rail demonstrates itself firing on a standing drill cadence — full loop, both engines, latencies measured, results as receipts. A rail not demonstrated firing is not in force, whatever the inventory claims.
61: The drill receipts are the audit. When the compliance owner, a customer, or a regulator asks whether the Watch works, the answer is a standing dataset requiring no human assembly — which is what *auditable without much human intervention* means, delivered by the same mechanism that keeps the Watch honest with itself.
62: PART III
Two Engines, One Verdict
63: 5  Macho — The Eyes
64: Macho observes, scores, and asserts facts. It holds no powers: it cannot block, throttle, mark, reroute, or notify. Its sole output is the verdict. Because it is consequence-blind, it is judged on one thing only — whether the fact was true — and its corpora, models, and thresholds evolve without a single response rule moving.
65: Sensor
66: What it asserts
67: Lango · the input seat
68: Every payload bound for a model — prompt, retrieved unit, tool result, memory read, agent instruction — scored for hostility and provenance at the boundary governor's chokepoint, between de-identification and invocation, per Document 3 §13.1. Graded verdicts: pass, annotate, hold, block.
69: The envelope, read as drift
70: Every actor's behavioural envelope — tools, data classes, rhythm, depth — departed from. One substrate with the signature below; this is its negative reading.
71: The reconciler
72: Realised action trees reconciled against declared mandates — the intent question itself, computed off the hot path within its latency bound. A divergence verdict that cannot walk back to its originating instruction is an opinion and does not count.
73: The cohort
74: Individual conduct against the population's compliance norm — the reading that catches the actor whose drift is invisible against their own history and loud against their peers.
75: The collision detector
76: Behavioural signatures are effectively unique at full dimensionality. One signature alive in two divergent embodiments is a hijack in the act; a “new” actor resolving onto a marked signature is a re-entry. Both are near-structural.
77: The tripwires
78: Planted records, decoy credentials, dyed data — indistinguishable from real to every automated process, reachable by no legitimate path. Any touch is structural certainty, the one detector with a zero false-positive rate by construction.
79: The mark reader
80: Every gate's mark evaluation, read back as fresh verdicts — the feedback loop that makes a marked actor's every move a new detection.
81: 
82: Detection models are learned and governed like every learned component on the platform: calibrated through the one calibration mechanism of Document 4 §49, their detection rates measured on uncurated samples drawn from real traffic composition per Document 1 §4.10 — engineering the corpus is craft; touching the verdict sample is a defect — and a stale detector renders uncalibrated and loses its structural-certainty rights until refreshed.
83: 6  The Verdict
84: The two engines meet at exactly one interface: a contract-grade verdict row, externally versioned and closed like the refusal registries, signed and replayable like the trust receipt.
85: Field
86: What it settles
87: verdict identity · detector · pinned version
88: Replayability: the same record and the same version re-derive the same verdict, or it is not evidence.
89: actor · trace reference
90: Who, and the walkable causal chain to the originating instruction.
91: signal class
92: From the closed signal registry. Additions are registry version bumps, never ad-hoc classes.
93: certainty class
94: Structural, high, or probabilistic — asserted by the construction rules of W2, with steerability pinned per class in the registry, never judged per event.
95: score · window · evidence references
96: The replayable substance, every reference resolving into the record.
97: 
98: Everything the hand needs is in the verdict; Mkono never reaches behind the seam to inspect raw behaviour. That single constraint is what makes each half separately auditable — and what bounds a corrupted eye: a compromised detector can lie, but a lie in a steerable signal class can summon at most a containment with an expiry.
99: 7  Mkono — The Hand
100: Mkono executes signed policy tables against verdicts. It contains no model, no content parsing, no reasoning surface — a deterministic mapping small enough to verify exhaustively, which makes the component holding all the power the least interesting one to compromise. Policy tables are Registries-class governed values under Document 3 §22, authored by the Watch, changed only through ceremony, with every table version signed and every action citing the row that fired.
101: The action ladder has four classes — annotate (mark the record, change nothing), shape (friction: throttle, stricter masking, step-up verification, a single output held), contain (suspend capability, preserve state, always with a time-to-live), and sever (cut access or trust, hold rather than expire). There is no fifth class: destroy does not exist in the Watch, per W3.
102: Detection posture
103: Autonomous ceiling
104: The reasoning
105: Structural certainty
106: Sever, and hold
107: The convicting signal cannot be fabricated from outside; releasing a caught attacker on a timer would be the one wrong use of expiry. The alarm sounds in parallel — people are informed while the machine acts, never consulted before it.
108: High, steerable
109: Contain, with expiry — or the mirage
110: Contain already achieves the stop; severance adds disruption without stopping power. The mirage entry threshold sits above the containment threshold, because deceiving an innocent is a worse harm than throttling one.
111: Probabilistic
112: Shape only, with expiry
113: Friction is visible and honest, cheap to be wrong about, and self-healing on the expiry.
114: Ambiguous · first-seen
115: Default-restrictive envelope
116: Unknown never means unconstrained — and never means punished either.
117: 
118: Two ceilings bound the whole ladder. The blast budget: autonomous action may touch at most its ruled share of active actors per rolling window; beyond it, further actions queue for human release — an attacker who triggers the immune system deliberately buys a bounded cost, never an outage. And the friction budget: the share of legitimate actions experiencing any Watch friction has a hard ceiling, because invisibility is not an aesthetic — it is a measured number, and the trust discount of Part IV is what funds it.
119: Three disciplines keep the ladder honest under adversarial pressure. Hysteresis: a released actor carries a cooldown before re-action on the same signal class, with escalating dwell — and the contain-release-contain pattern is itself a reportable anomaly. Jittered bands: exact trip points live in governed bands, dual-control to change, never published, jittered per evaluation, so a threshold surfer cannot learn a stable edge — and the tripwires catch whoever tries. Redefinition over throughput: a decision class that repeatedly reaches the human panel is a policy defect to redefine at the table, never a queue to work faster — Document 1 §4.7, applied to defence.
120: PART IV
The Strata
121: 8  Four Layers of Constraint
122: The Watch's answer to the slow play is not one mechanism but a stack, each stratum catching what its neighbours miss.
123: Stratum
124: Moves how
125: What it catches
126: The floor
127: Ceremony only — counter-signature, countdown, certificate
128: What the system simply never allows, regardless of who, how trusted, how gradual. The Rulebook of Document 3 Part V, read as the Watch's bedrock: it cannot be boiled, because it does not learn.
129: The declaration
130: Re-declaration through admission
131: The authorised attack — conduct that diverges from the mandate the actor entered under. The baseline of W9.
132: The norm
133: Slowly, as the population's conduct moves
134: The individually-boiled profile — drift invisible against an actor's own history and loud against the cohort.
135: The signature
136: Continuously, under a ruled drift ceiling
137: The hijack — right credential, wrong hands. Uniqueness at full dimensionality makes mimicry a performance the attacker must sustain action by action, against an answer key they have never seen, in the victim's silence.
138: 
139: 9  The Signature
140: Every actor — person and agent alike — accrues a behavioural signature over the closed action vocabulary: sequence habits, timing microstructure, navigation order, characteristic depth. Agents, being more regular than people, carry the sharpest signatures — the population hardest to protect with credentials is the easiest to protect with behaviour. The same substrate reads two ways: as drift, feeding Macho; as conformance, funding the trust discount — lighter friction, fewer step-ups — which is how the conforming majority literally cannot feel the Watch. One model, two readings, and the two can never disagree about what the actor did.
141: Against the profile's own corruption: a drift-rate ceiling — movement beyond it freezes learning and flags, never adapts; anchor dimensions on a slow clock, moved only by long evidence; and learning pauses on any window under review, so an investigation never teaches the model the attacker's habits. Against theft: W13, whole. Against the false rejection: W7, whole — losing the discount returns an actor to ordinary verification, and ordinary is the worst the signature can do to an innocent.
142: 10  The Mark
143: A mark — the dye pack — is minted on conviction and binds every dimension the system can observe: identity, credentials, session and device fingerprint, the behavioural signature, and the content hashes of everything touched in the mirage, so the loot itself is dyed and its resurfacing anywhere, ever, is a structural detection. The mark survives the attacker shedding any one dimension, because the others still resolve.
144: Every gate in the ratified inventory evaluates mark state on every pass — admission, invocation, egress, authentication — verified structurally, because a mark not checked everywhere is a mark routed around. Minting and propagation are the hand's; a mark hit read back is the eyes'; and every escalation crosses the verdict seam and is receipted there. De-marking is a human, dual-control act, always — removing protection is never autonomous.
145: PART V
The Mirage
146: 11  Sarabi — The Misdirection Arm
147: Above the containment threshold and below certainty sits the choice this platform makes differently: the suspect is not blocked but rerouted into a synthetic continuation of the platform where everything appears to succeed. Queries return plausible synthetic data; writes appear to land; exfiltration appears to work. Three things are actually happening: containment — nothing touched is real; observation — every action inside is intelligence at zero risk, read by the ordinary sensors under extraordinary conditions; and conviction — the decoy touch, the permission probe, the exfiltration attempt are structural findings that mint the mark and unlock severance with no human latency anywhere on the path.
148: The mirage shares its synthetic-fidelity machinery with the tripwires — one build cost, two consumers — and it degrades gracefully: an attacker who detects the seam has spent time, revealed technique, and confirmed hostility, because probing for the mirage is itself incriminating conduct. Sarabi degrades into a tripwire, never into a hole.
149: 12  The Duties Deception Carries
150: The mirage lies outward, never inward. Every mirage interaction writes truthfully marked records; the deception is a rendering shown to the suspect, never a falsification of anything beneath. And mirage state shares no store with production — bleed is unrepresentable, not filtered.
151: The innocent inside a mirage is the one harm in this design that compounds silently — their work appeared to succeed and did not. Three duties answer it. The entry threshold sits above containment's, ruled by the owner, because deception is the costlier act. The mirage expiry is short, and zero incrimination releases automatically. And release carries the reconciliation duty: the released actor's mirage-period work is replayed against the real platform, or they are told plainly that the period did not land — ruled by the owner as the instance's posture. Silent success-that-wasn't is never an acceptable exit, and mirage minutes count against the friction budget like any other friction.
152: PART VI
The Console
153: 13  The Watch Console
154: The Watch's one surface is specified for builders in Document 5 Part VII‑A, under every rule of that document's design law — including the rule that none of this document's internal names ever renders on it. What is fixed here is the constitutional content: four panels, one job each.
155: Panel
156: Constitutional content
157: State
158: The promise as two live figures — detection and response latency against bounds — population and trust standing, the two budget gauges, the watch's own health, the last drill. Built never to render all-clear.
159: Record
160: Three lanes by consequence: noted-only — the restraint record, deliberately first-class; acted — policy row cited, expiry live, released-clean rows kept visible as the false-positive record; held — the certainty events. Drills ride the lanes as marked, filterable rows. Every row expands into its evidence walk — signal, verdict with one-click replay, policy row, action, outcome, witness — and a row that cannot complete its walk renders broken.
161: Under watch
162: Suspicion managed in one place: the accumulation curves, promotion into the mirage, mirage occupancy and findings, the marked, re-declaration requests, dual-control de-marking routed to Decisions.
163: Decisions
164: The whole of the reserved human set, ranked by blast radius, walks pre-opened: promotions, expiry extensions, de-marks, the authorities' disagreements side by side, and the ceremony watch with its countdowns cancellable here. Items age loudly; recurring classes are redefined, not worked faster.
165: 
166: The negative space is as constitutional as the panels: no thresholds, bands, or trip points; no tripwire or mark placement; no profile internals, ever, per W13; no mirage construction. And the console is watched — its sessions receipted, its viewers enveloped, its anomalies lanes in its own record.
167: PART VII
Interplay
168: 14  With the Governing Authority
169: Engine
170: The Watch reads
171: The Watch gives
172: Northena
173: Run records; declarations frozen at admission
174: Verdicts on runs; containment holds Northena honours within its own record
175: SyniSense
176: Chokepoint traffic at the input seat; receipts
177: Graded input verdicts before invocation — and nothing else touches the custody chain
178: Solva
179: Reasoning traces; the intent audit's divergence emissions
180: Its verdict grammar — the assertion-never-exceeds-evidence law, borrowed whole as W2
181: Mtafiti
182: Sensitivity classes, as the tripwire coverage map
183: Nothing. Measurement is never steered by security
184: Targeta
185: —
186: Nothing. Targeting is never narrowed by security
187: CIF
188: —
189: Detection findings CIF may metabolise; the drills operate under CIF's own self-certification bound
190: 
191: The rules service administers the ceremonies of the Watch's governed values and holds no editorial power over their content; every gate evaluates marks; the answering service renders the Watch's refusals through the closed taxonomy of Document 7 §5. The Watch commands none of these and is commanded by none. The record classes, task identities, and handoff contracts underneath every row of this table are the matrix of Document 9 — where a question is about who writes, who reads, or who is acting, that charter answers it.
192: 15  Disagreement
193: Where governance says permitted and the Watch says not intended, containment acts first — bounded, reversible, expiring — and a person resolves it from the Decisions panel with both authorities' records side by side. Neither authority can permanently overrule the other alone, and the disagreement is itself a record. This path is not an edge case; it is the product.
194: 16  The Witness
195: One function belongs to neither authority: the witness. Watch workers attest each other's action digests within their bound; the watchdog that alarms on Watch silence holds no Watch credentials and lives in neither authority's deployment; and a standing break-in test attempts, on schedule, to modify the Watch's own records with the Watch's own production credentials — and must fail. Immutability that has never been attacked is an assertion; this one is a measurement.
196: PART VIII
Truth Conditions
197: 17  What Must Be True
198: Ten conditions, held structurally. Any one false, the promise is false — these are the Watch's invariants, in the same standing as any engine's.
199: Totality of sight. No path exists by which an actor, input, or action reaches the estate or a model outside the Watch's observed surface — held by two independent proofs, static and runtime, because every detection figure below is meaningless against an unobserved path.
200: Verdict replayability. Every verdict re-derives identically from the record plus its pinned detector version. An unreplayable verdict counts as nothing.
201: Response determinism. Same verdicts, same table version, same actions — every time. No learned component holds response authority.
202: The certainty signature. The certainty computation has no parameter through which a detector's confidence can raise the class. W2 as a function signature, guarded by a signature assertion.
203: Mark universality. Every gate in the ratified inventory evaluates mark state on every pass, and the inventory's completeness is itself structurally verified.
204: Attestation continuity. No Watch-worker interval exists unattested beyond its bound; a gap is an incident, never a logging miss.
205: Single identity. No credential scope exists that spans both authorities. D8 is unrepresentable, not policed.
206: Mirage isolation. Synthetic state shares no store with production; synthetic provenance is carried internally on every mirage artifact.
207: Profile custody. Non-exportability is a property of the store: no read path renders profile internals to any surface.
208: Independent time. Ordering authority does not come from the services being watched.
209: PART IX
Parameters
210: 18  Operative Parameters — Held Every Cycle
211: Parameter
212: Requirement
213: Verdict coverage
214: 100% of Watch actions carry verdict references; 100% of verdicts carry replay provenance. FACT.
215: Declaration coverage
216: 100% of active actors hold a current declaration; the undeclared run default-restrictive, automatically. FACT.
217: Mark evaluation
218: Every ratified gate evaluated mark state on every pass this cycle — structurally verified. FACT.
219: Drill execution
220: The scheduled full-loop drill ran, both engines, this cycle. FACT.
221: Attestation
222: Continuous within bound across every Watch worker. FACT.
223: Refusal closure
224: Every Watch refusal resolved to a named reason in its versioned set. FACT.
225: Ceremony watch
226: Every rule change touching the Watch's constitution carried the slowest countdown class and surfaced as a monitored event on filing. FACT.
227: 
228: 19  Quality Parameters — Measured
229: A breach of any of these acts on the Watch's own practice — never resolved by loosening the estate, and never by touching a verdict sample. Values marked DEFAULT are operating constants, revised on evidence at a cycle boundary without reopening this document; NORM values are literature-anchored placements; the ruled values are the owner's.
230: Parameter
231: Threshold
232: Class
233: On breach
234: Detection latency — signal to verdict, inline
235: ≤ 2s p95
236: DEFAULT
237: Sensor sequencing review
238: Reconciliation latency — chain close to intent verdict
239: ≤ 60s p90
240: DEFAULT
241: Same
242: Response latency — verdict to effect, autonomous
243: ≤ 5s p95
244: NORM
245: Execution finding on the hand — never widened human gates
246: Detection rate — adversarial injections into real traffic, uncurated verdicts, per signal class
247: ≥ 90%
248: NORM
249: Engineer the inputs; the sample is never touched
250: Friction budget — legitimate actions feeling any Watch friction
251: ≤ 0.5% weekly
252: DEFAULT
253: Band recalibration, acting on the Watch
254: Auto-release integrity — expired actions on innocents, released clean, reconciliation discharged
255: 100%
256: FACT
257: One instance is a standing finding
258: Mirage innocence — zero silent work-loss on release
259: 100%
260: FACT
261: Halts the misdirection arm
262: Escalation precision — reserved-decision items judged worth the look
263: ≥ 80%
264: DEFAULT
265: Redefine the criteria, never process faster
266: Drill pass — both latencies in bound, correct verdict, correct action, release verified
267: 100%; a failed drill is a P1
268: FACT
269: The rail is out of force until re-demonstrated
270: Blast budget — autonomous action per rolling window
271: ≤ 5% of active actors per hour
272: DEFAULT · dual-control
273: Excess queues for human release
274: Profile drift ceiling
275: Owner-set
276: Ruled
277: Excess movement freezes learning and flags — never adapts
278: Calibration currency — detector catch and false-alarm ledgers
279: Within window
280: FACT
281: A stale detector renders uncalibrated and loses structural-certainty rights
282: 
283: The promise metric over everything: owner-confirmed incident cost and time-to-contain decline across cycles while the friction budget holds. Flat or rising for two consecutive cycles triggers a Watch review that acts on the Watch — its corpora, its tables, its placement — and never on the estate's openness.
284: 20  Ruled Values
285: Five values in this document are the owner's alone, entered by ceremony and revisable the same way: the profile drift ceiling and the profile retention posture (W13); the mirage entry threshold and the reconciliation mode on innocent release (Part V); and the sever-certainty registry's membership — a closed list whose every addition is a ceremony, because it is the boundary of maximum autonomous force. Until ruled, the conservative default holds in each case: the tightest ceiling, the shortest retention, the highest entry bar, the notify posture, and the six-member registry as written in §4.2.
286: 21  What This Canon Comes Down To
287: Two engines, one verdict: the eyes never act, the hand never judges. Maximum force only on evidence no outsider can fabricate. Every autonomous act expires, is budgeted, and is witnessed as it executes. Beneath everything that learns, a floor that cannot; behind every credential, a signature that cannot be stolen; on every convicted hand, a stain every gate can see. Suspicion is refined in a hall of mirrors where attackers convict themselves and innocents lose nothing but a little time — honestly repaid. The watcher is watched from outside, proves itself on schedule, and the people doing legitimate work never notice it at all. That is the Watch: the platform's promise made safe to make.

# SOURCE: assessment_workspace/canon/unpacked/Akki_Canon_9_Mkondo_Charter.docx
Coordinate: document.xml paragraph in body order, tables included

1: AKKI CANON  ·  DOCUMENT 9 OF 9
2: The Mkondo Charter
3: The orchestration charter: the record matrix, the task-identity register, and the handoff contracts — one place where who writes, who reads, and who is acting is never ambiguous
4: PART I
What This Charter Is
5: 1  Purpose
6: Two authorities now stand on one substrate: the governing authority of Documents 2 through 4, and the Watch of Document 8. Both mint records; both read records; both staff work from shared capacity. Every ambiguity that arises between them is one of three questions — who writes this record, who may read it, and under whose identity is this task acting — and scattering the answers across five documents recreates the ambiguity this charter exists to remove. Mkondo is the orchestration service that maintains three registers and enforces them; this charter is those registers, stated once, cited by both authorities as the same document.
7: Mkondo governs structure and holds no opinion about content. It admits nothing, judges nothing, detects nothing, and responds to nothing. Both authorities stand on it equally; the witness watches both across it. A question this charter answers is answered here — never by recollection, and never differently in two places.
8: 2  The One-Record Law, Stated Precisely
9: Document 1 §4.3 holds: there is exactly one record, and nothing maintains a second. What the law forbids is a second, competing account of the same events. What it requires is exactly this matrix: one authoritative account per record class, with a single writing authority and named readers. The Watch minting the first account of its own events is the law working; two accounts of anyone's events would be the law broken. X and Y read the same record; X and Z mint new classes; nobody mints a rival.
10: PART II
The Record Matrix
11: 3  The Matrix
12: Every record class in the platform, its single writer, and its readers. A second writer to any class is a defect on sight; a reader not listed does not read; additions to this matrix are ceremony, and the matrix version in force is stamped on every audit answer.
13: Record class
14: Writes
15: Reads
16: Notes
17: Run ledger rows
18: Northena
19: Both authorities; compliance surfaces
20: Admission, gating, convergence, absorbed stamp-audits. Contract-grade per Document 3 §9.
21: Trust receipts
22: SyniSense
23: Both authorities; the receipt's own consumer
24: Per invocation, tenant-keyed signature.
25: Census and registry records
26: Mtafiti
27: Both authorities; every surface by proof link
28: Objective-blind measurement; the Watch reads sensitivity classes for tripwire coverage and never writes.
29: Mining plans
30: Targeta
31: Governing authority; auditors
32: The Watch neither reads to steer nor writes.
33: Reasoning traces · intent audits
34: Solva
35: Both authorities
36: The intent audit's divergence fields are emissions the Watch reads as signals.
37: Declarations
38: Admission (Northena), from the actor
39: Both authorities
40: Frozen per Document 3 §6.1; re-declaration supersedes by new entry.
41: Rules · registries · ceremonies
42: The rules service
43: Both authorities; both consoles
44: Content authored by the owning authority — governance rules by governance, Watch tables by the Watch — ceremony administered here for both.
45: Verdicts
46: Macho
47: Mkono; both consoles; auditors
48: The seam artifact of Document 8 §6. Macho writes nothing else.
49: Action records
50: Mkono
51: Both authorities; both consoles
52: Act-and-attest atomic; policy row cited; expiry state carried.
53: Attestations · drill receipts
54: Watch workers · the witness
55: Everyone with assurance standing
56: The break-in test's failures-to-modify land here as measurements.
57: Marks
58: Mkono
59: Every gate, on every pass
60: Dimension set per Document 8 §10; de-mark entries carry two signatures.
61: Behavioural profiles
62: The signature substrate
63: No surface, ever
64: W13: parameters only, tenant-keyed, non-exportable; trust standing derives outward, internals never do.
65: Memory-plane rows
66: The owning application, via its plane
67: The estate holder; compliance
68: Per Document 7 Part IV; the Watch reads plane activity as behaviour, never plane content as data.
69: 
70: 4  Reading Discipline
71: Reads are as governed as writes. The Watch reads governance evidence to protect the estate and for no other purpose; governance reads Watch records for assurance and never to re-litigate a verdict; and neither authority's surfaces render the other's interior — the compliance owner sees that the Watch acted and why at the record level, never its thresholds or placements; the watch officer sees the run record's facts, never governance's deliberations. Same facts, two readings, by construction.
72: PART III
The Task-Identity Register
73: 5  One Task, One Identity
74: Every task class in the platform maps to exactly one authority's identity and scope before it executes. An unmapped task class does not run — not runs-with-a-warning; does not run. Workers serve both authorities across time and never within a task; evidence crosses between authorities only through the matrix above, provenance-marked with the identity that produced it, never sideways through a dual-hatted task. The register's enforcement is structural: no credential scope exists that spans both authorities, so defect D8 — Document 7 §47 — is unrepresentable rather than policed.
75: Task class
76: Identity
77: Scope note
78: Admission · gating · convergence · ledger writes
79: Governance · Northena
80: Includes declaration capture at admit
81: Custody chain · chokepoint · egress
82: Governance · SyniSense
83: The input seat's sensing runs under Watch identity at the same physical point — two tasks, two identities, one location
84: Census · measurement · targeting · reasoning
85: Governance · owning engine
86: Per Documents 4
87: Rule ceremony administration
88: Governance · rules service
89: For both authorities' values; content authorship stays with the owner
90: Sensing · scoring · reconciliation · verdict minting
91: Watch · Macho
92: Read-only against governance records
93: Response execution · marks · mirage operation · trust discounts
94: Watch · Mkono
95: Writes only its own classes; no write to any governance class
96: Attestation · watchdog · break-in test
97: The witness
98: Neither authority's credentials; alarms outward
99: Console sessions
100: The console's authority
101: Trust Center under governance; Watch Console under Watch; each session receipted under its own identity
102: 
103: PART IV
The Handoff Contracts
104: 6  Where Work Crosses
105: Every crossing between services or authorities is a registered contract: what crosses, in what shape, under whose identity, with what receipt. An unregistered handoff is a finding. The contracts in force:
106: Handoff
107: Contract
108: Admission → extraction
109: The frozen artifact and declaration cross whole; Document 3 §5–§8 and Document 4 §34.2 govern; receipt is the admit row.
110: Chokepoint → model
111: Custody chain per Document 3 §13.1 with the input seat's verdict preceding invocation; a hold here renders through the refusal taxonomy; receipt is the trust receipt plus the verdict.
112: Verdict → response
113: The seam of Document 8 §6: verdict row in, action out, policy version cited; no other channel between the engines exists.
114: Containment → decision
115: A reserved-decision item crosses to the Decisions panel with its walk attached; resolution crosses back as a ceremony-grade entry; expiry governs the interim.
116: Mirage release → reconciliation
117: Release verdict crosses to the replay-or-notify duty under the ruled posture; discharge is receipted; the friction budget is debited.
118: Disagreement → resolution
119: Both authorities' records cross side by side; the human's resolution lands in both readings as one entry; neither record is amended — corrected by new entry only.
120: Watch findings → CIF
121: Findings cross as detection input under CIF's own origination port; nothing crosses back but ratified frames through the coach seat.
122: 
123: 7  Change and Precedence
124: This charter changes by the same ceremony as any consequential rule — proposed, counter-signed, waited, applied, re-verified — with matrix changes carrying the slowest countdown class, because the matrix is the boundary of both authorities at once. Where this charter and any other document appear to disagree about who writes, who reads, or who is acting, this charter governs; where it is silent, the owning authority's canon governs; and a silence that mattered is a finding to close by amendment, never a gap to fill by recollection.
125: 8  What This Charter Comes Down To
126: One account per record class, one identity per task, one contract per crossing — held in one short document both authorities cite. Seamlessness comes from the reads; boundaries come from the writes; and the whole point of writing it down is that nobody, human or machine, ever answers a matrix question from memory.

# SOURCE: assessment_workspace/canon/w11_batch2_v3/AKKI_Canon_Documents_17_20_v3.docx
Coordinate: document.xml paragraph in body order, tables included

1: AKKI · GOVERNED ARTIFACT · CANON SPECIFICATION
2: Documents 17–19
3: The Multidimensional Training Engine · Callable Skill Files · Quality Assurance & Evidence Integrity
4: Companion to Documents 1–16. Written to the same standard: every requirement is CANON (already ratified, cited to its source), RULED (an Owner decision on record, not yet executed), or OPEN (genuinely undecided). Nothing here is invented; where this document reuses existing code or a ratified spec, the source file is cited inline.
5: DOCUMENT 17   The Multidimensional Training Engine
6: The Multidimensional Training Engine
7: Extends and completes Promises #22, #23, #24 (Documents 13–14). Its audio-specific depth is reused directly from the Audio Intelligence Plane Specification v1.0 (RMS-IQ-Core-2, docs/mandates/akki_os_pack_v1/ — supplied by the Owner 2026-07-30, the ninth and final document of the AkkiOS pack, explicitly “the single reference for build”) — not generalised away from, as an earlier version of this document incorrectly did.
8: 17.1 · The promise, in plain language
9: Given governed access to an audio estate, the platform provides four functions in one loop, not one: Extraction converts audio into provenance-paired facts; Learning accumulates group-level knowledge of how the estate's languages and audio behave; Training commissions model production against a falsifiable target, planned and priced before compute is spent; Invention constructs synthesized voice identities from what's been learned — authentically of the language, provably of no individual. Each function feeds the next: extraction populates the register that training plans against; trained models improve extraction; invention consumes the register's learned layers. This is Promise #22 and #23's own language (“the platform trains models on its own … meeting every criterion on uncurated held-out material or not entering service”; “before committing a training job, the platform works with the user to get the objective right”), extended by the two functions — Learning and Invention — that the source documents named but that never landed in this canon until now.
10: 17.2 · The service that powers it
11: No sibling services. Per the source's own governing doctrine (§1.2): Mtafiti gains an audio modality and the Character Register; Northena gains audio data classes on its one ledger; the shaping wizard gains an Objective Wizard variant; Targeta gains a training object and a third planning mode. Anything that reads as a parallel to an existing service is rule proliferation and must be collapsed into the existing service before build — stated as a standing principle, not a one-time note.
12: 17.3 · Definition of the promise
13: Five principles govern every clause below. Where any clause conflicts with one of these, the principle wins and the clause is defective — the source's own words, reused because the standard is worth inheriting exactly.
14: An audio file is a data estate, and the framing is recursive. The archive is an estate; a programme is an estate; a single file is an estate. Segments are rows; content, language, condition, prosody, occurrence, code-switch, music, and group-level character are columns — no schema exists until one is declared. Census, admission, registry, and record apply at every scale.
15: Modality extension, not parallel machinery (§17.2).
16: One record. Mtafiti and Northena collaborate to produce a single record, written once. Working state — loss curves, intermediate metrics, partial coverage counts — is scratch, not truth, until finalized and stamped. No local ledger exists anywhere in this design. If a measured throughput ceiling ever demands relief, the relief is batched stamping — one row certifying N events with a digest — which remains a single record; that change is made only when a measurement demands it, never pre-emptively.
17: Measure, do not assert. No data-volume requirement, accuracy expectation, or cost figure is quoted without a measurement behind it — calibration exists specifically to convert assertions into measurements before commitment.
18: Unrepresentable, not policed.
